jobs.description: AIR is seeking a Quantitative Researcher to contribute to rigorous evidence synthesis and quantitative research across a range of education projects. The Quantitative Researcher will design and conduct systematic reviews and meta-analyses, evaluate the quality and strength of research evidence, and apply advanced quantitative methods to impact evaluations. The role will collaborate with researchers, subject matter experts, and clients to translate complex evidence into clear, actionable insights that inform education policy, programs, and practice. This position has the flexibility to work remotely within the United States (U.S.) or from one of our U.S. office locations. This does not include U.S. territories. About AIR: Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. We generate evidence and apply data-driven solutions that expand opportunities and improve lives for all. Responsibilities: Develop research designs and study protocols for evidence synthesis across education, workforce, and health programs and topic areas. Design and implement transparent, reproducible evidence synthesis workflows, including literature screening, data extraction, quality assessment, effect-size calculation, and meta-analysis. Apply appropriate methods to extract and synthesize evidence from diverse research designs, including randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies (e.g., regression discontinuity designs), single-case designs, and other quantitative research approaches. Conduct meta-analyses using advanced statistical methods and software, including methods for assessing heterogeneity, exploring variation in effects, and evaluating selective reporting bias. Develop and apply evidence review frameworks, study quality standards, and evidence-rating criteria for evidence clearinghouses, research syntheses, and related initiatives. Contribute to the design and implementation of impact evaluations, including randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental studies, using appropriate quantitative methods to estimate program impacts. Collaborate with clients and subject matter experts to develop and refine evidence review criteria and processes that align with project goals and policy needs. Contribute to the design, testing, and improvement of tools and software that support evidence synthesis workflows and methods. Develop and deliver training and other professional learning activities related to evidence synthesis methods and tools. Prepare written materials (e.g., technical reports and policy briefs) that communicate findings in ways that are accessible and useful to policymakers and other decision makers. Present findings to clients, professional associations, and the public. Manage or lead projects and tasks, assuming greater responsibility for project management over time. Participate in, and where appropriate lead, efforts to develop research proposals that generate external funding for evidence synthesis and impact evaluation studies. Mentor and support junior staff by providing methodological guidance, sharing approaches to solving problems, and providing feedback on their work. Qualifications: Education, Knowledge, and Experience A Master’s degree with at least 4 years of relevant experience, or a Ph.D., in education, statistics, research methods, or a related field, with demonstrated experience conducting systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Experience conducting key components of systematic reviews and meta-analyses, including literature screening, study coding, data extraction, effect-size calculation, and quantitative synthesis. Knowledge of diverse quantitative research designs, including randomized controlled trials and quasi-experimental designs, and demonstrated ability to assess study quality and apply quantitative methods in impact evaluation and evidence synthesis. Experience applying evidence standards, review criteria, or evidence-rating frameworks in research syntheses, evidence clearinghouses, or related initiatives. Demonstrated ability to communicate complex methodological concepts and research findings clearly, both orally and in writing, to technical and non-technical audiences. Skills Expertise in advanced evidence synthesis methods, including meta-analytic modeling, assessment of heterogeneity and variation in effects, and evaluation of selective reporting bias. Ability to assess methodological rigor across a range of study designs and translate research evidence into transparent, defensible evidence ratings or recommendations. Ability to apply appropriate quantitative methods to the design and analysis of impact evaluations, including experimental and quasi-experimental studies. Experience with or interest in applying AI-enabled tools to support literature screening, coding, data extraction, or other components of evidence synthesis. Proficiency in a statistical programming language or software (e.g., R) and ability to learn and apply new statistical and methodological tools as needed across projects . jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a member of the International Policy Applied AI team at Anthropic, you will be a trusted technical advisor to governments, AI Safety Institutes (AISIs), and multilateral institutions. You'll use your technical skills and your experience with government partners to help them understand frontier AI, test it, and apply it to their public missions with a high degree of reliability and safety. This role serves Anthropic's policy, mission, and public benefit goals. In collaboration with the Policy, Product, Research, and Engineering teams, you'll help partners develop strategies and plans to evaluate and adopt leading-edge AI systems. You will use your excellent communication skills to explain complex topics, including the potential benefits and harms of frontier AI, to technical and non-technical audiences alike. You will also play a critical role in identifying how our AI systems can best serve public interests around the world, while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards. Responsibilities: Act as a primary technical advisor for senior officials in partner governments, AISIs, and international institutions. Brief them on frontier AI capabilities, give an honest account of both benefits and harms, and explain safety research in terms that inform their decisions. Partner closely with the Policy team to understand each partner's goals and requirements. Develop demos, pilots, prototypes, and evaluation suites that show how Claude can support their public missions, such as cyber defense. Lead technical onboarding, enablement, and hands-on workshops for partner institutions, including national cybersecurity agencies. Guide their setup, architecture, and integration as they build with Claude Code and the Claude API. Act as the voice of our international partners and a key collaborator with our Product and Research teams to ensure we deliver the capabilities they need. Travel internationally to partner institutions for senior leader meetings, technical enablement, and building relationships. Establish a shared vision for creating solutions that enable beneficial and safe AI. Lead the vision, strategy, and execution of innovative solutions that leverage our latest models’ capabilities. jobs.description: The Office of the District Attorney, Bronx County (“BXDA”) is charged with the twin goals of ensuring public safety and striving for equal justice for the over 1.4 million members of the Bronx County community. By “Pursuing Justice with Integrity,” the BXDA places a focus on assistance for crime victims while simultaneously ensuring fairness to defendants. Moreover, the BXDA aims to balance the need to seek appropriate punishment for certain crimes while recognizing when punitive measures do not adequately advance justice. By recognizing these significant distinctions and acting accordingly, BXDA has established a standard of excellence in the representation of the Bronx community at large, which continues to grow stronger every day.  In furtherance of this mission, the BXDA seeks an experienced and enthusiastic Data Visualization Analyst Level to join the Strategic Planning & Analytics Bureau. Strategic Planning & Analytics uses data, research, and analytics to support evidence-based decision-making, measure performance, evaluate policies and initiatives, and promote transparency. The Data Visualization Analyst will develop and maintain dashboards, automated reports, and other data products that translate complex criminal justice data into clear, actionable information for Office leadership, staff, policymakers, and external audiences. jobs.description: Job Description: Position Purpose The Research Assistant position is responsible for recruiting and working with participants for a research study evaluating the overlaps between HIV, hepatitis C, and drug use across New England. (RISE-NE). RISE-NE involves working with people who use drugs and people at risk for or living with HIV to understand a changing risk and resource landscape over a period of many years. In this position, Research Assistants will conduct surveys with qualified participants at syringe services programs across Central and Western Massachusetts. This position requires the ability to travel between different community partner sites and be flexible in fast-paced settings where participants are often unhoused or at least facing many different kinds of structural vulnerability. This position also requires the ability to conduct research in English and Spanish. The Research Assistant will work closely with the Project Director, a Project Coordinator, other Research Assistants, staff members at community agencies, and Principal Investigators of RISE-NE. Job-related activities include, but are not limited to: study visit preparation, participant screening and recruitment (including direct outreach and field-based recruitment), participant retention activities, and survey conduct. The Research Assistant will also have to manage biological samples (i.e., blood and/or urine), and may be trained in phlebotomy. There may be future opportunities to be trained in qualitative research methods. The Research Assistant will have the opportunity to be part of a dynamic team, work with key state stakeholders (e.g., local harm reduction agencies), and contribute to some of the most pressing public health problems in the region. This position will be working in the location of Central and Western Massachusetts, and will travel to different community sites that range from Springfield to the northwest corner of Massachusetts. The position will entail having four days at community sites, and one day remote. All offers of employment are contingent upon a criminal background check and education verification satisfactory to Brown University. This is a fixed-term position with a current end date of December 31, 2027, which may be extended based upon available funding. Job Qualifications Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in relevant field and 1 to 2 years of experience (e.g., public health, anthropology, sociology, social work or other related field. Or equivalent combination of education and experience. Lived experience will be considered for peer-based research studies. Coursework in research methods is preferred 1+ years relevant work experience in the field of substance use (including but not limited to overdose prevention and harm reduction), HIV, public health, health services, or other relevant fields preferred Experience with survey and database software, such as Qualtrics or REDCap, preferred Experience in qualitative and/or ethnographic data collection methods and analysis, with evidence of strong facilitation skills preferred Comfort and experience working with people who use drugs, people living with HIV, and/or other vulnerable populations Community-based research experience preferred Phlebotomy trained preferred Job Competencies Experience and comfort working with people who use drugs and/or people living with HIV Strong software proficiency (i.e. Microsoft Office [Word, Excel, PowerPoint]), with willingness to learn and utilize new software applications as needed (e.g. REDCap, Qualtrics, NVivo). Proven ability to work effectively manage a caseload of participants, including setting priorities and meeting deadlines for administrative work. Strong interest in public health, with a focus on harm reduction and substance use Excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong interpersonal skills Strong attention to detail, high level of professionalism and organization required Efficient time management skills Knowledge of human subjects research procedures Able to conduct surveys and interviews in English and Spanish Reliable transportation to research and community sites is required. jobs.title: Talent Operations Specialist
jobs.description: ABOUT¿THE¿CAMPAIGN FINANCE¿BOARD¿¿   The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation.¿   We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers¿make a plan¿to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government.¿   We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust.¿   ABOUT THE¿UNIT¿   The People and Engagement Division is responsible for the agency's systems, policies, and resources that work to shape engagement and the employee experience at the CFB.     The division encompasses multiple units including the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) unit, People and Culture unit, the Learning and Development unit, and the Labor Relations, Timekeeping, Payroll, Benefits and Compliance unit.  Its work spans the entire employee lifecycle; from recruitment and selection, onboarding, to workplace culture, succession planning, learning and development, and organizational restructuring. The Division also manages employee and labor relations, payroll, timekeeping, offboarding, and benefits administration. Together we work to build people systems that allow for a positive employee experience and workplace culture.   The People & Culture Unit serves as an internal strategic partner dedicated to supporting employees and advancing the agency across every stage of the employee lifecycle. The unit delivers comprehensive HR-based solutions in the areas of talent operations, employee growth and development, and organizational culture. Its work begins with recruitment and selection and extends through onboarding, employee engagement, career development, workplace culture, and more. The team is committed to fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performing work environment where employees can thrive and grow professionally. Through data-informed practices and people-centered strategies, the unit helps strengthen the CFB while ensuring alignment with the CFB's goals, values, and overall mission. By balancing operational excellence with employee support, the People & Culture Unit Department plays a critical role in building a resilient, engaged, and future-focused workforce.   JOB¿DESCRIPTION¿¿   The Talent Operations Specialist reports to the Talent Operation Manager. This role will support the full recruitment lifecycle at the CFB, from workforce planning and sourcing through selection and hiring serving as one of the agency's talent acquisition experts within the People & Culture department.    The role develops and executes sourcing strategies to build diverse, qualified talent pipelines, partners closely with hiring managers on recruitment plans and hiring packets, and manages day-to-day operations including job postings, screening, interviews, and offer coordination. It also uses recruitment data and analytics to improve hiring efficiency and inform workforce planning, while integrating principles around fairness, equity, and inclusion, ensuring compliance with NYC civil service requirements, and the NYC EEO Policy throughout the process.    Beyond individual searches, the specialist acts as a strategic advisor to hiring managers, delivering high-quality service to candidates and stakeholders while keeping vacancies moving within established timelines.   By helping to build the team that carries out the agency's work, this role directly strengthens the CFB's ability to safeguard fair, transparent elections for all New Yorkers.   The responsibilities¿and tasks¿to be completed in this role include,¿but are not limited to:¿¿    Proactive Sourcing & Talent Pipeline Development     -  Maintain relationships with external recruitment vendors to ensure effective sourcing for current vacancies and pipeline roles, partnering closely with vendors on hard-to-fill positions.     -  Execute sourcing strategies to build strong, diverse talent pipelines using LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search queries, high-traffic and reputable job boards, professional associations, and other   - talent databases.     -  Build and nurture a passive candidate pipeline for recurring and high-volume roles within the agency.     -  Building diverse pipelines through partnerships with colleges, professional associations, and community-based organizations (not just databases/LinkedIn).     -  Partnering with the Director of EEO/Accessibility to integrate EEO best practice and guiding principles into sourcing and selection     -  Use the SmartRecruiters platform to strengthen talent pipelines by identifying and tagging high-potential candidates from previous applicant pools.     -  Support projects to improve and update sourcing and pipeline development policies and procedures.    Full Cycle Recruitment & Candidate Experience     -  Lead and facilitate recruitment intake meetings with hiring managers to review hiring packet templates, explain the recruitment process, and determine the level of support needed throughout each search.     -  Coach hiring managers through the hiring packet process, advising on salary, key responsibilities, hiring exercises, and how each document ties into the broader recruitment policy and process.     -  Collect job-related data points during intake (responsibilities, knowledge, skills, abilities, and other role requirements) to draft accurate hiring packets and guide hiring managers through packet submission and approval.     -  Provide end-to-end support to hiring managers, including candidate screening, interview scheduling, and candidate communication.     -  Conduct screening interviews to evaluate candidates' technical fit, alignment with company values, and other role requirements.     -  Serve as the primary point of contact for candidates, ensuring timely status updates and professional rejection communications that maintain goodwill.     -  Maintain regular touchpoints with high-potential candidates throughout the recruitment process.     -  Guide hiring managers in submitting hiring proposals for finalists.     -  Coordinate the logistics of hiring exercises, and ensure all scheduled screenings are completed on time.     -  Support the extension of offers and serve as liaison for salary negotiations between finalists and hiring managers.     -  Ensuring compliance with NYC civil service requirements and recruitment policy throughout the process     -  Proactively advising hiring managers (consultative, not just reactive support)     -  Maintaining confidentiality and ethical recruitment standards     -  Provide support with project to improve/update recruitment & candidate experience policies and procedures    Recruitment Data & Systems Management     -  Maintain the agency's Monday.com hiring board, ensuring recruitment status updates for each assigned vacancy are entered by the end of the week they occur and that all required data fields and tasks are kept current within hiring timelines.     -  Ensure SmartRecruiters is utilized accurately and kept up to date, with all applicants correctly placed in their appropriate recruitment stage.     -  Train hiring managers on how to use SmartRecruiters and its communication tools to move candidates through the process.     -  Managing NYCAPS position actions (opening/closing/canceling postings) with full accuracy     -  Use recruitment analytics (time-to-fill, source effectiveness, offer acceptance) to improve process efficiency and inform workforce planning, and presenting insights to leadership.     -  Support projects to improve recruitment data management policies and procedures.     -  Post approved vacancy announcements through NYCAPS and maintain external job postings across job boards and platforms (e.g., Indeed, Idealist, Handshake, Simplicity, diversity-focused sites, LinkedIn, and relevant newsletters).     -  Keep approved hiring packets organized within the People & Culture SharePoint system, and ensure interview notes, scores, hiring exercise results, and scoring matrices are collected from panelists and hiring managers and properly filed.    Onboarding Transition     -  Ensure a seamless handoff of finalist information to the Talent Operations Coordinator once a candidate accepts an offer, confirming onboarding kicks off within 24–48 hours.     -  Confirm that offer letters and onboarding documents are sent promptly and check in throughout onboarding to ensure a smooth process and resolve any roadblocks.     -  Assist with conducting new employee orientation.     -  Support projects to improve and update onboarding policies and procedures.     MOST ESSENTIAL¿KNOWLEDGE,¿SKILLS,¿ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs)¿   We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. We believe in the power of diverse perspectives and the unique blend of lived experiences, non-traditional education pathways, practical know-how, and a variety of skills and abilities that each candidate brings to the table. If you're ready to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply and be part of our dynamic team.¿¿    Knowledge¿¿     -  Knowledge of recruitment processes & best practices including sourcing, screening, interviewing, and onboarding.     -  Knowledge of NYC labor laws, NYC EEO policy, and guiding principles of, diversity, inclusion, and intersectionality in the workplace.     -  Knowledge of structured interviewing techniques and selection best practices sufficient to coach and train hiring managers across the agency.     -  Knowledge of NYCAPS (NYC Automated Personnel System) for position management, including opening, closing, and canceling job positions with 100% accuracy.     -  Knowledge of external job boards and sourcing platforms such as SmartRecruiters, LinkedIn Recruiter, Dice, Indeed, Idealist, Handshake, Simplicity (CUNY), and DCAS e-hire.     -  Knowledge of onboarding documentation standards, including checklist preparation, welcome package assembly, and accurate maintenance of onboarding spreadsheets.     Skill:     -  Skill in written and verbal communication to engage staff, agency partners, candidates, and hiring managers; drafting and sending accurate, timely onboarding checklists to hiring managers.     -  Skill in coordinating and scheduling Day 1 orientation, including preparing communications and ensuring all logistics are in place prior to a new hire's start date.     -  Skill in written and verbal communication to maintain regular, clear, and timely updates with hiring managers throughout the recruitment process.     -  Skill in using various types of data sources like Power BI, Tableau, and other data systems, formats, and tools such as spreadsheets, databases, and dashboards.     -  Skill in developing and maintaining job descriptions, recruitment materials, and scoring rubrics that ensure consistency and fairness in candidate evaluation.     -  Skill in developing, updating, and continuously improving onboarding templates and process documentation in partnership with the People and Culture Jr. Manager.     -  Skill in gathe

jobs.title: Senior Policy and Finance Analyst, Sustainability
jobs.description: Join the fight against climate change and take advantage of a unique opportunity on the cutting edge of climate policy at the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB). DOB plays an essential role in implementing New York City’s ground-breaking climate policies, including Local Law 97, which significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions from the city’s largest buildings. The Department’s Bureau of Sustainability is actively developing the policies and regulations needed to advance New York City’s climate goals. In a city where buildings contribute nearly three-quarters of our greenhouse gas emissions, a focus on efficiency, building energy usage, and decarbonization is critical. DOB is committed to becoming the nation’s premier municipal building organization, enhancing the quality of life for all New Yorkers, and making our city a safer and healthier place to live.    The Sustainability Bureau seeks a highly motivated individual to join our team as a Senior Policy and Financial Analyst, a key role responsible for helping to implement and administer DOB’s sustainability policies and support the Bureau’s mission. The Senior Policy and Financial Analyst will be instrumental in directing the development, management, communication, and evaluation of policies, processes, and programs that impact building energy efficiency and carbon reduction.   The successful candidate will be able to move between high-level policy questions and practical implementation details, including how laws and rules are operationalized through data systems, filings, guidance, case review, audit, and enforcement.   Under administrative direction, with the widest latitude for the exercise of independent judgment and initiative, performs technical work, research and analysis and serves as project leader to implement sustainability projects. Primary responsibilities will include but are not limited to:   - Analyze issues involving building energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, electrification, energy efficiency, renewable energy credits, offsets, and other carbon-reduction strategies, including through scenario analysis and implementation frameworks that assess costs, assumptions, emissions impacts, compliance options, and operational feasibility. jobs.title: Senior Policy Advisor
jobs.description: Agency Description:  The NYC Department of Small Business Services (SBS) helps unlock economic potential and create economic security for all New Yorkers by connecting New Yorkers to good jobs, creating stronger businesses, and building thriving neighborhoods across the five boroughs.   Job Description:  SBS is seeking a strategic, analytical and solutions-oriented Senior Policy Advisor to lead the agency’s work on predatory and anti-competitive practices that disadvantage New York City’s small businesses. Reporting directly to the Chief of Staff, the ideal candidate will bring strong legal and policy research skills, sound judgment and the ability to translate complex legal and market issues into concrete, actionable recommended policy or programmatic interventions.  Primary responsibilities will include but are not limited to:  • Maintain ongoing deep knowledge and awareness of the work of leading think tanks and the policies of other jurisdictions to address predatory market forces harming small businesses.  • Research federal, state and local laws, regulations and case law on anti-competitive and other predatory market forces, and assess where gaps or weak enforcement harm small businesses. • Through relationships with small business owners, merchant associations, BIDs, advocates, researchers and industry groups, understand the impact of anti-competitive or predatory market forces on small businesses in NYC and evaluate potential solutions. • Identify and analyze predatory or anti-competitive and predatory practices using data, stakeholder input, and research from other jurisdictions. • Develop and evaluate options for City or State action, including legislation, rulemaking, programs, advocacy and public-private partnerships. • Prepare well written, thorough memos, briefings and presentations that turn complex legal and economic analysis into recommendations for agency leadership.   To apply, go to www.nyc.gov/jobs and search for Job ID: # 808433  Note: We appreciate the interest and thank all applicants who apply, but only those candidates under consideration will be contacted.  If you are unable to apply via Jobs NYC, you can email your cover letter and resume to careers@sbs.nyc.gov with the following in the subject line: Senior Policy Advisor  If you do not have access to email, mail your cover letter & resume to: NYC Department of Small Business Services Human Resources Unit 1 Liberty Plaza, 11th Floor New York, New York 10006 Minimum qualifications: A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and at least 3 years of full-time paid experience in government affairs. Preferred skills: • At least 3 years of full-time paid experience in government affairs. • At least one year of full-time legal experience  • Excellent research, analytical and problem-solving skills required • Excellent verbal and written communication and presentation skills • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work in team environment • Strong project management and time management skills • Ability to prioritize assignments, handle multiple projects simultaneously to completion, and work under pressure against tight deadlines • Ability to actively listen, synthesize information and communicate effectively with all levels of staff and external stakeholders • Ability to research complex issues and synthesize information into internal and external communications quickly and effectively; and • Discretion and excellent judgment to handle sensitive and confidential matters • Ability to work flexible hours and occasional weekends

jobs.description: NOTE: ONLY CANDIDATES WHO HAVE A PERMANENT STAFF ANALYST OR COMPARABLE CIVIL SERVICE TITLE WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR AN INTERVIEW. THE AGENCY The Department of City Planning (DCP) plans for the future of New York City, working to create thriving and dynamic neighborhoods with access to housing and jobs, resilient infrastructure, and a vibrant public realm. The Department engages communities to develop inclusive plans, expand housing access and economic opportunity, and plans for long-term sustainability.  DCP supports the City Planning Commission in its annual review of hundreds of land use applications. The Department also advises on citywide strategic and capital planning, analyzes data, conducts policy analysis, and creates open data and civic engagement tools.  The Department of City Planning offers staff meaningful opportunities to help shape the future of New York City and address some of its most pressing challenges. The Department values public service, collaboration, and creativity, and supports professional development. Learn more about DCP and view current job openings at www.nyc.gov/planning.  THE DIVISION DCP’s Fiscal Division strives to improve the agency’s financial responsibility and operational effectiveness by providing information, analysis, and administrative and technical support to programs and divisions throughout the agency.  The Fiscal team’s daily operations include, but are not limited to, procurement, grant management, accounting for both payables and receivables, budgeting and financial reporting. The team also supports a small “Operations” unit responsible for facility and fleet management. Due to the relative size of DCP and its diverse funding composition, members of DCP's fiscal team have direct exposure to a wide range of financial functions.  THE ROLE DCP Fiscal is seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Accounts Payable & Receivable Specialist to monitor daily and monthly revenue operations through reconciliation, reporting, transaction review, and customer support as well as assist with other accounting functions, such as invoice review and payment processing. This role ensures the accuracy and integrity of financial records, compliance with internal controls and Comptroller Directives, and timely resolution of discrepancies and payment-related inquiries.  RESPONSIBILITIES - Perform daily and monthly revenue reconciliations to verify accuracy, completeness, and proper recording of transactions. - Monitor revenue activity and maintain internal revenue trackers, reconciliation schedules, and supporting documentation. - Investigate, analyze, and resolve reconciling discrepancies and variances in a timely manner. - Conduct monthly FMS reconciliations and validate related financial transactions. - Review deposits and verify accurate CRE creation within FMS. - Perform monthly bank-to-book reconciliations and ensure alignment between financial systems and bank records. - Track, monitor, and respond to chargebacks, reversals, refunds, and payment discrepancies. - Respond to payment-related inquiries from customers and the Address Assignment Verification Unit. - Prepare Year-End Close (YEC) reconciliations and other financial oversight or compliance reports. - Ensure adherence to generally accepted accounting principles, Comptroller Directives, internal processes, and other applicable policies and procedures. - Assist in identifying process improvements to strengthen revenue monitoring and reconciliation accuracy. - Prepare revenue data for various reporting and assist with revenue forecasting and analysis exercises. - Assist with the review of agency invoices and payments for accuracy and consistency with purchasing agreements and ensure appropriate back-up documents are received. - Assist with processing payments and employee reimbursements in the City’s payment systems. - Prepare ad hoc reports and assist with ad hoc accounting projects and tasks and for the Fiscal division as needed.  PREFERRED SKILLS - Experience in revenue operations, accounting, finance, or reconciliation functions preferred. - Knowledge of financial management systems (FMS), CityPay, and CPSS reconciliation processes. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. - Excellent customer service skills. - Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment. - Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other financial tracking tools. - Strong written and verbal communication skills. - Strong organizational and time management skills; detail oriented with the ability to multi-task and work both independently and as part of a team. - Familiarity with Comptroller Directives and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles  TO APPLY: Visit cityjobs.nyc.gov and follow the steps below: 1.  Search for job ID number: 808154 2.  Click on the job business title: Accounts Payable & Receivable Specialist 3. Only applicants under consideration will be contacted.  Appointments are subject to Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that they meet all minimum qualifying requirements for this position at the time of application.  The City of New York is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce and providing a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment based upon any legally protected status or protected characteristic, including but not limited to an individual's sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity, or pregnancy. An associate degree or completion of 60 semester credits from an accredited college and four years of satisfactory full-time professional experience as described in "2" above.  A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent approved by a State's department of education or a recognized accrediting organization and six years of satisfactory full-time professional experience as described in "2" above. The Administration and Planning Division is responsible for managing and overseeing administrative and operational services for the agency. The Department of Finance (DOF) currently occupies over 1 million square feet of space in 12 buildings in the five boroughs. jobs.title: Research & Correction Supervisor
jobs.description: IMPORTANT NOTE: CANDIDATES MUST HAVE A PERMANENT PRINCIPAL ADMINISTRATIVE ASSOCIATE CIVIL SERVICE TITLE OR ARE PERMANENT IN A COMPARABLE CIVIL SERVICE TITLE ELIGIBLE FOR A 6.1.9 TITLE CHANGE.   PLEASE INCLUDE YOUR EMPLOYEE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (EIN) WHEN APPLYING AND INDICATE IN YOUR COVER LETTER YOUR PERMANENT CIVIL SERVICE TITLE.   NYC Department of Finance (DOF) is responsible for administering the tax revenue laws of the city fairly, efficiently, and transparently to instill public confidence and encourage compliance while providing exceptional customer service.  DOF’s Customer Operations Division has oversight of the Department of Finance Business Centers, City Register’s Office, and the Land Records, Adjudication, and Collections divisions. Customer Operations is charged with the processing of tax payments, parking violations payments, and all other charges collected by DOF. The division is also responsible for recording property transfers, adjudicating parking and camera violations, and managing the full life cycle of the department’s enforcement activities related to unpaid business and excise taxes, parking fines, and Environmental Control Board summonses.  The Land Records Division and its Office of the City Register record and maintain all official documents related to real estate, including deeds, mortgages, and leases. The division has offices in every borough except for Staten Island, where the Office of the County Clerk provides these functions. Land Records records approximately 550,00 documents annually and collects over $5 billion annually in real property transfer and mortgage recording taxes. The Division maintains and updates New York City property ownership records and provides review and research services for those records. The Land Records Division also administers the property tax lien sale for property tax enforcement, interacting with the NYC Law Department, the Mayor’s Office of Management and Budget, and the Lien Trust Program.  The Research and Corrections Unit is responsible for assisting the public with inquiries related to document recording, troubleshooting the ACRIS system by phone and email, and processing edits and corrections to submitted documents. This team plays a critical role in delivering high-quality customer service to the public.   The Customer Operations Division is seeking a supervisor to serve in the Research & Correction unit. Reporting to the Manager of Research & Helpdesk Operations, the selected candidate’s duties and responsibilities will include, but not be limited to the following:   •	Supervise, direct, and evaluate the daily activities of staff assigned to the Research and Corrections Unit. •	Supervise and mentor staff in key functions including title research, index corrections, and investigation of suspected fraudulent filings. •	Assign and distribute work based on staffing levels, workload, employee experience, and operational priorities. •	Monitor staff productivity, accuracy, timeliness, attendance, and adherence to established procedures. •	Oversee the processing of document corrections, edits, and other requests involving recorded or submitted land records. •	Review complex correction requests and provide guidance on appropriate resolution. •	Oversee research of deeds, mortgages, leases, liens, property ownership, document histories, and other real property records. •	Ensure research is thorough, accurate, properly documented, and completed within established timeframes. •	Ensure timely and professional responses to public inquiries, maintaining full compliance with citywide customer service standards. •	Provide supervisory assistance with complex or escalated customer inquiries involving document recording and Land Records procedures. •	Oversee telephone and email responses to the public, City agencies, attorneys, title companies, and other stakeholders. •	Monitor pending correction requests, research assignments, customer inquiries, and other unit workloads to prevent backlogs and delays. •	Establish priorities and adjust staff assignments to address urgent or high-volume workloads. •	Prepare workload statistics, reports, performance information, and operational updates as requested. •	Work closely with Manager to develop and implement unit procedures and recommend improvements. •	Ensure the accuracy of public-facing index records and oversee correction workflows to maintain data integrity. •	Participate in special projects, process-improvement initiatives, system enhancements, and departmental workgroups.  Additional Information:  In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.  This position may be eligible for remote work up to 2 days per week, pursuant to the Remote Work Pilot Program agreed between the City and the Collective Bargaining Unit representing employees serving in the civil service title. Minimum qualifications: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and two years of satisfactory full-time progressively responsible clerical/administrative experience, one year of which must have been in an administrative capacity or supervising staff performing clerical/administrative work of more than moderate difficulty; or  2. Education above the high school level may be substituted for the general clerical/administrative experience (but not for the one year of administrative or supervisory experience described in "1" above) at a rate of 30 semester credits from an accredited college for 6 months of experience up to a maximum of 3 year. Preferred skills: •	Supervisory experience in a high-volume administrative, records, customer service, or public-sector environment. •	Knowledge of land records, document recording, property records, document correction, and records research procedures. •	Experience using ACRIS or similar records-management, document-management, or database systems. •	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills for researching complex or conflicting information. •	Ability to coordinate effectively with internal units, City agencies, attorneys, title companies, and members of the public. •	Excellent written and verbal communication skills. •	Knowledge of Microsoft Office, Excel, Word.

jobs.title: Investigator Analyst
jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION: The New York City Department of Probation is dedicated to improving public safety by supporting individuals on probation. DOP uses research-based practices to supervise and support people on probation and help prevent further interactions with the justice system. By expanding access to education and gainful employment opportunities, healthcare, family supports, and civic engagement, DOP empowers New Yorkers under their supervision to lead safe and thriving lives.  The Department of Probation is seeking to hire (2) Investigators.   The NYC Department of Probation (DOP) is a world leader in creatively and effectively engaging with people under court-mandated community supervision. Through innovative partnerships with people and organizations throughout New York City, DOP provides opportunities for those on probation to access services and programs that positively impact their life trajectory. Staff at DOP engage in meaningful relationships with those on probation to enhance community safety and decrease recidivism.  The Department is seeking to hire Investigator Analysts to support digital forensic examinations, social media investigations and cyber related operational support.  The analyst will assist sworn personnel by conducting both short term and long term investigations  ·	Use public records, databases, and social media to research case subjects ·	Ensure compliance with agency policy and legal standards ·	Conduct social media investigations to support investigations of nefarious activity ·	Identify, preserve and document case relevant online content ·	Prepare spreadsheets, charts, and graphs, both for internal and external use ·	Prepare intelligence reports for situational awareness and operational needs ·	Establishing links, discerning activity patterns within on-line and social media ·	Assist with identifying emerging cyber trends, risk and investigative leads ·	Support digital forensic examinations under established policies and procedures ·	Maintain accurate records, logs , statistical records and evidence tracking information as required ·	Utilize investigatory databases, public records, telephone records and social media platforms ·	May perform other related duties as assigned Minimum qualifications: A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college in criminal justice, forensic auditing, forensic science, police science, criminology, criminal justice administration and planning, and/or law or related field and two years of satisfactory full time related experience conducting investigations of alleged employee misconduct, interviewing witnesses and taking statements, managing caseloads, analyzing disciplinary procedures and making recommendations for improvement, interpreting rules, regulations and policies, preparing written reports of investigative findings, making presentations, or in a major operational area of the agency in which the appointment is to be made. jobs.title: Cycling & Greenway Maintenance Coordinator, Cycling & Micromobility
jobs.description: In order to be considered for this position candidate must be serving permanently in the title or reachable on the civil service list.  Transportation Planning and Management (TPM) is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working, and doing business in New York City.  The Division’s responsibilities include planning, street design, curb management, technical analysis, signs, transit development, freight mobility and markings, and ensuring the safety of motor vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and cyclists.   The Office of Livable Streets (OLS) is tasked with prioritizing strategic planning, community engagement, research, policy, design, implementation, and long-term management. Their goal is to create streets that are livable, supporting safety, accessibility, inclusion, resiliency, active modes, community cohesion, and economic vitality citywide. Additionally, they aim to enhance New York City's pedestrian, bicycle, and micromobility networks, providing comfortable, connected, green, and reliable transportation options across the five boroughs. They place special emphasis on Priority Investment Areas, mode shift, and reimagining streets. The office also develops innovative new programs, design typologies, project delivery, and analysis tools to meet the demands of a rapidly changing population with evolving needs and technologies.  The Cycling & Micromobility Unit is responsible for the nation's largest network of on-street bicycle facilities (1,200+ lane-miles), enhancing street safety for all users, and increasing bike ridership in the five boroughs. The team's focus is the innovative redesign of city streets to expand and improve the bike network, with emphasis on improving connectivity between neighborhoods, increasing access to safe bicycle infrastructure across the city, and creating a more equitable transportation network that serves all New Yorkers. Reporting to senior staff in the Cycling & Micromobility Unit, the Greenway Maintenance Program Coordinator will support the management and maintenance of NYC’s greenway network. Collaborating closely with City agencies and other entities, the selected candidate will lead the development of a comprehensive city-wide inventory of the existing greenway network, including facility types, design elements, other physical characteristics, and condition. The Greenway Maintenance Program Coordinator will work closely with others to coordinate day-to-day greenway maintenance through agency partnerships, programs, and other resources, with a focus on expanding and improving maintenance equitably across the five boroughs. Applying network prioritization methodologies, the selected candidate will assess the greenway facilities to identify opportunities for improving the quality, safety, accessibility, and connectivity of the network from an all-ages-and-abilities perspective. In this role, the successful candidate will also identify quality and physical gaps in the greenway systems and work closely with the Street Improvement Project and Capital teams to prioritize improvements and advance projects. The candidate will work with the Bridges Division to identify existing bridges for bicycle and pedestrian improvements and support the development and prioritization of new bicycle and pedestrian bridges. This role will also collaborate with relevant stakeholders on greenway wayfinding and initiatives to strengthen and elevate the identity and branding of the City’s greenway network. The candidate will develop and manage datasets; create graphics, reports, analyses, and other materials to support the assessment and management of the greenway network; participate in field visits, interagency meetings, and stakeholder meetings related to greenway maintenance, improvement, and conceptual project development. This role will collaborate with City agencies, public authorities, and other partners to identify funding opportunities for day-to-day maintenance, landscaping, state-of-good-repair needs, bridge projects, and other greenway improvements.  The Department of Transportation’s (DOT) mission is to provide for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods in the City of New York and to maintain and enhance the transportation infrastructure crucial to the economic vitality and quality of life of our primary customers, City residents. DOT is an equal opportunity employer, committed to recruiting and maintaining a diverse workforce in an open and inclusive environment. Minimum qualifications: 1. A master’s degree from an accredited college or university in city planning, urban planning, urban design, architecture, landscape architecture, transportation engineering, public administration, economic development or a related field; or  2. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and one year of satisfactory full-time experience in city planning such as in the review and development of housing, transportation, environmental, and city-owned land planning projects; or  3. A satisfactory combination of education and/or experience that is equivalent to "1" above. Graduate education in city planning, urban planning, urban design, architecture, landscape architecture, transportation engineering, public administration, economic development or related fields may be substituted for experience on the basis of 30 graduate semester credits from an accredited college or university for one year of experience. However, all candidates must have a baccalaureate degree.  4. To be eligible for placement in Assignment Level III, individuals must have, after meeting the minimum requirements, two additional years of professional experience as described in "2" above. Preferred skills: Professional experience in urban planning or a related field; demonstrated interest in cycling and the built environment of NYC; strong creative and analytical problem-solving skills; strong verbal and written communication skills; ability to establish excellent working relationships to support successful delivery of agency communications; experience working with the public, community groups, and New York City agencies; willingness to work in the field in all seasons, traveling by bike, walking, or using mass transit. Experience or interest in mapping software (ArcGIS), Computer-Aided Design (AutoCAD), Adobe Creative Suite, and Microsoft 365 is strongly desired. Preference given to candidates who have experience with project management and public outreach.

The Cycling & Micromobility Unit seeks to hire a highly motivated and detail-oriented GIS & Data Manager to support the management, analysis, and continuous improvement of the unit's GIS datasets, project databases, and reporting systems. Under the supervision of senior staff, the selected candidate will maintain and enhance spatial and tabular data, perform GIS analysis, develop maps and visualizations, and support data-driven planning, reporting, and decision-making across the unit.  The selected candidate will coordinate with planners, engineers, designers, project managers, and partner agencies to translate transportation projects into accurate spatial data, improve data quality and reporting systems, and support the production of the official New York City Bike Map. The position will play a central role in maintaining the unit's project tracking systems and developing new tools and workflows that improve the accuracy, efficiency, and accessibility of Cycling & Micromobility data. The candidate will manage GIS datasets and project databases supporting bicycle and micromobility planning, capital project development, network tracking, and reporting. The candidate will translate transportation projects into accurate spatial and tabular data through review of engineering plans, project documents, aerial imagery, and field observations to maintain the City's authoritative bicycle network dataset. The candidate will perform GIS analysis and prepare maps, dashboards, reports, and data visualizations to support planning studies, project development, performance reporting, and executive decision-making. The candidate will coordinate with planners, engineers, designers, project managers, and partner agencies to collect, validate, and integrate project information across multiple data systems. The candidate will develop new database tools, reporting workflows, and quality control procedures that improve project tracking, network analysis, and organizational efficiency. The candidate will support production of the official New York City Bike Map and prepare maps, exhibits, and other visual materials for presentations, public outreach, and agency communications. The candidate will perform other related duties as assigned. For Assignment Level I (only physical, biological and environmental sciences and public health) A master's degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological or environmental science or in public health.  To be appointed to Assignment Level II and above, candidates must have:  1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or  2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or  3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least a master's degree in an appropriate field of specialization and at least two years of experience described in "2" above. Two years as a City Research Scientist Level I can be substituted for the experience required in "1" and "2" above.    NOTE:  Probationary Period  Appointments to this position are subject to a minimum probationary period of one year. Preferred skills: •	Experience with ArcGIS Pro and other GIS software for spatial analysis, geodatabase management, cartography, and map production. •	Knowledge of transportation planning, bicycle and micromobility planning, complete streets, and roadway design principles. •	Experience interpreting engineering plans, construction drawings, aerial imagery, and other technical documents to develop and maintain spatial datasets. •	Experience developing, maintaining, and performing quality control on GIS databases, project tracking systems, or other transportation-related datasets. •	Experience preparing maps, dashboards, reports, data visualizations, and other technical products for planning, analysis, and executive decision-making. •	Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple assignments while maintaining a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail. •	Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite; experience with Adobe Creative Suite, SQL, Python, or other data management and visualization tools is desirable. •	Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to coordinate effectively with planners, engineers, designers, project managers, and other stakeholders.

A key focus of this role will be on identifying and managing opportunities for improving the city's cycling network through upgrades coordinated with street resurfacing and maintaining a safe and continuous network during construction events.  Duties include coordination and tracking of corridors to be resurfaced; identifying and coordinating repaving projects for design upgrades and future Street Improvement Projects (SIP); creating and updating Protected Bike Lane (PBL) Maintenance & Protection of Traffic (MTP) guidelines; coordinating the development of Street Assessments for PBLs; coordinating the installation of temporary markings for existing PBLs; identifying streets for markings refurbishment and conducting follow-up inspections; conducting field work and data collection and analysis; reviewing and recommending design changes; providing guidance and assistance coordinating implementation; attending monthly or quarterly coordination meetings. Additional duties may include attending, participating, and speaking at community meetings. jobs.title: Portfolio Specialist
jobs.description: DCAS's mission is to make city government work for all New Yorkers. From managing New York City’s most iconic courthouses and municipal buildings, to purchasing over $1 billion annually in goods and services for more than 80 City agencies — what we do ensures that all agencies can deliver on their mission. Our reach touches every facet of city government and is instrumental to the successful day-to-day operations of the City of New York.  Our commitment to equity, effectiveness and sustainability guides our work providing City agencies with the critical resources and support needed to succeed, including: •	Recruiting, hiring, and training City employees. •	Managing 56 public buildings. •	Acquiring, selling, and leasing City property. •	Purchasing over $1 billion in goods and services for City agencies. •	Overseeing the greenest municipal vehicle fleet in the country. •	Leading the City's efforts to reduce carbon emissions from government operations.  When you work at DCAS, you're not just working for one agency, but in service of them all. It's an opportunity to provide impactful support, quality customer service, and help protect the future of New York City for generations to come. Visit our website at nyc.gov/dcas to learn more about the work we do.  The Real Estate Services (RES) Line of Service of the Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) is the real estate arm of the City of New York  responsible for services such as leasing and acquisitions, architectural design and project management, real estate planning and dispositions, zoning and land use analyses, enforcement of space standards in office design and overseeing the equitable allocation of over 10 million square feet of privately owned space and 10 million square feet of City-owned space for agency use.  The Workplace Services Unit is tasked with creatively applying space standards to projects in leased and City owned space while developing workplace strategies that lead to improved office operations in order to support the work of our City workforce and leverage modern day office technologies. The unit oversees the development of architectural programs to ensure the design of the work environment is inclusive, inspiring, reflective of the City’s mission, safe, accessible, and functional. In addition, the group oversees the coordination of office furniture systems and technologies (including structured cabling, network, audio visual and security equipment) for projects in leased space in coordination with the Design & Project Management unit, while providing its own design and project management services for projects in City owned premises limited to interior buildouts. Lastly, the unit supports the work of the Real Estate Services Strategic Planning group by keeping up to date the space standards to reflect current industry trends and best practices in design.  The Portfolio Specialist position is a Design and Project Management role requiring daily use of AutoCAD, in-depth knowledge of space-planning strategies and execution, interior architectural design concepts and development, the ability to create construction drawings, and experience performing construction administration.  Responsibilities: 1.	Pre-Design, Programming and Planning •	Manage and/or assist in space planning. •	Evaluate city agency space requests, existing floor plans, employee rosters, and organizational charts to develop baseline Personnel and Equipment lists (P&Es) for assigned capital projects.  •	Consistently apply DCAS Citywide Space Standards as applicable. •	Conduct in-depth qualitative and quantitative analyses through space requirements surveys, site visits, and agency interviews to wholistically understand the agency’s needs, operations, and program. Revise P&Es and develop comprehensive architectural programs based on analyses. •	Serve as liaison to assigned city agencies and endeavor to ensure that their space needs are effectively addressed in project documents. Present and submit documents to agencies and OMB for review and approval.  2.	Design and Documentation •	Work with colleagues and directors to develop schematic drawings and related documentation to describe overall design concept(s) for assigned projects including precedent images, 2D and 3D design sketches, key architectural elements, reflected ceiling plans, lighting concepts, color palettes, key furniture items, and workstation finishes. Develop phasing plans if required. •	Consult with other RES units and FMC, as well as agency representatives, to evaluate and critique plans and concepts as they are developed to ensure viability, functionality, efficiency, and good design. Ensure agencies' needs are effectively met in the planning and development of the project. Present concepts to client agencies for review and sign-off. Integrate feedback from clients and propose alternative selections and design solutions as required. •	Create small scale design development drawing sets to depict scope of required work, design intent, material selection, furniture layout, data and electrical requirements, for use by in-house cost estimating team and landlord’s general contractor.  3.	Furniture Design, Coordination and Procurement •	Manage and/or assist in space planning of furniture, as well as furniture selection, specification, and procurement for projects in leased and City-owned space. Follow and implement DCAS Space Standards and City Furniture Requirements Contracts. Work closely with the Workplace Services Team and the Design and Project Management unit as required to coordinate with consultants and end-users. •	Create furniture packages including schedules and plans. Solicit and review quotes from vendors on City Furniture Requirements Contracts. Coordinate power, data, and furniture selections with vendors, consultants, and client agencies. Process Furniture Certificates to Proceed and Furniture Purchase Orders in a timely fashion. •	Perform project contract and general administration duties to ensure proper coordination of furniture with vendors, delivery, and installation on the job site. Manage and communicate with vendors to track progress of purchase orders and delivery dates. Coordinate deliveries and assist end users in receipt and generating furniture punch lists. Coordinate with vendors on punch list completion. Review final invoices for Director’s signature and payment.  4.	Portfolio Management •	Collaborate with other RES units to conduct site surveys and produce existing building drawings. Create and update architectural floor plans and furniture layouts in AutoCAD as required to document existing conditions for the DCAS portfolio of City-owned buildings and privately leased spaces. Review and evaluate site reports and measurements developed by Tenant Representatives or other RES Units. •	Oversee regular updates and suggestions to the DCAS Citywide Space Standards, P&E and other Programming Templates, Workplace Strategy Guidelines, and Interior FF&E standards in collaboration with the Workplace Services and Design & Project Management teams.   5.	Intra-Unit Support •	Collaborate with Strategic Planning, Leasing, and Design teams to plan the build out of new spaces. Provide support to the Strategic Planning team on special projects, front-end planning, and conceptual stacking plans.  •	Provide support in developing and transferring projects to the Design & Project Management (D&PM) unit.  •	Respond to follow up inquiries and participate in problem-solving to assist in the execution of a project. •	Assist Workplace Services colleagues in maintaining organized materials resource center.   Flexible Work Update: This position may be eligible for remote work up to two days per week, pursuant to the Remote Work Pilot Program agreed to between the City and DC37.   To Apply: Note: Only employees permanent in the title of Administrative Space Analyst, or those that are reachable via open competitive list call are eligible to apply.  Please go to www.nyc.gov/jobs or www.nyc.gov/ess for current NYC employees and search for Job ID #768476.  NO PHONE CALLS, FAXES OR PERSONAL INQUIRIES PERMITTED.  NOTE: ONLY THOSE CANDIDATES UNDER CONSIDERATION WILL BE CONTACTED. Minimum qualifications: 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and five years of full-time paid experience requiring general knowledge of construction and construction costs, electronic data processing equipment, telephone communications systems, building standards and leasing procedures, in the evaluation and layout of space in office buildings, garages and other structures used for commercial and industrial purposes, at least two years of which shall have been of a supervisory nature; or  2. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Health Department) seeks a dynamic, strategic, and results-oriented leader to serve as the Controller/Assistant Commissioner. Reporting to the CFO and Deputy Commissioner of Finance, the Controller/Assistant Commissioner is responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and efficiency of financial transactions for the NYC Department of Health. The Controller/Assistant Commissioner will join the Division of Finance, which has central responsibility and authority for the agency’s financial management and helps to ensure that programs and administrative operations have the information, analysis, funding and technical capacity to deliver critical services effectively and meet the NYC Health Department’s objectives. The Controller/Assistant Commissioner is the executive leader of the Bureau of the Controller and is responsible for directing the Agency's Offices of Payroll, Fiscal Management, Funds Management, and Cash Management.   The position provides strategic leadership and oversight for financial operations that generate and monitor more than $1 billion annually in personnel, vendor, consultant, contract, and miscellaneous payments. Leading a team of over 70 professionals, the Controller/Assistant Commissioner fosters a culture of operational excellence, accountability, customer service, and continuous process improvement. The position leads initiatives to modernize processes, strengthen financial controls, improve customer service, and implement technology solutions that enhance operational effectiveness. The Controller/Assistant Commissioner also serves as a primary point of contact for oversight agencies, including NYC Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Office of the NYC Comptroller, FISA/OPA, auditors, financial institutions, and other government stakeholders.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Direct and oversee the Offices of Payroll, Fiscal Management, Funds Management and Reporting. • Analyze complex financial, payroll, operational, and compliance issues and develop and implement strategic solutions. • Ensure the accurate and timely processing of payroll, vendor payments, contract payments, and other financial transactions. • Oversee payroll operations for more than 6,000 employees, including payroll accounting, compliance, examinations, timekeeping administration, and related functions. • Direct all cash management activities, including banking relationships, bank account reconciliations, cash flow monitoring, and financial controls. • Develop, implement, and monitor policies, procedures, and internal controls to safeguard agency resources and ensure financial accountability. • Ensure compliance with applicable City, State, Federal, and regulatory requirements, including directives issued by oversight entities. • Lead fiscal year-end closing activities, ensuring timely payment processing, accrual establishment, reconciliation activities, and accurate financial reporting. • Oversee funds management activities including expenditure monitoring, appropriations tracking, encumbrance management, and fiscal reporting. • Direct agency financial reporting, expenditure analysis, reconciliation activities, and executive-level reporting. • Lead business process reengineering initiatives and technology modernization projects designed to improve operational efficiency and strengthen internal controls. • Provide effective leadership and direction to managers, supervisors, and professional staff responsible for diverse financial and payroll functions through regular meetings and staff development efforts. • Represent the Agency in intergovernmental, citywide, and external forums involving payroll, fiscal management, financial reporting, and operational matters. • Collaborate with executive leadership to develop and implement strategic initiatives supporting Agency priorities and operational objectives. • Play a key leadership role in emergency management, continuity of operations planning, and emergency response activities.
