jobs.description: The Foundation We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally. The Team Development Policy and Finance (DPAF), part of the Gates Foundation’s Global Policy and Advocacy division, harnesses the power of finance and economics to address poverty and inequality. We serve the foundation’s economic policy, finance and analytical function by bringing rigorous economic analysis, development-finance expertise, and policy judgment to foundation strategies, investments, advocacy, and engagement with governments, multilateral development banks, international financial institutions, and other partners. DPAF works across issues including development assistance and the future of aid, sovereign debt and fiscal space, domestic public and private resource mobilization, multilateral development banks and the international financial architecture, country macroeconomics, and other questions affecting the resources available for health, development, and poverty reduction. DPAF is establishing a Policy Function to put its analytical and advisory role on a more systematic footing. Demand for DPAF’s expertise has grown as foundation teams seek timely perspectives on aid, debt, fiscal policy, MDBs, private finance, and domestic resource mobilization. The Policy Function combines rapid-response support for leadership and program teams with deeper knowledge production and anticipatory analysis. DPAF also leads the foundation’s body of work on catalyzing innovative financing and domestic capital mobilization. This work seeks to unlock private, external and domestic, resources for the foundation’s priority sectors, including health and agriculture, in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. It focuses on program investments as well as advisory, and on transaction instruments as well as systemic constraints in the country-specific capital markets. Your Role As Program Officer, you will report to the Deputy Director, Development Policy and Finance and work in a hybrid arrangement from our Washington, DC office. You will work across two connected areas of DPAF: the Policy Function, coordinating our analytical work, and the body of work on innovative financing and domestic capital mobilization. You will work closely with the respective Senior Program Officer leading on those two areas. You will support in the management of a defined set of investments within the innovative financing body of work and the Policy Function’s portfolio. You will, together with the SPOs build and manage relationships with external partners in these area and represent the foundation in related working groups and convenings. You will also collaborate with colleagues across program teams, regional offices, and external partners. *This position is a limited-term position for 12 months (not to extend beyond 12/31/2027). Relocation will not be provided. *Applications accepted until 5 PM PST on Wednesday, November 11th, 2027. *Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1, E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.). What You'll Do The below-mentioned areas of work will be prioritized under the management of the Deputy Director and in close collaboration with the Senior Program Officer leading the respective body of work. Economic and policy analysis Respond to analytical and policy requests from foundation leadership, program strategy teams, regional and country offices, and Global Policy and Advocacy colleagues. Conduct rapid research, quantitative analysis, literature and evidence reviews, and targeted data pulls to answer concrete policy questions. Lead research on topics such as blended finance structures, local currency financing, capital market development, credit enhancement, and sovereign and sub-sovereign financing. Synthesize findings into clear, decision-ready materials. Draft concise, decision-ready products for leadership and cross-foundation engagements, including talking points, meeting and travel briefs, policy notes, investment memos, presentations, and short analytical memos. Translate technical economic material into clear findings for non-specialist and senior audiences without losing analytical rigor or important caveats. Draft and contribute to policy papers, briefs, and thought leadership that advance the foundation’s positions on private capital mobilization and domestic resource mobilization. Investment portfolio and grantmaking Support the management of a defined set of investments within the innovative financing and domestic capital body of work, and agree a shared set of outcomes with each grantee. Co-manage these investments across the grant lifecycle, including: concept development and due diligence budget and proposal review results frameworks and monitoring reporting and close-out Contribute to strategy for the innovative financing and domestic capital portfolio, including landscaping, finding opportunities, and translating insights into priorities. Track portfolio performance and emerging evidence, and identify risks in your investments. Innovative financing and transaction support Analyze deal structures, financial models, and term sheets. Assess risk-sharing and credit enhancement mechanisms such as guarantees, first-loss capital, and securitization. Coordinate with transaction advisors, investors, and co-financiers to move transactions from concept to close. Policy Function knowledge products and operations Support the lead SPO, in managing the Policy Function’s portfolio of reusable knowledge products, including datasets, charts, analytical tools, templates, reference materials, and country and institution profiles, so recurring questions can be answered faster and more consistently. Curate DPAF policy notes, presentations, data products, and prior analytical work so that relevant intelligence builds over time rather than remaining in one-off files or inboxes. Standardize recurring analytical workflows, including data refreshes, chart production, source documentation, and quality-control checks. Support the design and upkeep of the Policy Function SharePoint site as the main internal access point for DPAF products, including information architecture, taxonomy, file naming, permissions, and publication workflows. Document the approach so it can be sustained. Maintain a tracker of incoming analytical and policy requests, prepare status updates for the Policy Function lead, and make demand and bottlenecks visible so urgent requests do not crowd out strategically important work. Track DPAF’s internal advisory contributions and external policy voice, and compile periodic summaries for staff review. Support the DPAF learning series, including materials, coordination with presenters, and archiving of recordings and supporting content, and support internal knowledge-sharing on the innovative financing portfolio. AI and data tools Apply AI-assisted research, synthesis, and knowledge-management tools where they improve speed, quality, or reuse, within foundation data-governance requirements. Improve analytical workflows in the Microsoft environment, including Power BI and, where relevant, Azure Databricks, for data preparation, analysis, visualization, and repeatable reporting. Prototype efficient workflows for recurring data and po licy products, including responsible automation and structured quality assurance. Partnerships and coordination Co-manage relationships with a defined set of external partners, such as development finance institutions, multilateral development banks, co-funders, and capital market actors, and represent the foundation in related working groups and convenings. Engage grantees, co-funders, development finance institutions, multilateral development banks, and capital market actors, including preparing for and following up on partner meetings, working groups, and convenings. Coordinate across teams so the body of work stays aligned with sector strategies in health and agriculture. Your Experience Advanced degree in economics, finance, public policy, international development, or a related field, ideally with substantive economics coursework, and 6+ years of relevant experience in development finance, investment, financial sector development, or economic policy. Candidates with a bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of relevant experience are also encouraged to apply. Solid understanding of the external financing landscape for low- and middle-income countries, including: development finance institutions and multilateral development banks blended finance and impact investors local capital markets and institutional investors sovereign and sub-sovereign financing Working knowledge of at least one other DPAF priority area, such as ODA, sovereign debt and fiscal policy, domestic resource mobilization, MDBs and the international financial architecture, country macroeconomics, or non-DAC finance. Familiarity with innovative financing instruments and transaction structures, such as guarantees, blended finance vehicles, local currency lending, bonds, and securitization. Exposure to transaction advisory, investment analysis, or deal structuring is a plus. Experience managing complex projects, with strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to work with quantitative data, interrogate sources and assumptions, and translate results into clear policy-relevant conclusions. Strong Excel skills expected; experience with statistical or programming tools is welcome. Excellent writing, editing, and synthesis skills, with a track record of producing clear, concise materials for senior and non-specialist audiences, such as policy papers, briefs, investment memos, and presentations. Judgment to work quickly without losing sight of the broader policy question, know when more rigor is needed, and surface risks, assumptions, and trade-offs clearly. Ability to build strong, trusting relationships with internal colleagues and external partners, and to work effectively in a matrixed environment across economists, policy specialists, and data and technology colleagues. Demonstrated ability to take ownership of ambiguous tasks, create structure where little exists, and manage several priorities to a finished product with minimal direct supervision. Experience working in or with Sub-Saharan Africa and/or South Asia; familiarity with the health or agriculture sectors is a plus. Sound judgment in handling internal and pre-publication material. Preferred Hands-on experience building or administering SharePoint sites, including information architecture, permissions, and publication workflows. Hands-on familiarity with AI-assisted research or analytics and with Azure Databricks and Power BI, especially to improve repeatable analytical or knowledge workflows. *Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. jobs.title: Information Security Analyst
jobs.description: By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive. Why join Harvard Medical School? Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership. You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine. Harvard Medical School nurtures a diverse group of leaders and future leaders in both clinical care and biomedical inquiry who are on the front lines of medicine and science serving individuals and populations locally, nationally, and globally. The Information Technology Department at Harvard Medical School enables this mission by delivering secure and scalable services. Digital Identity is a key underpinning of the digital transformation strategy driving trust and seamless experiences for our incredibly talented community. The Security team in the Harvard Medical School Department of Information Technology is seeking an Information Security Analyst to help build and sustain Vulnerability, Cloud and DLP Management solutions and to provide critical operational support for HMS infrastructure. This position offers a breadth of opportunity, ranging from traditional on-prem systems and solutions to contemporary cloud solutions. The Information Security Analyst will work collaboratively with all departments within HMS IT and Harvard University IT. PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Operate recurring vulnerability and compliance reporting, quality-check results, and distribute reports to HMS groups on schedule. Advise system administrators on findings and remediation, and track issues through to verified closure. Run day-to-day execution of the endpoint security compliance effort, ensuring required security agents are deployed and healthy. Monitor cloud security posture, triage misconfigurations, and work with cloud owners to remediate findings. Support vendor risk management, including security reviews and follow-up on identified issues. Triage data loss prevention alerts and coordinate remediation of sensitive data on shared storage. Support security assessments, penetration testing, and the security awareness program. Build dashboards and reports, and use basic scripting to automate recurring tasks. Basic Qualifications: Minimum of five years’ experience post-secondary education or relevant work experience. Additional Qualifications and Skills: Bachelor's degree in information systems, cybersecurity, or a related field. Working knowledge of vulnerability management fundamentals, including CVE and CVSS, risk prioritization, and remediation timelines. Demonstrated ability to obtain results from technical staff who do not report to you, with strong written and verbal communication skills. Hands-on experience with enterprise vulnerability scanning, endpoint protection, or asset inventory tools. Experience with cloud security posture management and common cloud misconfigurations. Experience with vendor or third-party security risk assessments. Experience with data loss prevention alert triage and sensitive data remediation. Experience with endpoint management and agent deployment at scale. Experience with IT service management or GRC ticketing and reporting. Familiarity with HIPAA, NIST SP 800-53, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, or comparable frameworks. Experience in higher education, an academic medical center, or a research environment, especially with decentralized IT groups. Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to act as a trusted advisor. Certificates and Licenses: SecAI+ Security+ PenTest+ CCSK Cloud+ Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week. Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Criminal. Interview Format: All interviews will be conducted remotely using a video conferencing platform. Staying Informed About Your Application: Due to the high volume of applications, we may not always be able to reach out right away, but you can track your status anytime through the Careers@Harvard portal. #LI-DK1 Work Format Details This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that the duties and responsibilities can effectively be performed fully remotely at a non-Harvard location. Employees in fully remote positions must work all scheduled hours in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts . At the discretion of the department, fully remote employees may occasionally be required on site at a Harvard location. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment. Salary Grade and Ranges This position is salary grade level 058. Please visit Harvard's Salary Ranges to view the corresponding salary range and related information. Benefits Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to: Generous paid time off including parental leave Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one Retirement plans with university contributions Wellbeing and mental health resources Support for families and caregivers Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page . EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination . We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes. Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy . As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.    Your Team:   The Division of Budget, in the Office of Finance & Administration, is composed of 3 Units: Expense, Grants & Revenue, and Operations. Your Team in the Budget Expense Unit manages the agency’s $1+ billion operating budget, which is comprised of nearly 25 funding streams from city, state, federal, and other categorical sources. The division’s staff advise and support HPD’s program managers and budget liaisons on matters pertaining to funding availability, grant compliance, cost savings initiatives, financial analysis, and program development.   Your Impact:  As budget analyst for the Division of Budget-Expense Unit, you will play a pivotal role managing the budget for the City Housing Assistance Program.  Your work will involve close collaboration with your colleagues in the division, as well as the division’s key stakeholders across the agency. jobs.description: ICF is seeking an experienced Senior Data Processing Specialist to provide technical leadership for data processing, digital data collection, and data-related innovation under The DHS Program and other large-scale surveys in low- and middle-income countries. This is a senior, hands-on role: the successful candidate will resolve complex technical and data-quality problems, strengthen the skills of Data Processing Specialists, consultants, and country counterparts, and promote consistent technical practices across the survey portfolio. The Senior Data Processing Specialist will also help shape how AI and automation are used in DHS data processing, contributing to a team that includes AI engineers and other specialists. jobs.description: ICF is seeking a motivated Survey Manager to provide technical leadership and coordination to national implementing agencies conducting population-based surveys through The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) Program; and to inform and support technology-enabled innovations that improve the efficiency of the overall survey process. Survey Managers typically lead one active survey at a time. The Survey Manager is ICF’s main day-to-day counterpart to the national implementing agency, usually a statistics office or ministry, and supports country ownership of the survey from design through dissemination. Survey Managers coordinate a cross-functional team of sampling, data processing, biomarker, GIS, and communications specialists. The Survey Manager works within a portfolio of surveys overseen by a Survey Portfolio Manager, who provides mentoring, budget and forecast information, and backup support. jobs.description: ICF is hiring a Junior International Labor Analyst to support work with the U.S. Department of Labor (USDOL) Office of Child Labor, Forced Labor and Human Trafficking (OCFT). On behalf of OCFT, ICF conducts research, analysis, and preparation of written communications related to international child labor, forced labor, human trafficking, trade, and supply chain issues. The Junior International Labor Analyst will apply knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research methods, write for the intended audience, and formulate strategies to engage with relevant countries or stakeholders based on USDOL priorities and interests. This position also coordinates between elements of USDOL, U.S. Government agencies, nongovernmental organizations, and regional and international organizations. The position will be full-time and onsite at the U.S. Department of Labor in Washington, D.C. (occasional meetings will occur in the ICF office in Rockville, MD). Key Responsibilities: Research and Analysis: Applying knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research methods, conduct systematic and objective inquiry and analysis of international child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking issues. Desk Research: Performs data collection from existing global and local sources of data. Conduct library and computer research. jobs.description: PUBLIC POLICY & COMMENT ANALYSIS SPECIALIST Are you interested in assisting Federal agencies by analyzing public feedback on current and emerging federal policy issues and regulatory programs? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy and Economics (RPE) portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of federal programs and is seeking an experienced public policy analyst and comment analysis project contributor/manager to join them. Join our multidisciplinary team of regulatory specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously and providing a wide range of support services for a variety of federal clients. This full-time position is available immediately and primarily located in Reston, VA (i.e., in the DC Metro area) with flexibility for telework considered. Job Responsibilities: The Public Policy and Comment Analysis Specialist will be focused primarily on the review, processing, and analysis of public comments on highly scrutinized and often controversial public policy topics. The Public Policy and Comment Analysis Specialist will contribute to and assist in directing teams of ICF staff on individual tasks and whole projects associated with comment analysis support for Federal regulatory initiatives. jobs.description: ICF is hiring a Senior Research Analyst to perform a critical role within the Office Child Labor, Forced Labor and Human Trafficking (OCFT) of the International Labor Affairs Bureau (ILAB) at the U.S. Department of Labor. ILAB increases American job and wage growth by combating foreign labor abuses and unfair trade practices in global supply chains that undermine U.S. prosperity and security. The position requires the ability to provide expert advice to ILAB regarding opportunities in global commerce to create and enforce labor standards for trade agreements to combat child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking in global supply chains that undermine the American economy and security. The Senior Research Analyst is a mid-level, non-supervisory position responsible for conducting complex, high-impact research in support of organizational priorities, statutory requirements, and congressionally mandated reporting. Working with a high degree of independence and analytical judgment, the analyst proactively identifies and executes research opportunities, evaluates complex qualitative and quantitative information, and develops findings and recommendations for senior leadership and other stakeholders. The position provides ILAB with expert research on governments’ efforts to eliminate exploitative labor from supply chains and the worst forms of child labor. The position also provides—in conjunction and under the supervision of OCFT leadership—mentorship, review, and guidance to junior analysts. The position reports to the ICF Senior Manager and at DOL the Lead International Relations Officers and/or Division Chiefs within OCFT and may be based in Washington, DC, or remotely. Key Responsibilities: Advanced Research and Analysis for Congressionally Mandated Reports: Conducts and supports research necessary to fulfill congressionally mandated reporting and other statutory or organizational requirements. Independently identifies and pursues research opportunities that strengthen, expand, or otherwise further the organization's ability to meet congressionally mandated reports, including the List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor and/or List of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor . Independently determines appropriate research approaches, methodologies, data sources, and analytical techniques based on the nature and objectives of the research. Synthesizes information from multiple qualitative and quantitative sources to identify trends, relationships, risks, gaps, and emerging issues. Evaluates the reliability, relevance, and limitations of available information and applies sound analytical judgment when information is incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous. Develops well-supported findings, conclusions, and recommendations and clearly communicates the significance and implications of research results to technical and non-technical audiences. Anticipates emerging research needs and identifies opportunities to address information gaps, improve the evidence base for required reporting, and enhance the quality and relevance of organizational research products. Maintains awareness of relevant legislative, policy, programmatic, and research developments and assesses their potential implications for current and future analytical work. Guidance and Mentorship: Provides technical guidance and mentorship to junior research analysts by sharing research best practices, analytical methods, institutional knowledge, and subject-matter expertise. Reviews research and analytical products and provides substantive, constructive feedback to strengthen methodological rigor, accuracy, clarity, and analytical reasoning. Assists junior analysts—in conjunction and under the supervision of OCFT leadership—in addressing complex research questions, evaluating sources and evidence, interpreting findings, and effectively communicating analytical results. Research Products and Communication: Prepares or contributes to high-quality reports, briefings, memoranda, presentations, and other analytical products for senior leadership, congressional reporting, and other internal or external stakeholders. Translates complex research findings into clear, concise, and defensible conclusions tailored to the needs of the intended audience. Presents and explains research methodologies, findings, limitations, and implications and responds to substantive questions regarding analytical work. Quality Assurance and Research Improvement: Provides a senior-level review of analytical research products, as appropriate, to help ensure research is methodologically sound, appropriately supported by evidence, and consistent with applicable standards and requirements. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: The position requires advanced knowledge of research principles, methodologies, and analytical techniques; demonstrated ability to independently design and execute complex research projects; and skill in evaluating and synthesizing qualitative and quantitative information from diverse sources. The incumbent must demonstrate strong analytical judgment, critical thinking, written and oral communication, and the ability to develop defensible findings and recommendations from complex or incomplete information. The position also requires the ability to provide effective technical guidance and mentorship, coordinate analytical work across multiple contributors, and communicate complex findings to senior leaders and other stakeholders. The Senior Research Analyst must demonstrate initiative in identifying emerging research needs and opportunities, particularly those that support or strengthen congressionally mandated reporting and other high-priority organizational requirements. Required Qualifications: Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional research experience conducting complex research on international child labor, forced labor, exploitative labor practices, or global supply chains. Experience contributing to congressionally mandated, statutory, or other U.S. Government reports and research products. Demonstrated ability to independently identify, develop, and execute research projects addressing emerging issues or information gaps. Security Clearance: Ability to obtain low-level security clearance (U.S. citizenship, having resided in the U.S. for the past 2 years, and ability to perform the work of this position from a location within the United States). Preferred Qualifications: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, or mentorship to less experienced analysts without formal supervisory responsibilities. Experience evaluating government laws, policies, enforcement efforts, and programs related to exploitative labor practices. Demonstrated ability to produce clear, well-supported analytical findings and recommendations for senior-level audiences. Professional Skills: Superb writing skills, including economic policy brief writing with an ability to tailor the tone, content and form of written output to different audiences and to suit a variety of formats; ability to synthesize information and communicate in an accurate and coherent manner. Humility to receive feedback, revise deliverables, and accept directions from others. Ability to think strategically, creatively and to find innovative ways to respond to emerging organizational and project needs. Detail-oriented and deadline-driven with strong organizational skills with an ability to work remotely. Ability to work in a dynamic environment with changing requirements and priorities. Strong cross-cultural, interpersonal, management, and collaboration skills in highly complex structures involving multiple teams and stakeholders. Critical thinking, sound problem solving, and decision-making skills. Highly self-motivated and able to work independently as well as in team settings. jobs.description: About Nava Nava is a consultancy and public benefit corporation working to make government services simple and effective. As a client services company, we guide agencies constrained by legacy systems to a future with sharp user experiences built on secure, reliable, fault-tolerant cloud infrastructure. Final title/compensation will be determined by how your interview weighs against our core competencies during your interview cycle. Position summary A data scientist uses data, statistics, and programming to help projects make better decisions and build predictive models that solve our clients’ problems. The data scientist works across the full data lifecycle, from collecting raw data to communicating insights to stakeholders in clear, actionable ways. Additionally, this role is responsible for exploring data using visualization libraries and business intelligence tools to identify relationships, trends, and anomalies that might not be obvious from raw data alone. These visualizations support both exploratory analysis—helping the data scientist generate hypotheses—and explanatory analysis—helping project teams quickly grasp key insights so they can make informed decisions. All duties will be in service of Nava's values: Be Active Stewards, Delivery over Dogma, Build Together, Innovation Requires New Perspectives, and Progress Takes Work. What you'll do Work with stakeholders to understand business problems and define data-driven questions to answer.​ Collect, clean, and transform large structured and unstructured datasets from multiple sources.​ Explore data to find patterns, trends, and anomalies using statistical analysis and visualization.​ Build, evaluate, and deploy machine learning and statistical models to make predictions or automate decisions.​ Communicate findings through dashboards, reports, and presentations to both technical and non-technical audiences.​ Participating in business development activities Participating in client stakeholder meetings related to growth Attending conferences and networking with potential clients Reviewing strategy plans and outlining technical requirements for potential work Hiring and growing data scientist talent Required skills 5+ years of experience in data science or applied ML roles Experience owning end-to-end analytics from discovery to modeling to storytelling to implementation Experience working with large, complex datasets across multiple sources Strong proficiency in Python Ability to design, train, evaluate, and operationalize ML models at production scale Builds and ships advanced statistical/ML models and pipelines using tools like Python and SQL in production Strong grasp of probability theory, random variables, common distributions, expectation, variance, and covariance.​ Solid training in estimation and inference: confidence intervals, likelihood, maximum likelihood estimation, and Bayesian basics Ability to choose appropriate statistical techniques for messy, real-world data and explain trade-offs, limitations, and uncertainties.​ Track record of translating statistical findings into clear, decision-ready narratives and recommendations for stakeholders.​ Ability to stay current with new methods and tools and apply them thoughtfully to real-world problems. Ability to create compelling visualizations (Tableau, Looker, matplotlib, Plotly) that clearly communicate patterns, trends, and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences. Strong intuition for model assumptions, uncertainty, and bias/variance tradeoffs; fluency with a broad range of statistical and machine-learning models and diagnostics. jobs.title: :    Executive Office Coordinator & Policy Analyst, NYC Housing Preservation Trust
jobs.description: On June 16, 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul signed the NYC Public Housing Preservation Trust Act, which authorized creation of the NYC Public Housing Preservation Trust (the Trust). The Trust is a public benefit corporation that will oversee the renovation and rehabilitation of the city’s public housing developments, owned by the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA). NYCHA remains permanent owner of the land/buildings and enters into a long-term ground lease with the Trust to secure a Section 8 rental subsidy contract with significantly higher value than NYCHA’s current federal subsidy. Using the rental subsidy contract, the Trust will raise financing to fund comprehensive building renovations. The Trust Act provides the Trust with the ability to convert up to 25,000 units, subject to a vote by the residents of a potential redevelopment site. No NYCHA site can convert to the Trust without a positive vote of the site’s residents. To date, residents at four developments have opted into the Trust, resulting in over 1,700 units that will be financed and renovated over the next five years, providing benefits to over 3,200 residents.   Our values are core to our work. The Trust has adopted the following values:  1)	Resident Empowerment: Center your efforts on the voices, needs, and leadership of residents in all aspects of the Trust’s operations. Actively engage and empower residents to foster stable, safe, and thriving communities.  2)	Action-Oriented Excellence: Commit to urgent and effective action while maintaining a dedication to high-quality outcomes. Drive impactful results with a focus on excellence.  3)	Future-Forward Resilience: Prepare our communities and buildings for the challenges of climate change and the future. Focus on creating resilient and sustainable environments to ensure long-term safety and adaptability.  4)	Informed Innovation: Integrate innovative ideas and best practices into our approach to public housing. Continuously improve and lead in the field by leveraging a network of global peers with similar missions and values.  5)	Collaborative Strength: Embrace the power of partnerships between the Trust, NYCHA, and various stakeholders. Involve multiple agencies and partners in finance, design, engineering, social services, training, and community rebuilding to transform public housing communities.   Position Summary  The Executive Office Coordinator & Policy Analyst serves within the Office of the President and reports directly to the Chief of Staff. The position provides policy analysis, executive support, and governance coordination for the President, Chief of Staff, and Board of Trustees.  Working at the intersection of strategy, operations, and public policy, the Coordinator/Policy Analyst researches emerging policy issues, prepares executive briefings and Board materials, supports organizational policy development, and manages cross-functional initiatives that advance the Trust's mission.  The position requires exceptional analytical, writing, project management, and organizational skills. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable conducting policy research, synthesizing complex information into executive-level recommendations, coordinating Board governance activities, and managing high-priority initiatives across multiple departments.  As part of a newly established public benefit corporation, the Coordinator/Policy Analyst will play an important role in helping shape organizational policies, governance practices, and strategic initiatives supporting one of the nation's largest public housing preservation efforts.  Primary Responsibilities   Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:  Board Governance & Executive Affairs  •	Serve as the primary coordinator for all Board of Trustees and committee meetings, managing scheduling, logistics, meeting materials, and day-of operations.  •	Prepare and distribute Board agendas, briefing books, presentations, resolutions, scripts, and other governance materials.  •	Ensure compliance with Open Meetings Law requirements and Board governance procedures, including public notices, webcast coordination, agendas, minutes, and official records.  •	Draft and maintain accurate Board meeting minutes and track Board actions, resolutions, and follow-up items across departments.  •	Coordinate responses to Board requests and support continuous improvement of Board governance processes.  Communications & Organizational Support  •	Manage the Trust's general correspondence, including monitoring shared email accounts, routing inquiries, and preparing responses as appropriate.  •	Manage incoming and outgoing mail and maintain organized records and correspondence.  •	Coordinate updates to the Trust's website, social media, and other public-facing communications in collaboration with leadership.  •	Review executive communications, reports, presentations, and public materials for clarity, consistency, accuracy, and alignment with the Trust's mission and organizational priorities.  •	Assist with the preparation, formatting, and quality control of reports, policies, guidance documents, and other executive communications.  Executive Office Coordination  •	Provide executive support to the President and Chief of Staff, including calendar management, correspondence, meeting coordination, travel arrangements, and confidential administrative support.  •	Prepare meeting agendas, briefing materials, and summaries; document discussions and monitor implementation of action items.  •	Support executive operations through document management, signature routing, records management, invoice processing, expense tracking, and maintenance of office systems and templates.  •	Coordinate internal and external meetings and facilitate communication among Trust leadership, NYCHA, government agencies, and external partners.  •	Perform other related duties and special assignments in support of the Office of the President.  Policy Analysis & Strategic Initiatives  •	Conduct research and analysis on policy, legislative, regulatory, and organizational issues affecting the Trust, including affordable housing, public finance, governance, procurement, capital delivery, sustainability, and resident engagement.  •	Monitor emerging policy and legislative developments and prepare executive summaries, briefing memoranda, and recommendations for senior leadership.  •	Research best practices from peer public agencies, housing organizations, and public benefit corporations to inform organizational strategy and decision-making.  •	Prepare executive briefing materials, presentations, talking points, reports, and decision-support documents for the President, Chief of Staff, and Board of Trustees.  •	Support the development and implementation of organizational policies, governance documents, strategic initiatives, and cross-functional projects.  •	Coordinate special projects and strategic initiatives on behalf of the Office of the President, working collaboratively across departments and with external stakeholders.  Additional Information  1.	NYCHA employees applying for transfer, promotional, title or level change opportunities must have served a period of one year at current location and in current title and level (if applicable). 2.	NYCHA residents are encouraged to apply. 3.	NYCHA provides benefits that include a choice of medical coverage plans, deferred compensation plans and a defined pension benefit plan as a member of the New York City Employees’ Retirement System (NYCERS).  Please read this posting carefully to make certain you meet the minimum qualification requirements before applying for this position. Minimum qualifications: •	Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as public administration, public policy, communications, business administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience. •	Three years' work experience in executive support, board administration, operations, or project coordination roles. Preferred skills: •	Experience conducting policy research, strategic analysis, or program evaluation. •	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to synthesize complex information. •	Excellent written and verbal communication skills. •	Exceptional organizational and project management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and meet deadlines. •	Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience drafting professional correspondence, meeting minutes, issue papers, and recommendations, and presentation materials. •	Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment in handling confidential and sensitive information. •	Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Excel, and Word. •	Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively. •	Detail-oriented. •	Interest in working for a mission-oriented organization. •	Experience supporting a board of directors or similar governance body, including public meeting requirements. •	Knowledge of New York City government, public housing, or public benefit corporations. •	Experience maintaining an organization's website and social media presence. •	Graphic design and digital production skills. •	Familiarity with using generative AI tools to support day-to-day tasks.

jobs.title: Heating Contract Analyst
jobs.description: The Heating Contract Analyst (HCA) will support the Heating Management Services Department (HMSD) Contracts Unit in the administration, coordination, and oversight of the department’s contracting and procurement initiatives.   Reporting directly to and under the direction of the HMSD Deputy Director of Contracts, the HCA will work closely with departmental purchasing liaisons, operational staff, vendors, and central procurement teams. The position will support the oversight of contracted work, assist with the procurement of materials and services required to maintain heating and mechanical equipment, and monitor contract utilization and vendor performance.   The HCA will also help ensure that contracted work is properly authorized, competitively and reasonably priced, performed in accordance with applicable procurement requirements, and adequately documented from initiation through completion and payment.   Contract Coordination and Oversight   Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:   •	Review requisition and procurement packages submitted by HMSD purchasing liaisons to ensure that scopes, supporting documentation, and vendor quotations are complete, reasonable, and consistent with NYCHA procurement requirements.  •	Review scopes of work and project requirements to help determine the most appropriate procurement pathway and contracting method.  •	Review contractor proposals, supporting documentation, and completed work to evaluate cost effectiveness, completeness, and quality of performance.  •	Review contractor requests for the use of subcontractors and coordinate the appropriate agency review and approval process.  •	Support the review of contractor invoices and payment documentation and assist in resolving issues that may delay invoice processing or payment.  •	Coordinate with vendors regarding performance concerns, incomplete work, documentation deficiencies, and other contract compliance matters.  •	Track recurring contract or vendor issues, document lessons learned and recommend process improvements to strengthen contract administration and purchasing practices.   Field and Site Responsibilities   As necessary, the Heating Contract Analyst may be required to:  •	Attend site visits, pre-bid meetings, vendor walkthroughs, and other in-person meetings related to procurements or contracted work.  •	Document site conditions, vendor discussions, questions, and concerns and communicate findings to HMSD management and other appropriate stakeholders.  •	Observe contracted work in the field to assist with evaluating scope compliance, work quality, and project documentation.   Physical and Environmental Requirements   The position may require standing for extended periods; working in confined or restricted areas; wearing hard hats and other required personal protective equipment; bending and stooping during site inspections; and navigating around equipment, piping, construction materials, and other physical obstructions.   Field assignments are infrequent but may involve being in mechanical rooms, boiler rooms, construction areas, and outdoor locations where conditions may be hot, cold, damp, dark, dusty, smoky, or otherwise challenging. jobs.description: TASK FORCE: 		Parks, Cultural Infrastructure, and Capital Development   UNIT: 			Parks  JOB TITLE: 			One (1) Assistant Analyst / Analyst / Senior Analyst  CONTROL CODE: 		PCICD-27-01   SUMMARY:  The Mayor’s Office of Management and Budget (OMB) is the City government's chief financial agency. OMB's staff of analysts and experts assembles and oversees the Mayor’s expense and capital budgets, which fund the services and activities of approximately 90 City agencies and entities.   OMB’s Parks, Cultural Infrastructure, and Capital Development Task Force includes four distinct Units: the Parks Unit, the Capital Project Scope Development (CPSD) Unit, the Capital Coordination Unit, and the Culturals and Libraries Unit.   The Parks Unit monitors the expense and capital budget of the Department of Parks and Recreation as well as the expense budget of the Landmark Preservation Commission, including developing cost reduction proposals, reviewing agency fiscal requests, and determining the budgetary impact of programmatic decisions.    JOB DESCRIPTION:  The duties of this position encompass the following activities:   •	Monitoring expenditures for the Department of Parks and Recreation (DPR) and the Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC). •	Reviewing DPR requests for capital funding and project design approval, including completion of Certificates to Proceed, Budget Code Modifications, and Commitment Plan changes. •	Monitoring major capital program initiatives, including waterfront park construction, signature equity programs such as the Community Parks Initiative, and the conversion of industrial or landfill space to recreational uses. •	Evaluating program performance in the Parks budget, including parks maintenance and cleaning, reconstruction of parks, playgrounds, ball fields, etc., planting of trees, rehabilitation of stadiums, recreation centers, and other facilities, as well as vehicle and equipment replacement. •	Acquiring and maintaining detailed knowledge of DPR and LPC operations and programs. •	Reviewing and making recommendations regarding funding and personnel requests. •	Preparing annual budgets for DPR and LPC using City, Federal, State, and other funding. •	Monitoring financial plans using the Financial Management System and other software. •	Analyzing Federal, State, and Local legislation and regulations for fiscal impact on City parks. •	Developing cost reduction programs.  DESIRED SKILLS:  •	Demonstrated quantitative and analytic skills.  •	Ability to use formulas and pivot tables to analyze large data sets and effectively format spreadsheets for presentation and review.  •	Basic knowledge of Microsoft Access, Crystal, and FMS is preferred. •	Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.  •	Self-starter able to generate and complete projects with limited supervision. •	Must be able to work evenings and weekends as needed. jobs.description: At Pearson, our purpose is simple: to add life to a lifetime of learning. We believe that every learning opportunity is a chance for a personal breakthrough. The ideal candidate will combine expertise in academic or applied research with clinical experience administering, interpreting, or working directly with standardized assessments within speech-language pathology, literacy, academic achievement, and/or early childhood. This position will report to the Lead Learning Scientist and can be remote or based in our San Antonio, TX, or Bloomington, MN offices. Working across Content, Product, Psychometrics, Design, Editorial, and Digital Development, this role helps translate scientific evidence, clinical needs, customer needs, and business strategy into innovative, high-quality assessment solutions. Key responsibilities include: Develop and lead research plans supporting new product development, product revisions, and portfolio priorities. Provide subject-matter expertise and scientific leadership in speech-language pathology, literacy, achievement, and/or early childhood assessment. Help define product scope and assessment design , ensuring solutions are scientifically sound, clinically meaningful, and aligned with customer and business needs. Lead and contribute to item development, review, and evaluation , applying research, clinical expertise, and assessment-development best practices. Partner with psychometricians and research colleagues to review and interpret data and psychometric findings Identify opportunities to responsibly apply AI and emerging technologies to assessment development, research practices, workflows, and product innovation. Represent Pearson and contribute to its scientific leadership through conference presentations, technical papers, research publications, and other scholarly activities. Maintain flexibility in work hours , as needed, to collaborate with international colleagues, approximately 10% of the time. Travel approximately 10% . Think strategically: Connect research and scientific priorities to portfolio and business strategy, anticipate future needs, and identify opportunities to evolve assessment solutions. Lead through influence: Build credibility as a trusted scientific and clinical expert, bring clarity to complex issues, and influence decisions across functions and levels. Collaborate and build trust: Foster an inclusive, respectful, and accountable environment, seek diverse perspectives, communicate openly, and build strong cross-functional partnerships. Drive results and accountability: Take ownership of outcomes, exercise sound judgment, effectively manage competing priorities, and help teams move complex work forward. Champion innovation and continuous improvement: Challenge established approaches when appropriate and explore new research methods, digital capabilities, AI, and emerging technologies that can improve products and ways of working. EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE Ph.D. in Speech-Language Pathology, Communication Sciences and Disorders, Early Childhood Development, School or Clinical Psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution. 5+ years professional experience in speech and language, literacy, academic achievement, school or clinical psychology, and/or early childhood. Clinical experience administering, interpreting, or working directly with standardized assessments, with a strong understanding of their use in real-world clinical or educational settings. Strong knowledge of test development, measurement principles, research methodology, data analysis, and psychometric principles, with the ability to apply these concepts to research and product decisions. Demonstrated ability to translate scientific and clinical evidence into strategic recommendations that balance scientific rigor, clinical relevance, customer needs, product priorities, and business objectives. Strong digital fluency and curiosity, including the ability to evaluate and appropriately apply AI and emerging technologies to research, assessment development, and evolving ways of working. The Civilian Development Unit (CDU) provides department-wide training for civilian and uniformed members, supporting operational readiness, professional standards, and supervisory development. jobs.description: Job Type: Regular Position Description RAND's Economics, Sociology and Statistics (ESS) department is seeking a National Security Economics Researcher at all career stages to contribute to rigorous, policy-relevant research at the intersection of economics and national security. RAND researchers lead and contribute to projects that deliver objective, rigorous evidence to inform decisionmakers across the defense, intelligence, and foreign policy communities. Researchers working on national security economics in ESS bring quantitative analytical skills to bear on a wide range of questions, including how U.S. commercial economic power (i.e. the capacity embedded in private firms, markets, and industries) can be identified, protected, and operationalized to advance national security while sustaining domestic prosperity. Their work spans economic statecraft, sanctions, and export controls; supply chain and critical materials dependencies; the defense industrial base and manufacturing strategy; cost- and benefit-sharing between government and commercial actors; and the strategic implications of concentrated technical expertise in frontier technologies. Why RAND? · Reputation for Excellence : Be part of a non-profit, non-partisan organization renowned for its rigorous and objective research. · Dynamic Opportunities : Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams on diverse projects that challenge and expand your skills. · Poised for Impact : Your research will directly inform senior policymakers across the defense, intelligence, and foreign policy communities, and will draw on close engagement with senior practitioners across the private sector. Responsibilities: National Security Economics Researchers at RAND apply their analytical and substantive expertise to: Design and conduct rigorous economic analyses of national security problems, including how commercial capabilities such as supply chains, financial networks, and technologies can be used to achieve strategic effects, and the secondary and tertiary consequences of doing so. Frame priority questions for and help convene small working groups of senior private-sector practitioners; translate government and RAND requirements into workable, unclassified formats; and distill practitioner judgment into objective, evidence-based findings. Produce short-form analytic products for U.S. government decisionmakers on timelines matched to the requirement alongside longer-form research on generational challenges such as cost- and benefit-sharing in national security, human capital as a strategic good, and manufacturing as a source of commercial economic power. Develop reusable analytic frameworks, models, and tools, including commercially informed tabletop exercises and AI-enabled capabilities for assessing economic leverage, exposure, resilience, and private-sector incentives. Communicate research results to national security policymakers and the public through written products and oral presentations. Contribute to business development efforts, including proposal writing and cultivating relationships with sponsors in the defense and national security community, as well as with private-sector partners and supporters. Mentor junior researchers and contribute to a collaborative, inclusive research environment. Qualifications All research positions at RAND require: Demonstrated training in quantitative research methods Strong analytic skills and intellectual curiosity Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English The ability to work effectively as a member of inclusive, multidisciplinary teams A strong commitment to RAND's core values of quality and objectivity Successful applicants will have demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following content areas: Economic statecraft, including sanctions, export controls, investment screening, and the national security uses of financial networks Industrial organization, supply chains, and the defense and broader industrial base, including manufacturing, critical minerals, energy, and logistics Public economics and mechanism design, including measuring and allocating private costs and benefits in public-private collaboration Economics of innovation and human capital in frontier technologies such as AI, semiconductors, and biotechnology International trade, finance, and macroeconomics as they bear on strategic competition Experience We welcome applications from candidates at all stages of their research careers, from recent PhD graduates to experienced senior researchers. Applicants should present evidence of research experience appropriate to their career stage, demonstrated through academic publications, conference presentations, or prior professional research products. The ability to conceptualize research studies and contribute to business development, commensurate with career stage, is expected. Experience working with private-sector practitioners, for example in finance, energy, manufacturing, technology, or law, or translating market insight for government decisionmakers is highly desirable. Education Requirements A PhD in economics, finance, policy analysis, or a closely related field; or a Master's degree with 10+ years of research experience. Economists (with a recent PhD in economics) should apply through Job Openings for Economists (JOE) to ensure application review aligns with the job market cycle. Security Clearance The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance is strongly preferred. Location Washington, DC Application Materials/Writing Sample A CV, cover letter, and at least one writing sample of 3 or more pages are required when applying. Applicants are encouraged to use recent research published in academic journals, conference proceedings, or research reports; policy memos or other short-form analytic products are also welcome. Applications should include documentation of academic and professional activities that meet the stated qualifications. Note that applicants invited to interview will be required to present a seminar describing recent research. Salary Range : $110,900 - $283,100 Associate Researcher: $110,900 - $180,300 Full Researcher: $126,400 - $211,700 Senior Researcher: $171,800 - $283,100 Hiring ranges for Economists, Management Scientists and Physician Researchers are slightly higher than the ranges shown. RAND considers a variety of factors when formulating an offer, including but not limited to, the specific role and associated responsibilities; a candidate's work experience, education/training, skills, expertise; and internal equity. Successful candidates will be offered employment as an Associate or Full Researcher, as determined by the candidate's education and experience. The salary range includes base pay plus RAND's sabbatic pay (which provides additional compensation above base pay when vacation is taken). In addition, RAND provides strong benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, paid time-off and more Application Deadline This notice will be open until November 16, 2026. Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description: Job Type: Regular Physical Security Analyst Overview The Physical Security Analyst plays an important role in protecting RAND’s people, facilities, assets, and classified information. This individual contributor supports the day-to-day delivery of a comprehensive physical security program across unclassified spaces, closed areas, and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs). Partnering closely with the Physical Security Manager, the Physical Security Analyst helps maintain a secure, compliant, and service-oriented environment. Responsibilities include assessing physical security risks, supporting access-control and security-system operations, coordinating with the contract guard force, and identifying practical improvements to policies, procedures, and facility safeguards. The ideal candidate brings sound judgment, technical aptitude, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to resolving security issues in a dynamic environment. This position requires 100% in-office support and may require occasional after-hours support. Duties and Responsibilities Evaluate and maintain compliance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), 32 CFR Part 117, ICD 705, applicable NIST 800-171 physical security requirements, Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), and other applicable requirements. Conduct physical security risk assessments to identify facility vulnerabilities, evaluate potential risks, and recommend and implement mitigation strategies. Prepare and review security documentation, fixed-facility checklists, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support government audits, inspections, and assessments. Analyze physical security metrics and recommend improvements to operational effectiveness and compliance. Oversee access control for open (unclassified), closed (classified), and SCIF areas. Operate and administer the Access Control System (ACS) database, ensuring accuracy and compliance with established security procedures. Enroll personnel into security systems and issue corporate and government-mandated identification badges. Verify security clearances and access authorizations for employees, contractors, and visitors; resolve access-related discrepancies. Evaluate access-control procedures and recommend improvements to strengthen facility security. Monitor and program facility Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) networks; identify and address security-system deficiencies. Coordinate preventive maintenance and emergency repairs for alarms, cameras, electronic locks, and related security equipment. Troubleshoot complex security-system hardware and software issues in coordination with external integration vendors. Review and analyze system logs and archived video footage to investigate security incidents or anomalies and recommend corrective actions. Assist with coordinating assignments and operational needs for the contract security guard force. Support company events to help ensure the security and safety of facilities and visitors. Perform other related duties as assigned. Basic Qualifications Strong knowledge of ICD 705 Technical Specifications, 32 CFR Part 117, and physical security requirements applicable to classified facilities and SCIFs. Knowledge of access-control systems, intrusion detection systems, and CCTV systems. Experience supporting physical security operations in unclassified, classified, and/or SCIF environments. Experience administering access-control databases and verifying personnel clearances and access authorizations. Knowledge of Communications Security (COMSEC) requirements and procedures. Ability to independently evaluate security risks, recommend corrective actions, and troubleshoot complex technical problems. Experience coordinating assignments for contract security guards. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with close attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and relevant security tools. Ability to prepare security documentation, SOPs, checklists, reports, and audit materials. Must be able to pass a background check. Education Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field required. An equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor’s degree. Experience Bachelor’s degree: At least five years of relevant experience in physical security operations, access-control systems, classified facility security, security systems administration, or a related security discipline required. Without a bachelor’s degree: At least nine years of relevant experience required. Security Clearance Must hold and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance and be able to obtain and maintain SCI eligibility. Occasional after-hours support may be required. jobs.description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION AND THE OPPORTUNITY The Education Trust (Ed Trust) seeks a Senior Research Analyst in our New York office (ETNY). The Senior Research Analyst will join a staff committed to fulfilling our mission of closing opportunity gaps that disproportionately affect students of color and students from low-income backgrounds. The Senior Analyst serves as a content expert on quantitative and qualitative research, advancing research and policy priorities in alignment with EdTrust-New York’s strategic goals. This role will produce research that highlights trends and inequities for students of color and students from low income backgrounds. The Senior Analyst will develop analyses, research briefs, data tools and visualizations, presentations, and other communications that advance, promote, and elevate strengths and opportunities for increasing educational equity in New York City and across the state. Successful candidates will bring knowledge of and ability to access and analyze publicly available education datasets in New York State and New York City through an education equity lens. Ed Trust is committed to advancing policies and practices to dismantle the racial and economic barriers embedded in the U.S. education system. Through our research and advocacy, Ed Trust improves equity in education from preschool through college, engages diverse communities dedicated to equity and justice, and increases political and public will to build an education system where all students will thrive. Available immediately, this role is based in our New York office and works primarily from a home office in New York or New Jersey. The Senior Analyst reports to the Lead II of Research. ABOUT THE SENIOR ANALYST, RESEARCH ROLE The responsibilities and objectives for the role include, but are not limited to, the following: · Develop and conduct quantitative analyses - using publicly available data - that examine socioeconomic and race-based patterns in opportunity and success, leveraging coding skills and analytics software to conduct descriptives and subgroup analyses. · Develop and conduct qualitative analyses; including original data collection that examine socioeconomic and race-based patterns in opportunity and success, leveraging focus groups, survey instruments, and analyses software. · Manage and implement multiple projects that identify promising policies for advancing educational equity, including producing tools and resources for diverse audiences (e.g., students, policymakers, families, and institutional leaders) · Mine data from publicly available sources to produce replicable datasets that help identify equity gaps and bright spots · Produce reports, briefs, data visualizations, blogs, and other resources to further inform policymakers, educators, journalists, and other public audiences of Ed Trust - New York’s agenda. · Serve as a spokesperson for Ed Trust - New York by sharing and elevating analyses and policy recommendations publicly with various audiences--including the media, advocates, and policymakers -- that inform and align with Ed Trust’s policy priorities of eliminating educational disparities and enhancing student outcomes. · Elevate Ed Trust’s policy priorities by developing key relationships and representing the organization in external meetings with external stakeholders, peer organizations, policymakers, leaders, funders, and other advocates. · Collaborate internally across EdTrust - New York to support fundraising and grants management, strategic communications · Support and facilitate advisory groups that inform EdTrust - New York’s strategic actions and research products, including topical advisory groups that include student members · Respond to rapid response inquiries about policy and/or data analyses from staff, as well as work with the team to respond to policymakers, advocates, the media, and the public IDEAL SKILLS AND CHARACTERISTICS · Shared belief in Ed Trust’s mission and a commitment to improving educational equity with a focus on racial equity · Dedication in contributing to and maintaining an equitable working environment · Excellent analytic and communication skills, both oral and written, and in a variety of formats and contexts · Strong project management (including time management) skills, with the ability to manage work across multiple stakeholders and meet project milestones / deadlines · Advanced knowledge and experience in Excel, R/R Studio, Tableau, Python, SQL and github; · Knowledge and experience in Excel, ASANA, Microsoft Outlook, and other administrative software · Demonstrated ability to manage and manipulate data and conduct descriptive analyses with excellence · Critical thinker, problem solver, and continuous learner, with ability and interest in working in a fast-paced and collaborative office · Willingness to receive and act upon, as well as provide, constructive feedback QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience: · At least a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; advanced degree a plus/preferred? · At least four years of experience conducting and/or analyzing research and data in education policy or a related field, preferably on topics of equity · Demonstrated ability to produce quantitative and qualitative research analyses that address education equity and closing gaps in opportunity and outcomes · Significant understanding of education policy in New York City / New York State, and the ability to learn, understand and apply relevant qualitative and quantitative education data to a policy context · Knowledge of and familiarity with publicly available data sources on P12 education in New York City / New York State · Demonstrated experience using analytical software and coding COMPENSATION This position falls in Level C of our salary structure. The new hire salary range for this position is $73,530 - $91,920. New hire offers are rarely offered at the top of this range and are commensurate with skills, experience and internal equity. The Education Trust prioritizes the health and well-being of its employees and, to that end, offers a highly competitive benefits package. Medical, dental and vision insurance are covered at 100% for the employee, with significant coverage also offered for spouses, domestic partners, and dependents. We provide sick leave, vacation leave, and personal leave, and we follow the federal government for most holiday closures. To ensure staff have synchronous opportunities for rest and renewal, the office is closed for a week-long summer break and a week-long winter break. Among other offerings, we provide an Employee Assistance Program at no cost to the employee, and a generous 7% contribution opportunity on a 403(b)-retirement plan. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play. Posted Job Title Qualitative Student Research Assistant Job Profile Title Temporary Employee - Co-op Worker Job Description Summary This Qualitative Student Research Assistant will assist the Army-SPRING qualitative research team with data collection (semi-structured interviews, periodic reflections), qualitative data extraction, and quality data checking. The qualitative research assistant will attend regular qualitative team analytic meetings weekly. This is posting is for graduate students from universities other than the University of Pennsylvania. Job Description Study: The Army-Suicide Prevention Research on Implementation in the National Guard (Army-SPRING) is a study designed to strengthen the implementation of suicide prevention policies within the Connecticut Army National Guard (CTARNG). Army-SPRING tests an implementation package of supports for suicide intervention officers (SIOs), chaplains, and religious affairs specialists in collaboration with CTARNG. This Hybrid Type 3 cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluates the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of this implementation package compared with a resilience-focused control group. The long-term goal of Army-SPRING is to inform scalable implementation strategies that can strengthen suicide prevention policy and military infrastructure, ultimately reducing suicide risk among National Guard service members nationwide. Role : This Qualitative Student Research Assistant will assist the Army-SPRING qualitative research team with data collection (semi-structured interviews, periodic reflections), qualitative data extraction, and quality data checking. The qualitative research assistant will attend regular qualitative team analytic meetings weekly. Preferred experience and skills : Completion of graduate-level qualitative research methods course or equivalent; experience conducting qualitative semi-structured interviews; proficiency in methods such as template analysis and analytic coding; knowledge of implementation science and research ethics. Timing and Time Expectation : Training will begin November or December 2026 with role to begin January 2027. Role requires between 10 and 20 hours a week, which will include qualitative team and research meetings. Minimum commitment through August 2027.
