jobs.description: About the role: The Manager, Development Prospect Research plays a vital role in advancing Vera’s ambitious fundraising goals by managing and strengthening our prospect identification, research, and qualification strategies across institutional, major, and principal giving and strategic board development. This role supports frontline fundraisers by delivering strategic insight and timely analysis to build and advance a dynamic pipeline of funders aligned with Vera’s mission. Working closely with the Development and Executive teams, this position leads the development of tools and processes that ensure prospect data is well-curated, actionable, and integrated into the department’s broader strategy. 1. Prospect Identification and Research Lead prospect identification, qualification, and due diligence efforts for individual, foundation, and corporate donors. Conduct and synthesize research on philanthropic capacity, affinity, giving history, networks, and engagement opportunities to support fundraising strategy. Develop clear, actionable prospect profiles, briefing materials, and strategic recommendations for development leadership, executive staff, and board engagement. Proactively identify and prioritize high-potential prospects through wealth screening, database analysis, and external research tools. Provide research support for donor meetings, events, board recruitment, and other strategic engagement opportunities. 2. Strategy and Collaboration Partner with frontline fundraisers, development leadership, and program staff to align prospect strategy with fundraising and organizational priorities. Provide strategic recommendations on donor capacity, inclination, and engagement opportunities to inform cultivation and solicitation efforts. Proactively share prospect intelligence, relationship insights, and emerging funding opportunities with key stakeholders. Lead targeted prospecting initiatives to identify new donors aligned with priority programs, geographies, and fundraising goals. 3. Systems and Tools Development Develop and optimize research systems, workflows, and data management practices to improve efficiency, consistency, and data quality. Partner with Development Operations to maintain accurate prospect data, ratings, and relationship intelligence within the CRM. Evaluate and recommend research tools, subscriptions, and vendors, and train staff on prospect research methodologies and best practices. Lead relationship-mapping and network analysis initiatives while staying current on emerging trends, technologies, and practices in prospect research and philanthropy. 4. Portfolio and Pipeline Management Lead efforts to build, assess, and sustain a diverse, high-quality pipeline of prospective donors. Partner with fundraisers and leadership to develop and optimize prospect portfolios based on capacity, affinity, and readiness. Oversee prospect ratings, wealth screening, moves management, and research tracking to support portfolio growth and fundraising performance. Analyze donor and prospect trends and establish policies and practices that strengthen pipeline management, data integrity, and fundraising effectiveness. What qualifications are we looking for? Required: Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of relevant experience. In lieu of degree requirement, applicable work or life experience may be considered. 5+ years of experience in development prospect research, donor intelligence, or related nonprofit fundraising roles. Expertise with donor research methodology and practice, including wealth indicators and data analysis. Experience with a broad range of subscription research tools. Preferred: Strong communicator, able to collaborate across teams and present findings in a concise, compelling way. Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities you'll bring: Ability to synthesize large amounts of information and provide analysis. Resourcefulness in pursuing knowledge. Highly organized, detail-oriented and adept at follow-up while working effectively to meet deliverable due dates. Demonstrated initiative, resourcefulness, and problem-solving skills. Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively. Strong communication skills, both oral and written. Committed to protecting donor data and sensitive or proprietary information. Willingness to learn new systems and technology. Committed to Vera’s mission of advancing justice and equity, and you bring a lens of inclusion and cultural competency to your work. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment and enjoy building systems that support strategy and growth. Drives learning and professional growth in prospect development and philanthropy. Location: Please note this role will report to either our Brooklyn, NY (preferred) or Washington, DC office. Vera employees adhere to a hybrid schedule and are in-office on an alternating schedule that generally amounts to 10 days per month. Compensation and Benefits: The compensation range for this position is $100,000 - $105,000 . Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience and performance. The salary range listed is just one component of Vera Institute’s total compensation package for employees. As an employer of choice in our field, supporting Vera staff - both personally and professionally - is a priority. To do this, we invest in the well-being of our staff through other rewards including merit pay, generous paid time off, a comprehensive health insurance plan, student loan repayment benefits, professional development training opportunities and up to $2,000 annual for education costs and fees relevant to Vera work, employer-funded retirement plan, and flexible time. To learn more about Vera’s benefits offerings, click here . Application Process: To receive further consideration for this career opportunity, applicants are asked preliminary questions about logistics, their interest and qualifications. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional details about their experience via a phone screen/form in advance of an invitation for a virtual or in-person interview with the team. Some searches may explore scenarios during the interview process and/or an assessment prior to reference checks and a hiring decision. Applications may also be faxed to: ATTN: People, Place, and Culture / [ JOBTITLE] Vera Institute of Justice 34 35th St, Suite 4-2A, Brooklyn, NY 11232 Fax: (212) 941-9407 Please use only one method (online, mail or fax) of submission. No phone calls, please. Only applicants selected for interviews will be contacted. Vera is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without unlawful discrimination based on race, color, creed, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, military status, prior record of arrest or conviction, citizenship status, current employment status, or caregiver status. Vera works to advance justice, particularly racial justice, in an increasingly multicultural country and globally connected world. We value diverse experiences, including with regard to educational background and justice system contact, and depend on a diverse staff to carry out our mission. For more information about Vera, please visit www.vera.org .

Experience for this position includes:(1) analyzing data modeling concepts and reviewing data for trends from multiple systems, (2) assisting in research and statistical analysis on available data to improve program materials and documentation, and (3) perform basic queries using various types of database and analytical tools. OR YOU MAY QUALIFY FOR THE Band 2 (GS-7) BASED ON EDUCATION: 1 full year of graduate-level education or superior academic achievement. jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Instructional Designer Fully Remote Description SUMMARY: The Instructional Designer - Learning Experience Design assesses learning needs and designs, develops, and delivers innovative learning solutions aligned with organizational goals, learner competencies, and regulatory requirements across multiple content domains and modality channels. The position includes hands-on development. The instructional designer completes projects from discovery through evaluation and supports ongoing curriculum management, content governance, and learning quality standards. Reporting to the Instructional Design Director, this position operates independently and collaborates with subject matter experts, program partners, and team members to turn complex information into practical, accessible learning resources across behavioral health, training, and organizational development initiatives. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include but are not limited to: Assess learner and performance needs and recommend appropriate solutions in collaboration with the Instructional Design Director and program partners. Gather, clarify, and translate complex technical, clinical, and regulatory content into plain-language learning materials and practical guidance, preserving the intended meaning and validating accuracy with appropriate subject matter experts. Conduct audience analysis and adapt content, terminology, examples, and learning approaches to learners’ roles, prior knowledge, work settings, and application needs; organize content into logical learning pathways and sequences. Develop learning objectives, instructional approaches, storyboards, activities, and assessments aligned with established content standards and learner needs. Create learning blueprints and, when projects are handed off, complete design packages for developers; remain available to review the product against the blueprint. Build eLearning modules, instructor-led training materials, facilitation guides, scripts, videos, job aids, webinars, and blended learning solutions using appropriate authoring tools. Prepare and test courses for LMS delivery, including SCORM packaging. Apply department standards for instructional quality, accessibility, usability, and visual consistency. Coordinate project responsibilities, reviews, and timelines with the Director and team members. Design evaluation measures and feedback mechanisms in partnership with Evaluation/Analytics team members and use data to refine and improve learning solutions. Support curriculum planning, content governance across the LMS, EHR knowledge base, and agency websites. Develop and maintain learning management system (LMS) documentation, templates, and best practices guides. Conduct instructional design reviews and quality assurance checks on learning materials to ensure adherence to standards. Support training and mentoring of new design team members or contractors on ID processes and tools. Stay current with instructional design best practices, emerging technologies, and industry trends through ongoing professional development. Other duties as assigned, demonstrating flexibility and commitment to organizational success. QUALIFICATIONS – An acceptable equivalent combination of education, experience, and skill may be considered. Education: Bachelor's degree in Instructional Design, Education, Learning Sciences, Human Resources, Communications, or a related field. Experience: Four (4) or more years of experience in instructional design, learning and development, training design, or related field. Demonstrated experience designing healthcare, compliance, behavioral health, or regulatory training materials. Experience with learning management systems (LMS) administration, course configuration and learning paths. Experience designing and delivering training across multiple modalities: eLearning, instructor-led, synchronous, asynchronous, and blended formats. Demonstrated experience with video production, editing, and multimedia content creation. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Job Specific Knowledge & Skills: Proficiency in eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline, Rise, or Captivate; ability to quickly master new authoring platforms. Working knowledge of SCORM standards. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and learning management systems. Strong working knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG accessibility standards for digital content. Experience with video production tools such as Camtasia, Adobe Premiere Pro, or similar. Proficiency with visual design and graphic design software such as Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or equivalent. Demonstrated ability to apply adult learning principles and instructional design models to practical learning outcomes. Strong SME collaboration, content synthesis, writing, and plain-language communication skills. Communication Collaboration & Time Management Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent written and verbal communication abilities. Ability to explain complex learning and instructional design concepts clearly to subject matter experts, leaders, and diverse audiences. Ability to exercise independent judgment, conduct research, and ask appropriate probing questions to complete necessary tasks. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously with varying priority levels and competing deadlines. Comfortable using virtual collaboration tools, including Teams, Zoom, and SharePoint. Personal Attributes: Detail-oriented and organized, with a strong commitment to accuracy, quality, and best practices. Demonstrates quality assurance mindset with excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in all work products. Demonstrates initiative, independence, sound judgment, and resourcefulness in completing assignments. Adaptable and able to manage shifting priorities in a fast-paced, evolving learning environment. Comfortable working in a remote environment and maintaining accountability to leadership. PHYSICAL DEMANDS - The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and stand; use phone and headset; use hands, arms, and fingers to type; answer phones; write; use a calculator; lift and carry materials weighing up to 10 pounds; demonstrate clear vision to read printed materials and a computer screen; use hearing and speech to communicate in person and over the telephone; and drive a motor vehicle on public roads and highways. SENSORY DEMANDS - The incumbent must spend long hours in intense concentration. The incumbent must also spend long hours on the computer entering information, which requires attention to detail and high levels of accuracy. MENTAL DEMANDS - There are a number of deadlines associated with this position, which may cause significant pressure. The incumbent must also deal with a wide variety of people on various issues and manage multiple concurrent projects and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment. REGULAR WORK SCHEDULE – Varies depending on business needs; however, company normal business hours are 8:00am to 5:00pm, Monday – Friday Salary Description $110,000 - $135,000

jobs.title: Supervisory Computer Scientist
jobs.department: Department of Health and Human Services
jobs.description: This position is located in the Department of Health & Human Services (HHS), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) located in Hyattsville, Maryland. This announcement will close at 11:59 PM, on the day that 50 applications have been received or on the closing date, whichever is first. Qualifications: WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Basic Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in computer science or bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of mathematics, statistics, and computer science. At least 15 of the 30 semester hours must have included any combination of statistics and mathematics that included differential and integral calculus. All academic degrees and course work must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Minimum Qualifications: You must have one year specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Planning, coordinating, and overseeing information technology hardware and software systems that support the collection, processing, and management of large-scale national survey or health-related data. Leading the deployment, integration, and maintenance of IT infrastructure and software applications used to collect, validate, transmit, and process national survey and Electronic Health Record (EHR) data. Planning, directing, and overseeing complex information technology projects and multidisciplinary teams supporting national survey and EHR data collection initiatives. Documenting experience: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE. Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience. In addition to describing duties performed, applicants must provide the exact dates of each period of employment (from MM/YY to MM/YY) and the number of hours worked per week if part time. As qualification determinations cannot be made when resumes do not include the required information, failure to provide this information may result in disqualification. Applicants are encouraged to use the USAJOBS Resume Builder to develop their federal resume. Do not copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational application questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description. Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment. The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record. In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to gain employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. If such experience is on a part-time basis, you must provide the average number of hours worked per week as well as the beginning and ending dates of the experience so it can be fully credited. jobs.title: Program Analyst (Navy Gold Star Coordinator)
jobs.location: Washington Navy Yard, District of Columbia
jobs.description: This position is assigned to Navy Gold Star Program; Casualty Support Programs (N95); Commander, Navy Installations Command (CNIC). Casualty Support Programs are the Navy's primary agency for the delivery of an array of human services programs intended to enhance the stability and self-sufficiency of wounded, ill and injured Service Members (SM) and survivors of deceased SM's. The programs fall under the Casualty Support category and include Wounded Warrior, Fisher House and Navy Gold Star. Qualifications: Resumes must include information which demonstrates experience and knowledge, skills, and ability (KSAs) as they relate to this position. Applicants are encouraged to be clear and specific when describing their experience level and KSAs. A qualified candidate must possess the following: At least three years of progressively responsible specialized experience providing assistance and case management service to military family members. A qualified candidate must also possess the following: Knowledge of military and DoD program guidance. Knowledge and understanding of DoD and DON long term survivor assistance programs and services. Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and Defense Casualty Information Processing System. Skill in the use of office software applications and required management data systems to enter data, prepare reports, and develop information. Skill in working with military casualty or bereaved families of fallen service members. Skill in collecting, organizing, and analyzing data from various resources, to include statistical studies and surveys. Skill in providing assessment of survivor needs and referral of survivors to appropriate resources. Ability to understand, be sensitive to, and have empathy for survivors. Ability to develop trusting helping relationships and to work effectively with individuals and families from diverse racial, ethnic, religious, and socioeconomic backgrounds. Ability to intervene in crisis situations, using sound professional judgment, ethical practice, and common sense. Ability to work cooperatively with military and civilian organizations on behalf of survivors. Ability to identify needs, trends, and performance measures to evaluate program effectiveness and provide recommendations for process improvements. Ability to use data management and reporting systems to collect and organize data drawn from databases. Ability to compose written reports and material clearly, concisely, and effectively. Ability to develop and effectively deliver presentations and/or training. Ability to maintain professional boundaries and ethics to the highest extent and use extreme caution when interacting with survivors. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

jobs.description: This position is being filled under the memorandum from the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (USD(P&R)) "Expansion of Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense," dated August 12,2024. This position is part of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency. Qualifications: You may qualify at the GS-14, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service as listed below: Developing long-range program/project goals, plans and objectives; Providing specialized scientific and engineering judgment on nuclear and conventional weapons effects, equipment fragility, and battle damage assessments as they relate to strategic C4I and WMD facilities; Conducting scientific and technical research in areas of seismic, acoustic, electromagnetic, multi-spectral, and hyper-spectral disciplines to identify, characterize, target, and assess battle damage to adversary C4I and WMD facilities; Managing scientific and technical research and mission critical component analysis to identify and quantify foreign system vulnerabilities, and; Using US intelligence systems to develop and execute national collection strategy (NCS) for identification, characterization, targeting and battle damage assessments (BDA) of C4I and WMD facilities. (Experience must be clearly demonstrated in your resume) Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0801/1301, series as listed below: A. For Engineering series 0801 - Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. B. For Engineering series 0801 - Combination of education and experience - college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test - Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses - Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum - Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all-inclusive.) C. For Physical Scientist series 1301 - Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. (Must provide transcripts) D. For Physical Scientist series 1301 - Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education. (Must provide transcripts and experience clearly demonstrated in resume)

To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-11 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples of creditable specialized experience may include planning and executing complex physical science studies, which usually involved intensive investigations into recognized phenomena. This work typically involved conventional methods and techniques though it required going beyond clear precedents, and required adapting methods to the problems at hand and interpreting findings in terms of their scientific significance. At this level, physical scientists have the ability to independently perform scientific work of considerable difficulty. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-12 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. Examples may include research design; analysis and implementation; analysis and/or consolidation of research findings data to identify strategic research areas or needs. FOR GS-14: Successfully completed 1 year of specialized experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position, and that is in or related to the position to be filled. To be creditable, the specialized experience must have been at the GS-13 grade level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service. jobs.description: About Ellucian Ellucian powers innovation for higher education, partnering with approximately 3,000 customers across 50 countries, serving more than 21 million students. Ellucian's AI-powered platform, trained on the richest dataset available in higher education, drives efficiency, personalized experiences, and strengthened engagement for all students, faculty and staff. These solutions and services span the entire student lifecycle, including data-rich tools for student recruitment, enrollment, and retention to workforce analytics, fundraising, and alumni engagement. Ellucian's innovative solutions, vast ecosystem of partners and user community of more than 45,000 provides best practices leading to greater institutional success and achieving better student outcomes. About the Opportunity At Ellucian, we believe in the transformative power of education, and our cloud solutions are central to powering that transformation for colleges and universities around the world. The FinOps team supports the development, scalability, and financial sustainability of Ellucian's cloud solutions through effective governance, financial transparency, and cross-functional collaboration. The team helps establish organizational accountability for technology consumption and costs while maximizing the business value of cloud and other consumption-based technology investments. Success is measured through predictable and scalable costs, effective governance, improved financial visibility, and measurable optimization outcomes. As a FinOps Analyst, you will help drive financial accountability, governance, and optimization across Ellucian's cloud and technology investments. You will independently own assigned FinOps initiatives, analyze technology consumption and spending, identify opportunities for improvement, and partner with technical and business stakeholders to translate financial and operational data into actionable decisions. Where You Will Make an Impact Own and drive FinOps initiatives within assigned areas of responsibility, improving visibility, accountability, governance, and optimization across cloud and technology consumption and spend. Analyze cloud and third-party technology usage, cost, and operational data to identify trends, anomalies, cost drivers, financial risks, and opportunities for optimization. Identify, quantify, prioritize, and track cost optimization opportunities, partnering with technology owners and stakeholders to implement improvements and measure realized savings, cost avoidance, and business value. Support and improve FinOps governance practices, including resource tagging, metadata standards, cost allocation, ownership, policy compliance, and controls that enable accurate financial accountability. Monitor consumption-based technology platforms and services, including Datadog, to understand usage patterns, evaluate cost drivers, forecast financial impact, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and value. Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, forecasts, and key performance indicators that provide visibility into technology consumption, optimization progress, governance compliance, and financial performance. Support budgeting and forecasting activities by analyzing historical consumption, growth trends, business drivers, and planned technology changes to improve financial predictability. Utilize cloud financial management, observability, analytics, and FinOps tools to support operational requirements, financial analysis, and technology optimization initiatives. Partner with stakeholders across Cloud Engineering/Operations, R&D, Product, Finance, Procurement, and other business functions to integrate FinOps practices into day-to-day technology planning and decision-making. Investigate unexpected consumption or cost changes, collaborating with technical teams to identify contributing factors, assess financial impact, and recommend appropriate corrective actions. Help evaluate and establish financial governance for emerging technologies and consumption models, including SaaS, observability, data platforms, and AI services as organizational needs evolve. Identify opportunities to improve FinOps processes, controls, reporting, and operational effectiveness through automation, improved analytics, and standardized practices. Support improvements in automated reporting, consumption monitoring, and cost anomaly detection to increase efficiency, data accuracy, and visibility into optimization opportunities. Contribute to the continued maturity of FinOps practices by improving cost allocation, forecasting, governance, and financial accountability across technology investments. What You Will Bring 2+ years of experience in FinOps, cloud financial management, cloud operations, observability/platform operations, technology governance, technical program/project management, financial/business analysis, or a related discipline. Hands-on experience with Datadog, including the ability to analyze usage, consumption trends, and cost drivers across one or more Datadog capabilities. Experience analyzing technology usage and cost data to identify trends, anomalies, optimization opportunities, and financial impact. Experience supporting or implementing technology governance practices such as resource tagging, metadata management, cost allocation, policy compliance, or ownership and accountability controls. Working knowledge of public cloud infrastructure and services, with AWS experience particularly relevant. Experience developing dashboards, reports, and analytical views used to communicate financial or operational performance, including consumption trends, forecasting, and optimization opportunities. Strong Microsoft Excel and data analysis skills, with the ability to work with complex datasets and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Familiarity with cloud financial management and analytics tools such as Cloudability, AWS Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Reports (CUR), CUDOS, or similar platforms. Understanding of consumption-based technology cost models, including cloud infrastructure, SaaS, observability platforms, or other variable-consumption services. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate cost drivers, evaluate opportunities, and recommend practical solutions. Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders and influence action without direct authority. Ability to independently manage assigned initiatives and priorities while collaborating effectively across technical and business teams. Detail-oriented, with strong documentation, organizational, and financial reporting skills. Familiarity with FinOps principles, technology cost optimization, and opportunities to improve reporting or governance through automation and analytics. Experience using AI-powered productivity tools, such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or similar solutions, to support data analysis, research, reporting, documentation, and workflow efficiency, with appropriate validation of AI-generated outputs. jobs.title: Assessment Administrator (Contract)
jobs.description: Today, 67% of students and 82% of low-income students can’t read at grade level by the end of third grade. That’s when students are supposed to go from learning to read to reading to learn. It’s America’s number one education crisis and we know how to fix it. Ignite Reading delivers one-to-one virtual tutoring that teaches every student the foundational skills they need to become a confident, fluent reader. We pair students who need extra support with expert reading tutors who provide daily, 15-minute, Science of Reading-based instruction that rapidly closes their decoding gaps. We focus on the foundational reading skills—phonics, phonemic awareness, and sight words—kids need to master so they can decode a sentence. Students in Ignite Reading’s program achieve over 2 weeks of reading skills growth per week of instruction, and notably all students achieve the same outstanding results including students with IEPs, multilingual learners, students of color and those receiving free or reduced-price lunch. Ignite Reading is a mission-driven public benefit corporation. We believe we can do well for our team members and shareholders while we solve one of the nation’s biggest challenges. We believe we will be more successful with a diverse team and are seeking candidates who have lived experience related to social justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Your Role : As a DIBELS 8th Edition Assessment Administrator contracted by Ignite Reading, your primary responsibility will be to travel to various schools in Massachusetts and administer the DIBELS (Dynamic Indicators of Basic Early Literacy Skills) assessments to the students enrolled in our program. Your role is crucial in helping us gauge student progress and tailor our instruction to their needs. Key Responsibilities: Assessment Administration: Travel to assigned schools within Massachusetts to administer DIBELS /Acadience assessments to K-3 students enrolled in Ignite Reading. Follow established assessment protocols to ensure consistency and reliability. Scheduling and Coordination: Collaborate with school staff and Ignite Reading's team to schedule assessment sessions, ensuring minimal disruption to the school's daily routines. Data Collection: Accurately record and maintain assessment data for each student in Amplify mCLASS. Ensure the security and confidentiality of student information and assessment results. Communication: Provide clear and concise instructions to students during the assessment process. Address any questions or concerns raised by students or school staff. Quality Assurance: Follow standardized assessment procedures to maintain the integrity and reliability of the assessment data. Report any irregularities or issues encountered during assessments. Reporting: Compile and submit assessment data and results to Ignite Reading in a timely and organized manner. Generate reports as needed to track student progress. Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in Education or a related field is preferred. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, especially when working with students in an educational setting. Must be located in the state of Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Albany, NY, Connecticut, or New Hampshire, preference for candidates in central or eastern Massachusetts. Flexibility in working with different schools and students within Massachusetts during the academic day. Strong/advanced knowledge of the science of reading and foundational skills Knowledge of the Amplify mCLASS assessment tool Knowledge and experience administering the DIBELS 8th or previous edition, Acadience, or other aligned early literacy and oral reading fluency assessments assessments Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail. The ability to work independently and follow established assessment protocols. Must pass a federal background check and a Massachusetts-specific background check Administration Windows: BOY (Beginning of Year) -9/9/2026-10/16/2026 MOY (Middle of Year) -exact dates TBD, but timeframe is Jan-March EOY (End of Year) -exact dates TBD, but timeframe is May-June Why Join Ignite Reading? Transparent Compensation At Ignite Reading, we've embraced a transparent compensation structure to promote fairness and equity, provide accountability, and build trust within our organization. Hourly Rate: $55 / hour (this role is part-time, non-exempt) The same role receives the same compensation, with no negotiation. This is a part-time role averaging 3-4 weeks in duration at 10-20 hours per week during administration windows. This role is not to exceed 300 total hours. We believe in building and fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace environment. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer where all applicants are considered for employment without attention to color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status. Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds often don't apply for roles if they don't meet all the criteria – unlike majority candidates meeting significantly fewer requirements. We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested! We are seeking candidates who have lived experience related to social justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are a virtual organization with headquarters in the California Bay Area.

jobs.title: Technical Writer / Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Technical Writer / Instructional Designer Remote Indianapolis, IN (Corp) Full time This position supports the Technical Instruction team in revising and producing high-quality training and technical documentation, and in transforming that documentation into structured, standardized learning solutions. Reporting to the Associate Director, Technical Instruction, the Technical Writer / Instructional Designer collaborates with subject matter experts (SMEs), quality, operations personnel, and business leaders to ensure that procedural documents, training presentations, competency verification documents, and other learning materials are accurate, clear, consistent, and ready for deployment in multiple learning environments. The role converts SOPs into learning pathways, develops modular training content and a training catalog, maintains standardized curricula, and prepares reskilling and upskilling pathways that support a harmonized, global approach to technical training and strengthen the effectiveness of training across the organization. Key Accountabilities Document Revision & Writing Review, revise, and restructure quality documents to improve clarity, accuracy, and compliance with applicable quality and regulatory standards. Map current workflows with subject matter experts before drafting or revising procedures to ensure documentation reflects how work is performed. Draft new SOPs and work instructions in collaboration with subject matter experts. Apply consistent style, formatting, and language aligned with company templates and document control procedures Training Material Development Revise and develop training presentations and job aids for instructor-led and self-guided formats, ensuring content is engaging, logically structured, and aligned with learning objectives. Develop visual process aids, such as flowcharts, decision trees, and swim lane diagrams to supplement written procedures and training materials. Create and update competency verification documents, including knowledge checks, practical assessments, and sign-off forms. Adapt complex technical content into accessible, audience-appropriate language for varied learner levels. Coordinate with subject matter experts to validate technical accuracy prior to finalization. Produce learning and training materials in a variety of formats, including print, graphics, audio, video, animation, and multimedia, selecting the format best suited to the content and audience. Develop the production of classroom handouts, instructional materials, learning aids, and manuals. undefined Instructional Design & Learning Pathways Convert SOPs and work instructions into structured learning pathways with defined learning objectives, content sequencing, practice activities, and competency verification. Develop modular, reusable training content and build and maintain a training catalog that allows learning to be built once and deployed across sites and roles. Prepare reskilling and upskilling pathways that support role transitions, new or revised processes, and individual and team development. Apply best practices in instructional design and adult learning theory to the strategy, design, and delivery of online, in-person, and blended learning. Training Evaluation & Continuous Improvement Create evaluations and report on the effectiveness of training programs to confirm that taught skills and techniques are incorporated into employees’ work behavior. Evaluate ongoing programs to ensure continued relevance to business processes and employee development. Regularly maintain and update online course content, learning pathways, and the training catalog based on feedback, process changes, and evaluation results. Maintain training records and present training data and effectiveness metrics to management teams. Learning Support Prepare scripts, presenter notes, and on-screen text for prerecorded training presentations, ensuring alignment between narration and visual content. Review draft or recorded training modules for consistency, completeness, and readability; provide written revision recommendations as needed. Support the Associate Director, Technical Instruction in organizing and maintaining the training content library and training catalog. Collaboration & Communication Partner with department SMEs to gather accurate technical information for documentation projects. Develop and maintain strong working relationships with SMEs and business leaders to support training needs assessment, content validation, and adoption of learning solutions. Assist with periodic document reviews and audit-related updates as assigned. Communicate project status, timelines, and risks to the Associate Director, Technical Instruction in a timely manner. Participate in team meetings and contribute to process improvement initiatives related to documentation and training workflows. undefined Minimum Requirements Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Technical Writing, Instructional Design/Technology, Educational Technology, English, Communications, Information Systems, or a related scientific discipline; or equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum 2 years of technical writing experience in a regulated industry environment; familiarity with lean methodologies (5S, standard work, kaizen, or similar) and experience documenting processes in a continuous improvement culture preferred. Demonstrated experience writing and revising SOPs, work instructions, or equivalent procedural documentation. Experience translating verbal or informal process descriptions into structured visual workflow documentation (process maps, flowcharts, swim lane diagrams). Experience developing or revising PowerPoint presentations for training or instructional purposes. Proven experience designing and developing multiple training events, curricula, or learning using adult learning principles. Experience maintaining training records. Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English; strong organizational and multitasking skills required. Skills and Abilities Exceptional written communication skills; ability to write clearly for both technical and non-technical audiences. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Teams) and Adobe Acrobat; SharePoint experience preferred. Ability to analyze and document workflows; experience creating process maps, flowcharts, or swim lane diagrams using Visio, Lucidchart, PowerPoint, or similar tools. Familiarity with document control principles and regulated-industry standards (GLP, GCP, or ISO environments preferred). Ability to quickly learn scientific subject matter and translate it into accurate, understandable documentation. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and meet deadlines independently. High attention to detail; consistent, error-free deliverables. Knowledge and application of adult learning principles and instructional design models; ability to design online, in-person, and blended learning. Ability to write effective documentation, user guides, and learner materials. Ability to evaluate training effectiveness and present data and findings to management teams. Preferred: 5 years of experience in human resources, education, instructional design, or a related field; experience with training evaluation systems; multilingual ability desirable. Working Conditions & Physical Requirements Work is primarily performed in an office or remote environment; periodic on-site presence will be required. Sitting for extended periods of time, talking for extended periods of time, reaching while standing and general repetitive motions, especially as related to computer work. Ability to read and interpret materials, verbally communicate, and hear required. Office environment. Moderate noise level. Critical Success Factors Communication. Able to communicate information and ideas clearly and articulately both in oral and written form. Uses appropriate language, style and methods depending on audience and the purpose of communication. Able to convey complex information clearly. Anticipates the information that others will need. Expresses ideas effectively. Practices attentive and active listening. Collaboration. Actively supports and contributes to the success of the team. Actively encourages and practices collaboration and cooperation on the team. Shares information and supports other team members. Can get things done with and through others and set realistic objectives. Seeks opportunities to develop others. Relationship Builder. Develops, maintains, and strengthens strong partnerships with others internally and externally, cross functionally, in person and remotely. Improvement Driven. Inspires and generates new solutions and approaches to issues and challenges to maximize efficiency and effectiveness through everyday practice of root cause analysis and critical thinking problem solving; Continually works to refine skills and abilities; Builds on ideas of others to come up with new ways to address issues or problems; Generates creative new solutions and approaches to issues and processes. Organization and Time Management. Plans and prioritizes work, manages time appropriately to meet deadlines, follows up with others to ensure one’s own work and commitments are completed on time, deals with pressure and deadlines through good planning. jobs.title: Instructional Designer Level III
jobs.description: Atlassian Instructional Designer Level III Job Locations US-Remote ID 2026-14816 # of Openings 1 Overview LMI is seeking an Instructional Designer at the Level III level to develop accessible, effective learning experiences supporting Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Agile practices and Atlassian Cloud adoption. This role combines learning strategy, curriculum design, digital content development, and performance support to translate complex processes and tools into practical instruction for a diverse federal workforce. The Instructional Designer will design role-based learning paths for leadership, Scrum Masters, Product Owners, delivery teams, and tool administrators. The position develops live-instruction materials, self-paced e-learning, hands-on exercises, job aids, assessments, and adoption-hub resources using ADDIE or SAM and tools such as Articulate Storyline and Rise. Content will be prepared for the existing learning management system and validated against accessibility requirements. This is not a slide-production-only role. The designer must identify the performance problem behind a training request, define measurable learning objectives, test content with representative learners, and refine materials based on completion data and user feedback. The ideal candidate balances technical accuracy with adult-learning principles, concise writing, visual clarity, and Section 508 compliance. LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed. Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value. Responsibilities Conduct needs analysis and translate assessed learner cohorts and job roles into measurable learning objectives. Design role-based courses on Agile practices, Jira Cloud, reporting, and administrative workflows using ADDIE or SAM. Develop instructor guides, presentations, demonstrations, exercises, assessments, e-learning modules, and concise job aids. Author and maintain Articulate Storyline or Rise content and package courses for SCORM-compatible LMS delivery. Coordinate publishing, course metadata, completion tracking, pilot testing, and revisions with LMS and training operations staff. Perform accessibility reviews and coordinate Section 508 and WCAG testing and remediation for self-paced content. Maintain consistent, version-controlled adoption-hub and knowledge-base resources. Create curriculum maps that connect learner role and readiness level to objectives, prerequisites, modality, activities, practice tasks, and knowledge checks. Script accurate Jira Cloud and Agile demonstrations with consistent terminology, realistic workflows, annotated screenshots, and accessible interaction patterns. Build facilitator notes, learner guides, scenario-based exercises, quick-reference cards, and assessment items that reinforce on-the-job application. Conduct editorial, functional, and accessibility quality assurance; document remediation decisions before course publication and updates. Manage content versions, review cycles, SME approvals, and content ownership so learning materials stay aligned with changing platform configurations. Qualifications Required: Bachelor's degree in instructional design, education, learning technologies, educational psychology, or a related field. 3+ years of instructional design, e-learning development, or performance-support experience. Demonstrated use of ADDIE or SAM and Articulate Storyline or Rise. Experience with SCORM packages, LMS course publishing, and training evaluation. Knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG accessibility requirements and accessible content design. Ability to obtain and maintain a favorable Public Trust determination and satisfy applicable federal personnel vetting, security, privacy, accessibility, and data-handling requirements. Section 508 Trusted Tester certification or equivalent formal accessibility testing credential. Portfolio or work samples demonstrating both instructor-led design and interactive e-learning or digital performance support. Ability to collaborate with technical SMEs and translate detailed workflows into accurate, concise, and accessible learner-facing content. Desired: Prior experience supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), or federal health programs is highly desirable. Master's degree in instructional design, education, learning technologies, or a related discipline. Agile, Jira Cloud, Confluence Cloud, or federal enterprise training experience. Experience creating blended learning for large distributed audiences. Experience designing simulation-based software instruction, formative assessments, and post-training performance reinforcement. Additional certifications such as ATD Associate Professional in Talent Development (APTD) or Certified Professional in Talent Development (CPTD) are desirable. Target Salary Range: $85,000 - $115,000 Disclaimer: The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation. Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances. LMI recruits, hires, trains, and promotes people without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, pregnancy, disability, age, protected veteran status, citizenship status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

jobs.title: CLINICAL LABORATORY SCIENTIST
jobs.description: About the Position: This position is located within the A.T. Augusta Military Medical Center, in a Clinical Laboratory setting. The incumbent will be responsible for coordinating the full range of clinical laboratory services. This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Certain Personnel of the DoD to recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. Qualifications: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Clinical Laboratory Scientist: A. A Bachelor's or graduate/higher level degree from a regionally accredited college/university including courses in biological science, chemistry and mathematics, AND successful completion of a Medical Laboratory Scientist/Clinical Laboratory Scientist program accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS) or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education at the time the degree was obtained. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts and proof of program completion.) OR B. At least a full 4-year course of study that included 12 months in a college or hospital-based medical technology program or medical technology school approved by a recognized accrediting organization. The professional medical technology curriculum may have consisted of a 1-year post- bachelor's certificate program or the last 1 or 2 years of a 4-year program of study culminating in a bachelor's in medical technology. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR C. A bachelor's or graduate/higher level degree from an accredited college/university that included 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) of biological science (with one semester in microbiology), 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) of chemistry (with one semester in organic or biochemistry), one semester (one quarter) of mathematics, AND five years of full time acceptable clinical laboratory experience in Blood Banking, Chemistry, Hematology, microbiology, Immunology and Urinalysis/Body Fluids. This combination of education and experience must have provided knowledge of the theories, principles, and practices of medical technology equivalent to that provided by the full 4-year course of study described in A or B above. All science and mathematics courses must have been acceptable for credit toward meeting the requirements for a science major at an accredited college or university. Acceptable experience is responsible professional or technician experience in a hospital laboratory, health agency, industrial medical laboratory, or pharmaceutical house; or teaching, test development, or medical research program experience that provided an understanding of the methods and techniques applied in performing professional clinical laboratory work. Certification/licensure as a medical technologist (generalist) obtained through written examination by a nationally recognized credentialing agency or State licensing body is a good indication that the quality of experience is acceptable. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) Evaluation of Education and Experience: The four major areas of clinical laboratory science are microbiology, clinical chemistry, hematology, and immunohematology (blood banking). Qualifying course work in these areas includes bacteriology, mycology, mycobacteriology, tissue culture, virology, parasitology, endocrinology, enzymology, toxicology, urinalysis, coagulation, hemostasis, cell morphology, immunology, serology, immunoserology, immuno-deficiency, hemolysis, histocompatibility, cyto-genetics, and similar disciplines or areas of laboratory practice. Related fields include physiology, anatomy, molecular biology, cell biology, embryology, pathology, genetics, pharmacology, histology, cytology, nuclear medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, infection control, physics, statistics, and similar areas of science where the work is directly related to the position to be filled. Exemption: You are exempt from the basic requirements above if you are a current federal employee occupying a position in the 0644 occupational series and have been continuously employed in this occupational series since September 27, 2017 or before. Note: You will be required to provide appropriate documentation to the respective Human Resources Office to validate your status. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes establishing quality control methods and/or ranges; performing highly technical blood banking procedures; identifying and resolving inconsistent tests results; and analyzing lab test systems to ensure quality control. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.

jobs.description: About the Position: Serve as a Clinical Laboratory Scientist at the Andrew Rader Army Health Clinic located at Joint Base Myer, Virginia. Responsible for performing duties as a Clinical Laboratory Scientist for Chemistry, Hematology, Microbiology, and Urinalysis. This is a Direct Hire Authority (DHA) solicitation utilizing the DHA for Certain Personnel of the DoD to recruit and appoint qualified candidates to positions in the competitive service. Qualifications: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirements for Clinical Laboratory Scientist: A. A Bachelor's or graduate/higher level degree from a regionally accredited college/university including courses in biological science, chemistry and mathematics, AND successful completion of a Medical Laboratory Scientist/Clinical Laboratory Scientist program accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS) or an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education at the time the degree was obtained. OR B. At least a full 4-year course of study that included 12 months in a college or hospital-based medical technology program or medical technology school approved by a recognized accrediting organization. The professional medical technology curriculum may have consisted of a 1-year post- bachelor's certificate program or the last 1 or 2 years of a 4-year program of study culminating in a bachelor's in medical technology. OR C. A bachelor's or graduate/higher level degree from an accredited college/university that included 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) of biological science (with one semester in microbiology), 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) of chemistry (with one semester in organic or biochemistry), one semester (one quarter) of mathematics, AND five years of full time acceptable clinical laboratory experience in Blood Banking, Chemistry, Hematology, microbiology, Immunology and Urinalysis/Body Fluids. This combination of education and experience must have provided knowledge of the theories, principles, and practices of medical technology equivalent to that provided by the full 4-year course of study described in A or B above. All science and mathematics courses must have been acceptable for credit toward meeting the requirements for a science major at an accredited college or university. Acceptable experience is responsible professional or technician experience in a hospital laboratory, health agency, industrial medical laboratory, or pharmaceutical house; or teaching, test development, or medical research program experience that provided an understanding of the methods and techniques applied in performing professional clinical laboratory work. Certification/licensure as a medical technologist (generalist) obtained through written examination by a nationally recognized credentialing agency or State licensing body is a good indication that the quality of experience is acceptable. Evaluation of Education and Experience: The four major areas of clinical laboratory science are microbiology, clinical chemistry, hematology, and immunohematology (blood banking). Qualifying course work in these areas includes bacteriology, mycology, mycobacteriology, tissue culture, virology, parasitology, endocrinology, enzymology, toxicology, urinalysis, coagulation, hemostasis, cell morphology, immunology, serology, immunoserology, immuno-deficiency, hemolysis, histocompatibility, cyto-genetics, and similar disciplines or areas of laboratory practice. Related fields include physiology, anatomy, molecular biology, cell biology, embryology, pathology, genetics, pharmacology, histology, cytology, nuclear medicine, epidemiology, biostatistics, infection control, physics, statistics, and similar areas of science where the work is directly related to the position to be filled. Experience or graduate education must have been in (1) the general field of medical technology; (2) one of the disciplines or specialized areas of medical technology; or (3) a field directly related and applicable to medical technology or the position to be filled. Also, clinical laboratory intern (student medical technologist) experience in an education program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (external link) (CAAHEP) education program may be credited on a month-for-month basis toward meeting the GS-7 specialized experience requirement. Be sure to incorporate into the group standard language on the vacancy announcement and occupational questionnaire. Exemption: You are exempt from the basic requirements above if you are a current federal employee occupying a position in the 0644 occupational series and have been continuously employed in this occupational series since September 27, 2017 or before. Note: You will be required to provide appropriate documentation to the respective Human Resources Office to validate your status. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes establishing quality control methods and/or ranges; troubleshooting clinical analyzers when quality control is out of range; identifying and resolving inconsistent tests results; and making decisions on the validity of lab results before sending them out to providers. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Medical Laboratory Science, Medical Technology, or Clinical Laboratory Science. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Certification Preferred: Issued by the American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or the American Medical Technologists (AMT).

jobs.title: Operations Research Analyst
jobs.description: This position is part of the Department of War (DoW), Missile Defense Agency (MDA). The incumbent will be responsible for: Serve as the principal cost estimating expert for the program/team, providing authoritative guidance and analysis to program/organization leadership. The advertised salary for Fort Belvoir and Dahlgren, VA does not include the current rate of tax-free Cost of Living Allowance (COLA), which is 33.94%." Qualifications: You may qualify at the NH-04 Broadband Level, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-03/GS-13 grade level in the Federal service as listed below and must meet 3 of the 5 specialized experience listed below to be qualified: Develop, document, and deliver credible, accurate, comprehensive cost estimates and cost analysis to drive decision-making, program planning, resource allocation, and acquisition/contract efforts. Develop and maintain responsive cost estimating and analysis tools and models to quickly deliver cost estimating and analysis products to internal and external customers. Collect, validate, clean, and store data to establish secure databases to enable future use of such data in cost estimating and analysis. Conduct cost research, evaluate complex data, identify trends, and apply quantitative methods-such as linear and non-linear regression-to develop cost estimating relationships (CERs) and generate data-driven results. Prepare and present cost estimates and/or cost analysis, including results and recommendations, to customers and stakeholders to support decision-making. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 1515, series as listed below: Degree: in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus. Evaluation of Education: The primary requirement of operations research work is competence in the rigorous methods of scientific inquiry and analysis rather than in the subject matter of the problem. Therefore, applicants should have sufficient knowledge of applied mathematics to understand and use the fundamental concepts and techniques of operations research methods of analysis. In addition, some positions may require knowledge of a specific subject area. Courses acceptable for qualifying for operations research positions may have been taken in departments other than Operations Research, e.g., Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science. The following are illustrative of acceptable courses: optimization; mathematical modeling; queuing theory; engineering; physics (except descriptive or survey courses); econometrics; psychometrics; biometrics; experimental psychology; physical chemistry; industrial process analysis; managerial economics; computer science; measurement for management; mathematical models in social phenomena; and courses that involved application of operations research techniques and methodologies to problems of management, marketing, systems design, and other specialized fields; or other comparable quantitative analysis courses for which college-level mathematics or statistics is a prerequisite. Courses in theory of probability and statistics are highly desirable, but are not specified as minimum educational requirements because to do so would possibly exclude some applicants who would otherwise be well qualified. NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position. All materials must be submitted by the closing date of the announcement.
