jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Instructional Designer Full-Time 25-9030 SC, US Waterbury, CT, US Salary Range: $65,000.00 To $80,000.00 Annually JOB SUMMARY The Instructional Designer is responsible for designing and developing engaging, accessible, and performance-first online learning experiences that promote authentic application and student success. This role applies evidence-based instructional design principles to create aligned course content, meaningful learning activities, and assessments that support measurable learning outcomes. Working collaboratively with Program Chairs, faculty, Subject Matter Experts, multimedia professionals, Builders, and academic leadership, the Instructional Designer leads instructional planning and content development while contributing to academic initiatives, quality assurance, technology innovation, and continuous improvement. This is a 12-month position, working remotely in the United States, with hours corresponding to the Eastern Time zone. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS 1. Instructional Design & Content Development Apply evidence-based instructional design principles, adult learning theory, and performance-first design practices to create engaging, rigorous, and accessible online learning experiences. Develop course roadmaps, student-facing instructional content, authentic scenarios, interactive activities, guided and independent practice, and meaningful feedback. Design aligned learning objectives, formative and summative assessments, and authentic performance tasks that support measurable student learning. Design cohesive instructional sequences that progressively develop knowledge and skills while ensuring purposeful activities, appropriate workload, and meaningful opportunities for application. Prepare detailed instructional content and development specifications, maintain instructional ownership, and collaborate with Builders and multimedia professionals to ensure accurate implementation of approved learning experiences. 2. Academic Partnership & Collaboration Partner with Program Chairs, faculty, Subject Matter Experts, and academic leadership to translate academic requirements into effective learning experiences. Serve as an instructional design consultant within assigned academic schools, supporting curriculum alignment, program outcomes, online pedagogy, assessment strategies, and continuous improvement. Participate in Course and Program Reviews (CPRs), academic school meetings, Design Labs, and other collaborative planning initiatives. Collaborate with multimedia professionals and Builders to design, develop, and refine interactive, scenario-based, and immersive learning experiences. Communicate instructional recommendations, project expectations, and development needs clearly and professionally while fostering productive stakeholder relationships. 3. Learning Technology, Artificial Intelligence & Innovation Demonstrate working knowledge of Blackboard Ultra, Articulate Rise 360, SCORM, HTML, and other institutionally approved instructional technologies. Use artificial intelligence responsibly to support instructional planning, content development, assessment design, quality review, and workflow efficiency. Critically evaluate and refine AI-generated content for accuracy, rigor, accessibility, and alignment while adhering to institutional policies for data privacy, intellectual property, and responsible AI use. Design learning experiences that align with the capabilities and limitations of available technologies, ensuring appropriate functionality and usability. Participate in testing, piloting, and evaluating new educational technologies, AI tools, LMS features, and digital learning products, recommending solutions that enhance teaching and learning. 4. Quality Assurance, Accessibility & Continuous Improvement Apply institutional quality assurance standards, instructional design rubrics, and accessibility requirements throughout course development. Review and test instructional content, assessments, multimedia assets, interactive activities, and completed course components for accuracy, alignment, accessibility, and functionality. Participate in peer reviews, quality calibration, and course improvement initiatives, incorporating feedback and verifying that identified instructional issues are resolved. Collaborate with faculty, Builders, multimedia professionals, and other stakeholders to identify and resolve instructional and technical issues. Use quality review findings, course feedback, and available learning data to recommend improvements to instructional experiences and departmental practices. 5. Project Management & Professional Growth Manage multiple concurrent course development projects, meeting established timelines, milestones, and quality expectations. Maintain accurate project documentation, proactively communicate progress and challenges, and coordinate effectively with stakeholders. Participate in departmental meetings, collaborative development processes, and initiatives that improve workflows and team effectiveness. Maintain current knowledge of instructional design, accessibility, learning technologies, artificial intelligence, and emerging practices in higher education. Engage in ongoing professional development, demonstrate adaptability, and contribute to a collaborative, accountable, and innovative team environment. ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Perform other duties as assigned by the Assistant Director of Instructional Design. QUALIFICATIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. The requirements below represent the knowledge, skills, and abilities required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Learning Sciences, Educational Technology, or a related field. Five or more years of experience in online instructional design, course development, or learning experience design. Demonstrated ability to apply instructional design principles, adult learning theory, and performance-focused learning practices. Experience developing online instructional content, learning activities, assessments, and meaningful feedback. Working knowledge of learning management systems and interactive content development tools, including Blackboard Ultra, Articulate Rise 360, SCORM, and basic HTML. Proficiency in using generative AI tools to support instructional design and content development, including critical evaluation of AI-generated materials. Knowledge of accessibility standards, copyright, fair use, intellectual property, and academic integrity considerations. Strong instructional writing, communication, collaboration, organization, and project management skills. Ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment. Demonstrated creativity, adaptability, problem-solving, and commitment to continuous improvement. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Learning Sciences, Educational Technology, or a related field. Higher education teaching experience, preferably in online or adult learning environments. Experience developing or modifying interactive learning experiences using Articulate Rise 360, SCORM, and HTML. Experience designing authentic, scenario-based, interactive, or immersive learning experiences. Experience collaborating with multimedia developers, technical teams, and academic stakeholders. Experience facilitating instructional design consultations, Design Labs, or academic planning initiatives. Familiarity with quality assurance frameworks, peer review processes, and accessibility evaluation. Experience with AI-assisted instructional design workflows and testing or evaluating emerging educational technologies.

jobs.title: Market Data Statistician
jobs.description: The Division of Economic and Risk Analysis (DERA) is seeking early career Statisticians with strong analytical skills and attention to detail. As a Statistician, you will be part of a team that manages and analyzes specialized, high-frequency market microstructure data to support the SEC's rulemaking and oversight mission. DERA emphasizes data and analysis quality, and monitoring advances in the tools available to analyze such data. Qualifications: Applicants are responsible for confirming all required materials are submitted by the closing date of the announcement. Please check the How You Will Be Evaluated and Required Documents sections carefully, as missing documents will render the application incomplete and ineligible for review. Qualifying experience may be obtained in the private or public sector. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualification requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement. BASIC REQUIREMENT: A. Degree: degree that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing. OR B.Combination of education and experience. Courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance. MINIMUM QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENT: In addition to meeting the basic requirement, applicants must also meet the minimum qualification requirement. SK-11: Applicant must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS/SK-9 level: 1. Evaluating economic data for trends, completeness, and accuracy; AND 2. Applying statistical methods and procedures to analyze quantitative data; AND 3. Interpreting statistical results to support studies, surveys, or program decisions. OR Education: Successful completion of a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree, in a field directly related to the position. ACCOMPLISHMENT RECORD COMPETENCIES: Your Accomplishment Record narratives should address the following competencies. See the How You Will Be Evaluated section below for more information: Competency 1: Statistical Expertise - Performs and interprets data analysis. Competency 2: Critical Thinking - Considers a variety of factors, general and subject matter-specific, when making decisions and determining next steps in a case. Competency 3: Technical Communication: Translates technical information into non-technical terms and accurately convey technical information to end users (e.g., staff, management) and outside parties, including the technical documentation of applications, systems, Standard Operating Procedures, etc. Competency 4: Workload Management - Effectively prioritizes workload in a way that accommodates unforeseen developments and achieves successful outcomes.

jobs.description: The Smithsonian Institution is the world's largest museum, education, and research complex, with 21 museums and the National Zoo. jobs.title: Data Scientist (Direct Hire)
jobs.description: This position is being offered under OPM Direct Hire Authority. See more about Direct Hire under Conditions below. Serves as subject matter expert in the specialized area of data sciences and advisor on matters related to the application of mathematics, statistical analysis, modeling/simulation, machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, data and computer sciences and geospatial analysis. See QUALIFICATIONS and EDUCATION for more information about this position. Qualifications: To meet Minimum Qualifications for this Data Scientist position you must demonstrate: (1) the Individual Occupational Requirement (IOR) for the federal 1560 series AND (2) at least 52 weeks of Specialized Experience (1) INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT (IOR) (All Applicants) A. Successful completion of a course of study in an accredited college or university resulting in a degree in one of the following: mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science or field directly related to the position. The degree must be in a major field of study (at least at the baccalaureate level) that is appropriate for the position. OR B. A combination of education and experience that includes successful completion of courses equivalent to a major field of study (30 semester hours) in mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science or a field directly related to the position, plus additional education or appropriate experience. Individual Occupational Requirements must be demonstrated even if you currently hold, or have previously held, a position in this series in the federal government. Transcripts are required to substantiate claimed education SEE EDUCATION BELOW -- Applicants who don't demonstrate these requirements will not be considered. (2) SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE must have been gained in a federal position at or above GS-13 OR (if your position is on another federal pay scale OR outside of federal service) by performing duties at a level of responsibility and difficulty equivalent to GS-13 or above. Specialized Experience is work that primarily consists of: (1) Leading the development and improvement of enterprise data pipelines using SQL and Python; AND (2) Providing guidance on data architecture, data security, and complex data issues; AND (3) Managing the evaluation, integration, and automation of new data sources. If you have this experience, your resume must describe, in your own words, the specific duties you perform that demonstrate it. Reviewers cannot assume you perform duties you don't describe. Since Specialized Experience also has a time component, it must be evident that the duties you describe are at the required level for at least 52 weeks. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS (IOR and Specialized Experience) must be met by the closing date of this announcement. You’ll work non-traditional hours when needed – evening and weekend coverage, whatever it takes to deliver the best-in-class experience.We’re looking for team members who thrive in: High-energy, in-person environments where innovation happens face-to-face Flexible scheduling that follows student needs, not the clock Startup intensity within a world-class university structure We’re not looking for people who want a job. We’re looking for builders who want a mission. The Instructional Design Specialist – Emerging Technologies is responsible for designing and developing high-quality online courses while serving as an internal expert in emerging instructional technologies, artificial intelligence, and UX/UI design. This position plays a dual role, contributing directly to course development and leading the exploration, evaluation, and implementation of innovative digital learning solutions. The Instructional Design Specialist – Emerging Technologies collaborates closely with faculty and cross-functional team members to produce engaging, accessible, and effective learning experiences, while also building institutional capacity through training, documentation, and the development of best practices in emerging technologies. Education and Experience | Master’s degree in Instructional Design, User Experience Design, Education Technology, or a related field. At least 3 years of experience in instructional design. At least 3 years of experience applying UX/UI design and/or AI implementation in a digital learning environment. Hands-on experience with AI tools and applications, including: building or leveraging automations and AI agents to scale content creation, delivery, and evaluating, piloting, and documenting emerging AI tools for instructional use. Experience with HTML for basic formatting and accessibility adjustments within LMS environments. Knowledge of instructional design frameworks and models. Experience with eLearning authoring tools (e.g., Articulate Rise, PlayPosit).Demonstrated experience designing and developing online courses, including building content in a Learning Management System (e.g., Blackboard).Experience applying ADA required accessibility standards, adult learning theories, and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex or technical concepts for non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective professional relationships with faculty, team members, and stakeholders. Skills and Knowledge | Preferred Qualifications: Certification or formal training in UX/UI design. Certification or formal training in AI. Experience developing courses for higher education. Experience in teaching/training. Experience in programming. Responsibilities | Instructional Design & Course Development Facilitate organized, adaptive meetings with faculty to gather information, establish course delivery strategies, and build buy-in for the development process. Define and outline learning objectives, course structure, content delivery methods, assessments, and complementary learning approaches in collaboration with faculty. Articulate and reinforce course development process and clarify faculty responsibilities, as well as establish milestone deadlines, and maintain accountability throughout the project lifecycle. Utilize eLearning authoring tools to design interactive, engaging learning experiences. Build and update courses in the LMS, ensuring content meets accessibility requirements. Lead and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including video production team, and multimedia design team to produce draft and final versions of course material. Collaborate closely with faculty and stakeholders to develop course content; maintain strong professional relationships and clear communication throughout the project lifecycle. Track and report the statuses of courses throughout the development process. Manage courses independently with continued support from the development team. Emerging Technology & Innovation Serve as an internal subject matter expert on UX/UI, AI implementation, and emerging instructional technologies; translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and leadership. Research, evaluate, and implement emerging technologies, including Generative AI, in instructional design and content development; document best practices and contribute to institutional innovation strategy. Explore and integrate innovative digital learning solutions into course and program development. Design AI-driven workflows and automation strategies to improve efficiency in content production, iteration, and delivery at scale. Training & Professional Development Provide training sessions, workshops, and resources for instructional designers and related staff to build capacity in UX/UI, AI, and emerging technologies. Other duties as assigned. jobs.title: Research and Learning Scientist
jobs.description: Research and Learning Scientist 12 Research - United States (Remote) About TalkingPoints TalkingPoints is an award-winning education technology nonprofit on a mission to unlock every student’s potential by activating one of the most underutilized forces in education - families. We believe that when families and schools work together, students thrive - and we’re building the tools to make that partnership possible for every family. Our platform helps schools reach and engage every family - including those historically underserved - through accessible, two-way communication in 150+ languages, along with data, insights, and supports that strengthen relationships and drive student success. Today, millions of educators and families are using TalkingPoints in their classrooms, schools, and districts across the U.S. to build stronger partnerships and improve outcomes for students. Our work is grounded in research and has been shown to meaningfully impact attendance, learning, and more. We partner with leading school districts nationwide and are supported by a strong community of philanthropic and strategic partners, including major foundations, technology leaders, and education organizations. TalkingPoints is at an exciting stage of growth and impact. As we continue to expand our reach and deepen our impact, we’re looking for passionate, mission-driven team members who want to help schools and families succeed - together. Learn more at www.talkingpts.org . The Opportunity The Research and Learning Scientist drives rigorous, actionable research on how TalkingPoints improves student outcomes through family-school partnerships. They support R&D for our family learning products, making sure the home practices we promote match how children build literacy and numeracy skills. They also contribute to studies across our broader research agenda. Reporting to the Director of Research, they own projects from design to dissemination and work cross-functionally on a team that values rigor and rapid iteration. You will: Drive research for our at-home learning and personalized recommendation products, and contribute to studies across the research agenda Support product R&D by applying learning science and behavior-change principles and testing whether features strengthen family practices and student learning Advise on AI-powered family recommendations, including which data signals to use, how they map to skills, where data is too thin to personalize, and how good the outputs are Design and run mixed methods studies from rapid-cycle, descriptive, and correlational analyses to quasi-experimental designs and randomized trials Manage, clean, and analyze quantitative and qualitative platform, partner, and public data (e.g., NCES, state systems) Develop and administer measures of family and educator outcomes linked to student outcomes Turn findings into impact stories and strategic recommendations for product, partnerships, and fundraising Represent our research with districts, funders, and external researchers, lead long-term district research partnerships, and informally mentor other researchers as needed Who You Are Required PhD in education, learning sciences, developmental or educational psychology, or a related field 8+ years of applied research experience, including product, R&D, and funder-facing work Learning science expertise in literacy and/or math, home learning, and families as learning partners Expertise in mixed methods, experimental and quasi-experimental design, and measure validation, with honest communication of tradeoffs A record of translating evidence for non-research audiences and delivering with little oversight Proficiency in R, working knowledge of SQL and/or Sigma, comfort using AI tools, and experience with public education datasets and PII Nice to Haves Family engagement or attendance research expertise Evaluating AI-powered or personalized recommendation tools Overall fit with our org culture - we look for team members who are: User and Mission-Oriented: we are devoted to our mission with empathy towards the communities we serve. jobs.description:
About Amplify

Description:

The Revenue Systems Analyst is the connective tissue between Revenue Systems, the overall Revenue Operations team, and the Business Systems team. This role leads structured process discovery, maps current and future state workflows, and translates operational needs into clear, testable requirements for Business Systems and other partners, with a focus on business clarity rather than system configuration. The focus of the Revenue Systems team is improving seller and sales-operations execution across lead-to-cash (quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, renewals/amendments), reducing rework, strengthening data integrity, sales finance/ budgeting, and accelerating change adoption.

This role also supports the strategy, administration, and adoption of the platforms that power revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform. Success in this role depends less on producing documents than on the human work behind them, building trust with business partners, asking the questions that surface what people actually do versus what the process says they do, and driving decisions across teams that don't always agree. This is not a system administration or configuration role.



Essential Responsibilities:



Business Process Discovery and Design

 - Facilitate workshops and working sessions with key stakeholders (Account Executives, District Managers, Sales Support, Renewals, Sales Finance, and Business Systems) to document current state end-to-end business processes and define improved future state designs facilitated by systems and process improvements.

 - Create clear, multi-level process maps (e.g., lead-to-quote, quote-to-contract, order-to-cash, renewals/amendments) that reflect real seller and operations workflows, handoffs, approvals, and exception paths.

 - Establish and maintain a lightweight process library (maps, SOPs, definitions, decision trees) so institutional knowledge is durable and scalable.

Requirements and Solution Definition (Sales and Sales Operations Lens)

 - Translate process and policy decisions into well-structured requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules, and operational scenarios - ensuring clarity, completeness, and testability.

 - Partner with Business Systems to validate feasibility, clarify ambiguities, and ensure requirements reflect both the operational intent and system constraints.

 - Maintain traceability from process maps -> requirements -> test cases -> release notes to reduce rework and ensure end-to-end quality.

 - Use AI-powered tools (e.g., Glean, Claude, Gemini) to accelerate drafting of user stories, business cases, acceptance criteria, process documentation, and stakeholder synthesis — applying judgment to validate accuracy, completeness, and business fit rather than accepting output at face value.

Tools Strategy and Administration

 - Support the administration and strategy development of the platforms supporting revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform, assisting in configuration, user access, adoption tracking, and vendor coordination.

 - Translate market intelligence signals into usable seller and sales-operations workflows, partnering with Business Systems on data flow, attribution, and reporting integration.

 - Build and maintain enablement resources (playbooks, prompt libraries, use case guides) that drive consistent, high-value usage across the field.

 - Evaluate, pilot, and operationalize additional platforms as needed, including AI-enabled solutions, and make recommendations on fit, sequencing, and expansion.

Operational Readiness, Testing, and Change Enablement

 - Co-design UAT approaches and test scenarios rooted in real-world seller and Sales Operations use cases; coordinate execution with Business Systems and key business testers.

 - Develop end-user documentation (job aids, playbooks, process guides) and support enablement activities to drive adoption and consistent execution.

 - Support release readiness by confirming training, communications, reporting impacts, and operational 'go-live' checklists are complete.

Continuous Improvement and Performance Insights

 - Use operational data and qualitative feedback to identify friction points, bottlenecks, policy leakage, and process variability - and recommend improvements.

 - Support defining process KPIs (cycle time, rework/defect rates, adoption, SLA attainment) and partner with reporting teams to surface actionable insights.

 - Promote standardization and simplification while preserving necessary state/district/contracting complexity through clear guardrails and exception handling.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions that can simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Governance

 - Act as a neutral facilitator to align Sales, Finance, and Business Systems on process decisions, definitions, and sequencing - especially in quoting, contracting, ordering, and invoicing workflows.

 - Support governance routines (change intake, prioritization, documentation standards, decision logs) to keep cross-functional work moving and reduce 'spin.'

 - Contribute to program initiatives across the revenue systems roadmap (e.g., quoting modernization, amendments/contracting improvements, data governance, commission and budget operationalization, seller enablement).

Minimum Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, or related field (or equivalent experience).

 - 4+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Process Analysis, or related roles focused on process design and operational improvement.

 - Demonstrated ability to create process maps and documentation that non-technical audiences can follow (e.g., Lucidchart, Visio, Miro, or similar).

 - Experience translating business needs into clear requirements (user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules) and supporting cross-functional delivery.

 - Experience working with CRM and revenue operations platforms (Salesforce preferred) and familiarity with lead-to-cash processes including quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, and renewals.

 - Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and written communication skills; comfortable driving alignment across teams with competing priorities.

 - Analytical mindset and comfort using data to diagnose issues and validate improvements.

 - Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies, methodologies, and ways of working, including the use of AI-powered tools to improve productivity, process design, analysis, documentation, and decision-making.



Travel required (about 10-15%).



Preferred Qualifications:

 - Experience in K-12 education, EdTech, or other subscription/SaaS environments with complex contracting and renewal processes.

 - Experience with CRMs and Quoting automation and contract/amendment workflows (e.g., Salesforce CPQ / Revenue Cloud/ or similar) from an operational design perspective.

 - Lean / Six Sigma (Green Belt or higher), PMP, or comparable process improvement training.

 - Familiarity with Agile delivery practices, backlog hygiene, and tools like Jira/Confluence (or equivalent).

 - Experience building playbooks/SOPs and partnering with enablement teams to drive adoption in the field.

jobs.description: Summary About the Team and the Program The Pathway Gap Data and Systems Coordinator works within the Department of Community Engagement and Postsecondary Pathways (CEPP) at New Visions for Public Schools. Our vision is that every young person in New York City can clearly see, navigate, and access best-fit career pathways, supported by shared civic infrastructure that helps the adults advising them guide the way. Reporting to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap, the Data Coordinator plays a key role in the success of the Pathway Gap Initiative —a cross-sector collaboration of more than 75 organizations designed to address the systemic challenges that make it difficult for youth-serving professionals to connect young people to postsecondary and workforce opportunities. For more information on the Pathway Gap project, please see this project overview . About the Role The role owns the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of the program data that powers the New Visions Career Directory. The main focus for the first two years of the role is launching the project’s new Training Dates solution—a not-yet-built system for surfacing real-time training program dates and application deadlines, and ensuring young people have an actionable next step. Because the Training Dates solution is a new effort, this role will be central to its earliest stages: Piloting the data collection process with a small initial cohort of training providers (~30 programs) Identifying and troubleshooting issues as they arise Helping shape what it takes to scale the approach in future phases Working closely with the Associate Director of Pathway Gap to liaise with the technology team, translating pilot learnings into clear design requirements Beyond the pilot, you'll work directly with workforce training providers to collect, verify, and maintain program information—building the kind of trusted relationships that keep data accurate as programs evolve. This role is a great fit if you enjoy direct outreach to external partners, research, and data quality work; are comfortable with ambiguity; enjoy problem-solving in a developing system; can bring structure and rigor to a new process; and want your day-to-day work to translate into real opportunities for young people across New York City. Core Responsibilities 1. Training Dates Solution: Pilot & Scaling Pilot Cohort Coordination: Serve as the primary point of contact for the initial pilot cohort of organizations, representing approximately 30 programs, guiding them through the new data submission process to guarantee data completeness, clarifying data requirements, and ensuring clear communication around the strategic goals of this initiative. Process Troubleshooting & User Testing: Identify friction points, data gaps, and breakdowns in the data collection process as they emerge—troubleshooting issues directly with providers and flagging systemic problems to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap and technology team. Participate in user acceptance testing for product features before and after launch to curate and elevate feedback and concerns. Scaling Refinement: Contribute pilot-informed recommendations on what's needed to refine and scale the solution beyond the initial cohort, based on provider and user pain points, inclusive of process and workflow changes, automation and process optimization opportunities, collection of additional data points central to the initiative, and continuous improvement ahead of subsequent rollouts. Help the team identify opportunities for greater efficiency and consistency as the number of participating programs grows, and use feedback to inform reporting to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap and funders. 2. Directory & Systems Maintenance Career Directory Content Maintenance and Verification Audits: Update program information directly within the Career Directory's content management system, ensuring listings are current, properly formatted, and reflect the most recent verified data. Conduct scheduled audits of existing program listings to confirm that programs are still active, accurately, described, and correctly categorized. Identify and resolve inconsistencies, outdated information, or gaps in program data, applying close attention to detail to maintain a high bar for accuracy across the Directory. Data Outreach: Proactively reach out to providers via phone and email to request updated information, clarify details, and follow up on outstanding data needs, balancing persistence with professionalism. Respond to provider questions and concerns about how their program information appears in the Directory, as well as Directory data standards, and escalate more complex issues to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap as needed. New Program Sourcing and Research: Research and source information for new training programs to be added to the Career Directory, ensuring all required fields are complete, accurate, and consistent with established data standards. 3. Relationship Management Partner Engagement: Build and maintain strong, trusted working relationships with workforce training providers, serving as solutions-oriented point of contact for data collection and program updates. Feedback Loops: Solicit ongoing feedback from training providers about the data collection process itself—identifying friction points, unclear requirements, or process improvements that would make it easier for providers to keep their information current. Relay provider feedback to the Pathway Gap and technology teams to inform future tool and process improvements. Cross-Team Coordination: Coordinate with the broader Pathway Gap and technology teams to relay provider feedback that may inform future improvements to data collection tools and processes. Committee mobilization: Partner with the project lead to manage the operations of the cross-organizational Quality and Standards Committee, including leading relevant monthly subcommittees, and supporting the planning and execution of three annual in-person convenings. Qualifications Required Education and Experience Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent blending of academic and applied experience. Professional Experience: 2-4 years of experience in operations, program support, content management, or a related field. Data Collection + Quality Assurance Experience : Demonstrated experience compiling and maintaining accurate, well-organized data sets, including spotting inconsistencies and resolving discrepancies. External Communication: Experience conducting outreach and communicating with external partners or providers via phone and email to gather or verify information. Familiarity with the NYC workforce development ecosystem , including training providers, career pathways programs, and the types of credentials and outcomes they offer, strongly preferred. Required Knowledge and Skills Strong attention to detail, with the ability to verify information against source materials and maintain high data accuracy across a large, frequently changing data set. A friendly, persistent, solutions-oriented approach to building and sustaining relationships with both new and known external partners. Ability to listen actively, ask clarifying questions, follow through independently, and know when to escalate. Comfort with ambiguity and shifting practices: energized rather than thrown off by the early-stage nature of a new initiative, with ability to bring structure and patience to shifting operational workflows and still-developing processes to and help shape what scaling should look like. Comfort working alongside a technology team and contributing stakeholder perspective to product development processes; proficiency with standard productivity and data tools. (e.g., Google Workspace, spreadsheet); experience with content management systems or databases to organize and track information preferred. Physical requirements Ability to traverse an office environment to attend meetings and interact with colleagues Ability to operate a computer and other relevant technology, such as phones, screens, printers, and tablets Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, as is common in office settings Ability to communicate and exchange accurate information with internal and external stakeholders Ability to travel to partner organizations across the 5 boroughs on a periodic basis Ability to carry up to 10 pounds (such as for a laptop and carrying case) Candidates must be able to perform the essential functions of this role with or without reasonable accommodation. jobs.description: About Overdeck Family Foundation Overdeck Family Foundation (“the Foundation”) was founded in 2011 to provide all children the opportunity to unlock their potential. The Foundation focuses on enhancing education through funding efforts in early childhood, hands-on STEM education, and K-9 programs, supporting both educators and student-centered learning environments. Our grantmaking and strategic support focus on unlocking innovation, evidence, and growth opportunities to accelerate key academic and socioemotional outcomes for all children. At Overdeck Family Foundation, we achieve our impact by collaborating with rigor, fostering a culture of curiosity and learning, and living our core values to drive meaningful change. Visit www.overdeck.org for more information on our foundation, including our research repository . The Research Fellow Position Overdeck Family Foundation is seeking a Research Fellow to work with the Research & Impact Officer, Meghan McCormick, to support the Foundation’s evidence and research efforts. This role will contribute to activities including evidence reviews for prospective grantees, evidence summaries for funding recommendations, and targeted communication activities such as updating summaries of research funded by the Foundation. The position is ideally suited for advanced doctoral students or post-doctoral researchers in economics, public policy, sociology, applied psychology, or education, particularly those with expertise in econometrics and K-12 education. Develop evidence summaries to support funding recommendations and presentations. Collaborate on updating and maintaining a repository of research studies funded by the Foundation. You are motivated by the Foundation’s mission to open doors for every child in the U.S. by measurably enhancing education both inside and outside the classroom. You bring expertise in quantitative research . You have advanced training in research methodology (ex: experimental and quasi-experimental designs), knowledge of the federal ESSA evidence tiers, and experience conducting independent research. You communicate effectively . Your ability to synthesize and clearly present complex research findings ensures your work drives understanding and decision-making. You are independent and proactive . You excel at managing your tasks and producing high-quality outputs with minimal supervision. You value collaboration . You’re a team player, open to feedback, and eager to work with internal colleagues to enhance the Foundation’s learning and impact. jobs.description: Advocates For Children (AFC) is a dynamic social justice organization that strives to ensure a high-quality education for New York students who face barriers to academic success, focusing on students from low-income backgrounds. AFC works on behalf of children and youth who are at greatest risk of academic failure due to poverty, race, ethnicity, disability, homelessness, immigration status/limited English proficiency, or involvement in the child welfare or juvenile/criminal legal systems. We use uniquely integrated strategies to advance systemic reform, empower families and communities, and advocate for the educational rights of individual students. AFC grounds our work in our organization’s values: Family-Centered: We listen to what families want for their children and empower them with information and support. Expertise: W e ground our advocacy in more than 50 years of experience with the NYC public schools and deep knowledge of the legal and education systems affecting the students and families we serve. Passion: We are united by our unrelenting drive to dismantle obstacles to education and our unwavering dedication to NYC’s students and families. Community: We foster collaboration and inclusive practices within our team and with outside partners so we can learn from different perspectives and unite in advancing our common goals. Justice: We view the law as a powerful tool to bridge gaps in access to education and help families from under-represented communities fight for their rights. Impact: We recognize that our value lies in the difference we make in the lives of students and their families and push ourselves to achieve concrete results. For more information on AFC, see www.advocatesforchildren.org . JOB SUMMARY AFC seeks an Education Advocate in our Immigrant Students' Rights Project (ISRP). ISRP works to protect the education-related rights of underserved immigrant families. Immigrant families face unique obstacles in NYC public schools related to their linguistic and cultural backgrounds. We are looking for an advocate to join our team to serve immigrant families of children with disabilities and English Language Learners (ELLs). The Education Advocate will report directly to ISRP's Project Director. PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Assisting families with school related issues such as special education, school enrollment, bilingual programs, and bullying. Conducting intakes of new clients. Participating in school meetings and school visits. Providing know-your-rights trainings to families across New York City and staffing tables at information fairs. Locating and connecting families with resources in their communities. Drafting and updating informational materials for immigrant parents. Supporting ISRP policy advocacy efforts as needed. QUALIFICATIONS Understanding of and alignment with AFC’s mission. Please review AFC’s work at www.advocatesforchildren.org . Desire to learn, both as an individual and as part of an organization, and apply diversity, equity, inclusion, and anti-racism principles. A bachelor's degree. Fluency in Spanish. Organized, detail oriented, and able to work independently on tasks and deliverables . Experience working with families is preferred. Strong presentation skills and comfort with public speaking. Strong writing ability and analytical skills. Ability to explain complex concepts in a manner that is easy to understand. Ability to multi-task and respond to changing needs. Available to work occasional evenings and weekends and to travel within the five boroughs. Proficient in Microsoft Office programs: Word, Outlook, SharePoint . APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Candidates should submit a resume and cover letter highlighting why they are interested in this role at AFC and how their experience aligns with the Education Advocate position, including any personal or profession al experience that demonstrates your connection to the populations that AFC serves. The position is available starting in August 2026, and resumes will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Due to the high volume of applicants, only qualified candidates will be contacted. COMPENSATION This is a full-time position, with a salary in the range of $63,702 - $69,323, depending on experience, and includes a comprehensive benefits package. This position is expected to work at least 2 days a week in the office and remotely on the remaining days. ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION INFORMATION AFC’s current compensation package includes medical and dental insurance, with a plan option that covers full payment of medical plan premiums for staff and their qualified dependents . AFC has generous time-off policies that include 10 federal holidays, office closure between Christmas and New Year’s Day, and 15 vacation days and 15 paid time off days in the first year of employment . AFC also offers a 403(b) plan with a fully vested employer match and coverage of the premium cost of life insurance and short-term and long-term disability insurance. AFC is an equal opportunity employer that actively seeks to recruit and retain a diverse staff and encourages all applications including from people of color, persons with disabilities, parents of persons with disabilities, persons of diverse sexual orientations, gender identities or gender expressions and persons of diverse socioeconomic backgrounds. AFC is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability or other protected characteristic. The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment, including the application process. For more information and to request an accommodation, contact Human Resources at HR@advocatesforchildren.org .

jobs.title: Anthropic Fellows Program, The Anthropic Institute (Economics & Policy)
jobs.location: London, UK; Ontario, CAN; Remote-Friendly, United States; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. Anthropic Fellows Program overview The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience. Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis. Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you. What to expect 4 months of full-time research Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country) Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses Interview process The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Compensation The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension). The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy) Mentors, research areas, & past projects Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include: Economics Maxim Massenkoff Peter McCrory Policy, Security, and Society Jack Clark Marina Favaro Jim Baker Projects in this workstream may include: Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement For past project examples, see: How AI Impacts Skill Formation : Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models : Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus Unique candidate criteria You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you: Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required Are adaptable and collaborative, able to take direction and contribute to team priorities rather than needing to pursue a predetermined research agenda Are skilled at writing up and communicating your results, even when they're null or unexpected Are passionate about translating research insights into actionable recommendations for improving AI systems and informing policy You may be a good fit if you: Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole Are excited to transition into AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic Strong track record of empirical research Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly Candidates must be: Fluent in Python programming Available to work full-time on the Fellows program Logistics - Fellows Program Submit your application to the Anthropic Institute Fellows at the bottom of this page. Logistics Requirements: To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program. Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in SF. We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada . Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada. Program Duration: The program runs for 4 months, full-time. If you can't commit to the full duration, please still apply and note your constraints in the application. We review these requests on a case-by-case basis. The below are Anthropic's policies for full time roles. These do NOT apply to the Fellows Program. Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. What you learn at one site - what worked, what slipped, what should become standard - becomes the playbook for the next wave. If you have delivered data center hardware at scale, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic’s Data Center team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and vendors to stand up facilities that can reliably cool some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry. As a Senior Data Center Mechanical Engineer based in the United States, you’ll lead the design direction and technical oversight of building mechanical systems — cooling, chilled-water distribution, liquid cooling, plumbing, and fire protection — across our rapidly expanding U.S. portfolio. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on driving and reviewing mechanical design from concept through detailed design and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms and development partners, ensuring every facility meets Anthropic’s standards for reliability, efficiency, and scalability. You’ll own the mechanical design direction from Basis of Design through construction and commissioning, serving as the primary technical interface between Anthropic’s internal teams and our external engineering and development partners. A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication and modular construction — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture that compress schedules and reduce onsite labor. You’ll bring deep familiarity with U.S. mechanical, plumbing, and fire codes and the local regulatory environment, and ensure the cooling architecture keeps pace with rapidly increasing rack densities and the shift toward direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Strong candidates will bring deep mission-critical mechanical design experience and the judgment to make sound trade-offs when the standard playbook doesn’t apply. Responsibilities Design direction & review Drive mechanical design concepts for data center cooling plants, chilled-water distribution, liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and CDUs), plumbing, and fire protection systems. Review and direct design drawings, specifications, and construction documentation produced by external engineering firms, ensuring alignment with Anthropic’s Basis of Design and owner requirements. Evaluate design submittals, shop drawings, and equipment selections; respond to RFIs with clear technical direction. Identify design conflicts and drive resolution across mechanical, electrical, and controls disciplines. Maintain and evolve Anthropic’s internal mechanical design standards and reference configurations. Prefabrication & modular delivery Drive Anthropic’s prefabricated and modular mechanical strategy — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping and pump assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture and onsite assembly — to accelerate deployment and reduce onsite labor. Drive standardization of modular mechanical designs across sites while preserving flexibility for site-specific constraints and evolving hardware generations. External partner & vendor coordination Serve as the primary mechanical engineering point of contact for external developers, design engineers, and construction partners across the U.S. portfolio. Develop scopes of work, equipment specifications, and bid packages for mechanical infrastructure. Perform technical due diligence on third-party and colocation facilities, evaluating mechanical designs against program requirements and redundancy targets. Coordinate with equipment vendors and manufacturers on cooling system procurement, including chillers, CDUs, pumps, and piping assemblies, and partner with supply chain to mitigate lead-time and single-source risk. Construction & commissioning Monitor mechanical system installation for compliance with design intent, applicable U.S. codes and standards, and industry best practice. Conduct site visits to review progress, resolve field issues, and validate construction quality; travel to sites across the region as needed. Support testing and commissioning of mechanical systems; analyze data and troubleshoot issues against design intent. You may be a good fit if you Have 10+ years of experience designing building mechanical systems for data centers or mission-critical facilities, across the project lifecycle from concept design through construction, commissioning, and handover. Have deep familiarity with U.S. mechanical, plumbing, and fire codes and standards — including the International Mechanical Code (IMC), International Plumbing Code (IPC), International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), International Building Code (IBC), NFPA 13 (automatic sprinkler systems), ASME B31 piping codes, and applicable state and local amendments, alongside ASHRAE guidance (incl. TC 9.9). Have strong knowledge of chilled-water systems, air-cooled cooling plants, liquid cooling (direct-to-chip and CDUs), and redundant piping configurations. Have hands-on experience with prefabricated and modular mechanical infrastructure — modular cooling skids, prefabricated piping assemblies, and design for offsite manufacture. Have experience driving and reviewing mechanical design work produced by external engineering consultants, and are proficient reading and marking up construction drawings, P&IDs, and single-line diagrams. Hold a bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering; a Professional Engineer (PE) license (or eligibility) is valued but not required. Communicate clearly and can drive technical decisions across internal teams and external partners, and are results-oriented with a bias toward practical solutions. Are able to travel up to ~30% to data center sites across the region. Strong candidates may also have 15+ years of experience designing building mechanical systems for data centers or mission-critical facilities. Direct project experience delivering data centers in multiple U.S. markets (e.g., Virginia, Ohio, Texas, Arizona, Oregon). Experience with thermal-hydraulic modeling software (AFT Fathom, Cadence 6SigmaET, ANSYS, or similar), CFD modeling, and energy analysis. Familiarity with controls/BAS systems and sequences of operation for cooling plants. Experience preparing SOWs, facility audits, and TCO analyses. A track record building modular prefabricated products in mechanical or electrical areas of the data center, and driving designs toward offsite manufacturing. Proficiency with Revit MEP or AutoCAD MEP. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI). As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is. This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness. What You'll Do Delivery planning and schedule integration Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule. Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut. Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths. Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio — a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating. Supplier execution and escalation Run weekly delivery cadences with OEMs and integrators on open orders; verify production progress against committed slots rather than accepting reported dates at face value. Act as the primary escalation point for factory slips, component shortages, FAT failures, and shipping delays; drive recovery plans (expedites, partial ships, resequencing, alternate sources) with Sourcing and Engineering. Partner with Sourcing on corporate-level supplier escalations, bringing site-level schedule intelligence to commercial conversations. Hold GC OFCI teams accountable for receiving, storage, and installation-readiness performance; manage the change/claim process when delivery issues affect the GC's schedule. Logistics and site readiness Plan and coordinate transportation for oversize/overweight and high-value equipment — carrier selection, route surveys, permits, crane and rigging coordination — with our logistics partners and the GC. Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements. Ensure equipment arrives complete — accessories, spares, documentation, and vendor startup support scheduled — so installation and commissioning are not delayed by missing pieces. Risk management and reporting Identify, triage, and report delivery risks across the portfolio; propose solutions and drive decisions to protect capacity milestones. Establish and lead recurring Capacity Delivery Reviews giving leadership converged visibility into OFE delivery status and risk by site and by equipment category. Track delivery KPIs — on-time-to-ROS, schedule drift by supplier and category, escalation cycle time, expedite spend — and use them to surface systemic issues. Feed lessons learned back into Sourcing (lead-time assumptions, contract delivery terms, buffer strategy) and Construction (ROS sequencing) to improve the next program. Who You Are 8–12+ years in supply chain delivery, equipment expediting, construction management, or infrastructure program management on large-scale, schedule-driven construction programs. Hands-on experience delivering power and/or cooling equipment for mission-critical facilities — transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS, busway, chillers, CDUs, air handlers — and familiarity with how those OEMs actually build and ship. You've managed cross-functional escalations across construction teams, suppliers, and internal partners, and you know when to expedite, when to resequence, and when to escalate commercially. Comfortable reading and influencing construction schedules (P6 or MS Project) and tying equipment milestones to them. Strong written and verbal communication — you can turn a messy delivery problem into a one-page recommendation for leadership. Data-fluent: you build and maintain trackers and dashboards, and you'd rather look at the numbers than trust a status email. Thrive with high autonomy in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment; you own outcomes, not just updates. Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Experience supporting multiple concurrent projects (5–10+) across a regional portfolio. Working knowledge of FAT/SAT and commissioning workflows and how equipment documentation gates them. Heavy-haul / project logistics experience, including international freight, customs, and Incoterms. Technical understanding of data center electrical distribution and cooling system design.
