jobs.title: Healthy Aging Program Coordinator, Bureau of Equitable Health Systems
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity and Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems (BEHS) is the health care systems bureau of DOHMH. Our mission is to apply policy, evidence, and practical expertise to improve equity in health care delivery at the individual, organizational and systems levels. The Health Care Access & Policy (HCAP) Office within BEHS drives policy, programming, and research that maximizes health insurance coverage and increases access to a fordable high quality, and coordinated primary care with a strong focus on health equity. HCAP has dedicated staff working to improve access to quality, culturally appropriate primary care for New Yorkers, particularly those who are at risk for poor health outcome, by ensuring that on-the ground programmatic work, policy, and data activities inform one another. Within HCAP sits the Healthy Aging Unit, a program that builds support for older adults and their caregivers and strengthens the NYC Health Department's ability to monitor and respond to the health needs of older adults. The unit offers an exciting, unique opportunity for a public health professional with an interest in disease prevention, healthcare policy, health insurance (Medicare/Medicaid), and research.   The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems seeks to hire a Healthy Aging Program Coordinator who must be able to effectively manage initiatives and multiple projects simultaneously in supporting the Bureau's mission.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Contribute to strategizing, developing, implementing, and evaluating program initiatives that help support the health of older adults and address intersectional inequities.  - Assist in research and quantitative data analysis on public health initiatives including health insurance and including reviewing relevant literature.  - Disseminate information and serve as liaison between the Healthy Aging Unit and other agency programs and assist with troubleshooting.  - Coordinate with other city agencies to align priorities related to Healthy Aging.  - Collaborate with policy-focused staff across the agency to analyze and interpret aging-related policies and policies related to health insurance for older adults.  - Coordinate communication efforts to internal and external partners.  - Prepare reports, as appropriate.  - Conduct background research and prepare proposals for new programs.  - Maintain up-to-date knowledge base on relevant policy issues including public health insurance programs, health reform and transformation initiatives impacting primary care and health insurance coverage and healthy aging.  - Assist in planning, coordinating, and evaluating educational events, community outreach activities, and Healthy Aging initiatives.  - Maintain and update Healthy Aging contact lists, partner networks, and program resources.  - Identify and coordinate community outreach opportunities and events to support NYC Health Department engagement with older adults. jobs.title: Manager for Translational Epidemiology, World Trade Center Health Registry
jobs.description: The World Trade Center Health Registry (WTCHR) was created in 2002 to monitor and evaluate the physical and mental health impact on more than 71,000 persons exposed to the September 11, 2001 disaster. Housed within the Center for Population Health Data Science in a renowned and dynamic agency, WTCHR research influences national policies concerning healthcare for those who survived the attacks and contributes novel epidemiologic findings to the post-disaster public health literature. Reporting to the Director of Research, you will be serving as the manager for a newly established sub-unit devoted to Translational Epidemiology. As manager for the Translational Epidemiology sub-unit, you will oversee and improve effectiveness and reach of our Treatment Referral Program, design and integrate multi-source data pipelines for detection of 9/11-related emerging conditions, and serve as a resource for advanced predictive analytics. jobs.title: Naloxone Informatics Specialist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  The Overdose Education and Naloxone Distribution Unit (OENDU) develops, implements, and evaluates initiatives to reduce and prevent opioid overdose deaths in New York City. The Unit provides naloxone, training, and technical assistance to over 350 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs) across New York City. OOPPs provide community-based overdose prevention, recognition, and response education and distribute naloxone directly to community members. OENDU solicits data from these OOPPs to evaluate their naloxone dispensing. DOHMH has its own OOPP and provides in-person and virtual overdose prevention training and naloxone via mail-based distribution. In addition, OENDU provides contract management, fiscal, technical, and programmatic support to at least 27 contracted OOPPs for strategic naloxone distribution and 4 contracted OOPPs for the implementation and management of 8 Public Health Vending Machines.   Position Summary:    The Naloxone Informatics Specialist will support the Overdose Prevention Unit by supporting the submission of accurate and timely naloxone distribution data, with the goal of preventing overdose deaths in New York City.  Under general direction from the Naloxone Data Coordinator, with wide latitude for independent judgment and initiative, the Naloxone Informatics Specialist will:  Job Duties and Responsibilities:    •	Collaborate with colleagues in OENDU and the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) to gather and analyze data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution in NYC  •	Use Microsoft Access and/or R studio to clean and maintain data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC  •	Generate PowerBI dashboards and data tables to support the ongoing evaluation of naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC.  •	Solicit monthly naloxone distribution reports from over 190 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs); follow up with OOPPs who do not submit timely reports and provide technical assistance as needed  •	Train newly registered OOPPs to submit individual-level dispensing data through the Naloxone Dispensing Form (NDF); support OOPPs as they integrate form submission into their workflows; monitor form submission and provide support to OOPPs to increase their response rate.   •	Manage timely entry of monthly distribution reports into database; reconcile naloxone fulfillment with monthly data; manage timely preparation of report materials for data processing  •	Develop and refine surveys, RedCap forms, and other dispensing data collection forms as needed.  •	Collaborate with NYS Department of Health AIDS Institute, the Overdose Prevention Coordinator, the Naloxone Inventory Coordinator, and other BADUPCT staff to maintain registration and contact information for all OOPPs  •	Provide timely response to requests for naloxone fulfillment and dispensing data, naloxone reversals and other relevant information  •	Refine systems, as needed, for tracking naloxone dispensing data   •	Support Naloxone Inventory Coordinator in the packaging of naloxone kits  •	Participate in Overdose Prevention Unit meetings, including facilitation on a rotating basis; provide administrative support to the Overdose Prevention Unit including scheduling meetings, developing agendas, and other tasks as needed.  •	Participate in agency-wide activities for advancing racial, gender, and social equity.  •	Other duties or tasks may be assigned on an as-needed basis  Preferred Skills:   •	Knowledge of substance use issues and harm reduction practice and theory, including syringe exchange, overdose prevention and education for HIV and Hepatitis C prevention. •	Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. •	Ability to work independently and as part of a team. jobs.title: One Health Analyst, Bureau of Communicable Diseases
jobs.description: The Bureau of Communicable Diseases (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory, zoonotic and vector-borne diseases. You will assist the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit and the One Health team by providing dedicated analytical support to monitor and control multi drug resistant organisms in humans and animals in New York City. Within BCD, the Antimicrobial Resistance Unit (ARU) aims to 1) conduct surveillance for and facilitate rapid response to high-priority multidrug-resistant organisms, 2) undertake epidemiologic research on the transmission of these organisms in the community, and 3) promote judicious antibiotic prescribing practices and infection prevention efforts by disseminating resources to NYC stakeholders, including data on local antibiotic use and resistance trends. The ARU is comprised of three teams: the Surveillance and Data team, the Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) and Antimicrobial Stewardship (AS) team, and the One Health team. The goals of the One Health team are to understand and control the spread of multidrug-resistant organisms in humans, animals, and our shared environment.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Under the supervision of the One Health team lead, this analyst will provide data support for both the One Health team specifically as well as the ARU more broadly. Their duties will include, but are not limited to:  • Building, maintaining, and strengthening surveillance of antimicrobial resistance and antimicrobial use data from humans and animals.  • Supporting IPC and AS for veterinary professionals including creating new and innovative resources. • Providing analytical support for whole genome sequencing (WGS) initiatives, including: o Coordinating with epidemiology, laboratory, informatics, and information technology teams to ensure proper transmission of WGS data.  o Developing and maintaining routine reports to analyze and share WGS data. • Providing analytical support for ARU projects including:  o Surveillance of carbapenem-resistant organisms (CRO) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in New York City and detection of community-associated transmission  o Core ARU duties and data needs such as CRO case investigations, routine data cleaning, quality assurance activities, etc. • Supporting project management needs based on data analytics.  • Presenting results of data analyses to internal and external stakeholders.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Proficiency in Statistical Analysis Software (SAS), R, SQL, and/or REDCap • Proficiency in navigating computer systems; ability to learn new data systems quickly; and ability to comply with data integrity and security safeguards for personal identifiable information • Experience and training in public health, one health, and/or antimicrobial resistance • Excellent interpersonal skills including the ability to interact professionally with people from diverse cultural, racial, ethnic, gender, and socioeconomic backgrounds • A positive attitude and strong work ethic • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, critical thinking ability, and sound judgment • Ability to speak, read, and write in English • Must be a NYC resident or become one within 90 days of hire  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Policy Manager, Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Development Disabilities
jobs.description: The Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Developmental Disabilities (CYF-DD) is responsible for planning and monitoring much of NYC's comprehensive network of child and adolescent community mental health services. Grounded in a commitment to equity, the CYF-DD's mission is to promote the mental health of all children, youth and families and to empower individuals with developmental disabilities to lead integrated and fulfilling lives. To achieve this, we work to improve policies, plan and fund services, conduct research and evaluation, support community based partners and connect children and youth to needed services. CYF-DD's Office of Policy and Planning supports the bureau’s mission by understanding community needs, conducting mental health and intellectual/developmental disabilities systems-level planning, shaping effective policy changes, and ensuring that program models and initiatives are fiscally viable and responsive to need. families and people with IDD. • Conduct prompt research and analysis of local, state and national policies including: legislation, regulations, guidance, budgets, and emerging trends. • Research and relevant policy issues and the policy development process. • Monitor emerging legislative, regulatory and other policy proposals related to the mental and emotional wellbeing of children, youth, and comments. • Maintain a database to track and document local, state, and federal policy issues and the bureau’s efforts to advance policy priorities. • Assist with the design and implementation of quantitative and qualitative data collection (e.g. surveys, focus groups, informational interviews), in collaboration with the Office of Research and Evaluation and interpret and apply population-level data for policy development (e.g. Medicaid). • Develops and maintains relationships with government partners and other stakeholders. • Support the development of the bureau’s planning The Bureau of Division Management & Systems Coordination (DMSC) leads administrative, surveillance, informatics, preparedness, policy, communications, community engagement, and racial equity and social justice activities for the Division and guides the strategic use of Division resources to advance innovative and effective policies and programs.   We are seeking to fill a position in the Division of Disease Control that will provide key support for grant coordination and sustainability initiatives. It is expected that the position will work 35 hours per week to help coordinate grant related activities, track progress on grant milestones, support cross-bureau programmatic coordination, and assist with sustainability initiatives and other projects. This position will work across teams and bureaus to ensure timely reporting and alignment with organizational goals and will report to the Director, Programs and Strategy within DMSC. jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorker. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems and the Bureau of Finance, Administration and Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race To Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The NYC Health Department's Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention (BDCP) strives to reduce the burden of chronic disease, including heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, among New Yorkers. BCDP focuses on nutrition, tobacco use, the built environment, and reducing the impact of cancer. BCDP aims to advance evidence-based policies, programs, community engagement, and research aimed at shifting environments, changing systems and promoting health equity. As a bureau within the NYC Health Department's Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW), BCDP contributes to CHECW's goal of eliminating racial inequities and reducing overall premature mortality among New Yorkers. BCDP puts a focus on reducing exposure to and consumption of unhealthy foods and tobacco industry products and countering industry practices that negatively impact health. In addition to pursuing population-level approaches, BCDP prioritizes communities that bear a disproportionate burden of chronic disease.   The Active Design Unit within BCDP seeks to hire a Program Manager, the Program Manager will oversee the implementation and day to day management of the unit's place-based programs in schools and neighborhood settings, including program planning, partnership coordination, research, and evaluation activities. organizations, government agencies, consultants, and other external partners.  • In collaboration with unit Director, manage and oversee programmatic budgets, contracts, and procurement.  • Manage strategic relationships with peer city agencies, community organizations, academic institutions, and other external partners to share information, coordinate activities, and collaborate on projects that support and inform the work of the Active Design Unit.  • Support community engagement and partner coordination throughout program planning and implementation, including activities that incorporate community perspectives and lived experience into Active Design projects.  • Prepare program updates, grant proposals, funder progress reports, and other written materials to communicate program activities, accomplishments, and outcomes.  • Supervise and manage staff and other team members as assigned, providing guidance, setting priorities, and overseeing work assignments.  • Conduct research and review public health and built environment literature to inform the design and implementation of evidence-informed initiatives that leverage urban planning, architecture, and design strategies to promote healthy behaviors and improve health outcomes.  • Coordinate with Bureau and agency colleagues and external city agency and private partners to plan and implement research and evaluation activities in support of Active Design programs and strategic initiatives.  • Support the development and implementation of data collection and evaluation protocols to document program implementation, participation, utilization, and outcomes, and contribute to analyses, reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. • Monitor and synthesize emerging research, best practices, and public policy developments related to the built environment, physical activity, mental health, social connection, and other health outcomes, particularly in school and neighborhood se tings.  • Plan and coordinate meetings and events, including developing event logistics, preparing presentations and other materials, and communicating program information to key audiences.  • jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The mission of the Bureau of Tuberculosis Control (BTBC) is to prevent the spread of tuberculosis (TB) and eliminate it as a public health problem in New York City. The office of Medical Affairs is looking to fil the role of Program Manager. The Program Manager will provide programmatic leadership across multiple non-clinical functions within the Office of Medical Affairs, overseeing program operations, supervising professional staff, and leading program improvement and evaluation initiatives. The group includes non-clinical staff working in areas including drug-resistant TB case management, regulatory affairs, and the evaluation of newly arrived immigrants and refugees at risk for TB disease. The Program Manager will oversee a portfolio of activities in these areas and supervise professional staff with specialized program responsibilities.   The ideal candidate will be an experienced public health professional with strong leadership, program management, and analytical skills. They will use data to assess program performance and identify opportunities for improvement and will demonstrate initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to translate complex programmatic challenges into actionable solutions.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Use surveillance, clinical, and operational data to monitor program performance, identify gaps and trends, evaluate interventions, and inform program and policy decisions. • Lead or contribute to research and evaluation activities, including study design and data analysis; protocols and IRB submissions; and preparation of reports, presentations, abstracts, and manuscripts. • Provide leadership and oversight for assigned program areas, including program implementation, performance monitoring, operational improvement, and continuity of essential functions. • Supervise and mentor professional staff, establish priorities, oversee work assignments, provide feedback, and support staff development and increasing independence. • Identify programmatic challenges and opportunities for improvement and independently develop, implement, and evaluate solutions. • Lead public health projects and initiatives from planning through implementation and evaluation, collaborating with clinical, epidemiologic, analytical, and operational staff and external partners as needed. • Develop and improve program protocols, workflows, policies, and standard operating procedures, including cross-training and coverage plans to strengthen program continuity.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Experience managing public health, healthcare, research, or program improvement projects through planning, implementation, and evaluation. • Experience supervising or mentoring staff, including delegating responsibilities, establishing priorities, providing feedback, and supporting professional development. • Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple projects and priorities. • Strong analytical skills, including experience using programmatic, surveillance, clinical, or other data to evaluate performance and inform decision-making. • Experience with public health research or program evaluation, including developing research questions, analyzing and interpreting data, and communicating findings. • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, and experience with statistical or data analysis software such as R. • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and internal and external partners. • Knowledge of tuberculosis, infectious disease prevention and control, or clinical public health is preferred but not required. jobs.title: Program Quality Manager, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The NYC Health Department’s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS) falls within the Division of Disease Control, oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Its mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and STIs. BHHS does this through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS’s over 500 staff members work across eight programs: Administration, HIV Care and Treatment, HIV Epidemiology, HIV Prevention, Policy and External Affairs, Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiatives, STI, and Viral Hepatitis. The Viral Hepatitis Program conducts surveillance, and develops and implements programs and projects to prevent, manage and treat hepatitis B and C in New York City.   Reporting to the Project Director and working with the Capacity Building unit, you will be assigned specific viral hepatitis linkage to care initiatives and strategies addressing the Plan to Eliminate Viral Hepatitis in New York City by 2030. Under direction of the Project Director and Director of Capacity Building, you will develop, implement, and evaluate program activities; meeting with external organization staff (such as program managers, clinicians, and service providers) to understand their program implementation and service delivery needs; and provide tailored technical assistance to support effective program outcomes. jobs.title: Qualitative Research Analyst, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy, and Communications within BADU conducts alcohol- and drug-related surveillance, program evaluation and research, maintains databases, designs research protocols, produces reports, writes scientific articles for peer-reviewed journals, facilitates program and policy development, and develops messaging and other communication materials for provider and public audiences.   The Qualitative Research Analyst will support the development and implementation of BADU’s qualitative research and evaluation activities, including project design, data collection, analysis, and dissemination of findings.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Under the supervision of the Senior Qualitative Research Associate, the Qualitative Research Analyst will work collaboratively with program staff and analysts to coordinate qualitative research activities, including conducting literature reviews, designing and implementing study protocols, collecting and analyzing qualitative data, and supporting dissemination activities. 1. Draft qualitative research materials (e.g. protocols, interview guides, and surveys) and support IRB applications. 2. Conduct research literature reviews and desk research, including organizing citation and reference libraries. 3. Collect, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze qualitative data using Dedoose, REDCap, Excel, and other platforms. 4. Support the Senior Qualitative Research Associate in developing training resources for qualitative methods/analysis and building partnerships with other analytic teams in the agency. 5. Support the creation and revision of study and data management systems related to qualitative research, including qualitative codebooks and analytic plans. 6. Support research administrative tasks including scheduling data collection activities, managing study materials, and gift card tracking and dissemination. 7. jobs.title: Research Analyst, BMH, Bureau of Mental Health
jobs.description: The Bureau of Mental Health’s (BMH) mission is to improve mental health and wellness for people in New York City, and to eliminate racial and other long-standing societal disparities by providing services, resources, and opportunities to New Yorkers that are grounded in accurate, data-driven information that fosters community participation, thus reducing the stigma around mental health. To accomplish this mission, the Bureau of Mental Health contracts for supportive housing, crisis intervention, mental health treatment, care coordination and psychiatric rehabilitation services. The bureau directly operates the City’s court-mandated Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT) program, Single Point of Access (SPOA) to mobile treatment and care coordination, and the NYC Supportive Transition and Recovery Team (NYCSTART) for young adults experiencing a first episode psychosis. The bureau also evaluates mental health services and conducts population level surveys and behavioral health care system surveillance to identify gaps care and inform decision making, advocacy and policy. jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst, Strategic Operations and Performance Management
jobs.description: The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) is a world-renowned agency with a long tradition of protecting and promoting health in the nation’s most culturally and linguistically diverse city. Our 7,000-plus team members bring an extraordinary array of languages, cultures, and experiences to bear on the work of public health. Our diversity fuels creativity because all perspectives are heard and valued. DOHMH aims to improve the health outcomes of all New Yorkers by centering persistent racial inequities and promotion of social justice at the core of its work. The Office of Strategic Operations and Performance Management (SOPM) in the Office of the Chief Operating Officer for DOHMH is responsible for leading the implementation of policy efforts across the agency. This office supports the overarching strategies of DOHMH, fosters organizational alignment with those strategies, and supplements divisional capacity as needed. jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality. With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems, the Bureau of Finance and Administrative Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race to Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The Health Department launched Race to Justice (RTJ) in 2016 as its agency-wide internal transformation initiative. The primary purpose of the initiative is to build the Health Department's capacity to address structural racism and health inequities by promoting anti racism and embedding racial equity and social justice in our policies, processes, and programs, ensuring that our internal and external practices reflect our values without perpetuating injustices. Spearheaded by the RTJMT, the initiative aims to transform the Health Department by building capacity and embedding racial equity and social justice within every aspect of DOHMH to ultimately improve equitable health outcomes for all New Yorkers by: 1) Increasing staff's awareness of how racism and other intersecting systems of oppression operate within institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, including the Health Department, are not separate and immune from these systemic injustices. 2) Developing staff's skills to address how internal systems of oppression create health equities. 3) Examining how structural racism and other intersecting systems of oppression impact the Health Department's work, decisions, interactions, and priorities. 4) Implementing policies and practices to mitigate the impacts of systems of oppression.   The Office of the Chief Equity Officer seeks to hire a Senior Manager of Capacity Building to join the management team to build internal capacity among staff to advance racial and social justice and the Health Department's equity goals.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the development and facilitation of communities of practice for agency staff, including equity-focused staff and senior level leadership.  • Organize and/or deliver capacity building trainings and workshops, among other learning activities, focused on embedding equity into daily practices and job responsibilities.  • Evaluate capacity building programs for quality assurance through surveys and analysis of findings.  • Stay abreast of current research, evidence-based best practices, and tools/resources for applying equity in public health.  • Manage, update, and serve as the technical point person for a tool library that includes equity focused tools and resources to assist staff in embedding racial justice and equity.  • Serve as central point of contact for agency equity stakeholder community, including implementing a system of accountability for staff working on projects that advance the goals of the Office of the Chief Equity Officer.  • Connect and coordinate with other team members as it relates to capacity building.  • Contribute to the overall design, strategy, and implementation of Race to Justice activities, as a member of the management team. Strong project management and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with government agencies, community organizations, consultants, academic partners, and other external stakeholders  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Team Lead: TST for SU & EAU, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The Team Lead for TST (SU & EAU) directs tuberculosis surveillance, environmental infection control, and outbreak prevention strategies across DOH chest centers, shelters, and high-risk facilities. In this role, you will manage a multidisciplinary team of research scientists, epidemiologists, and public health advisors conducting quantitative research on airborne tuberculosis detection, managing employee tuberculin skin testing (TST) programs, and overseeing patient isolation protocols. You will evaluate airborne mitigation technologies—such as UVGI, negative pressure, and ACH air-flow systems—to recommend compliant products and establish evidence-based safety guidelines. Additionally, you will oversee outbreak investigations, represent the TB Control Program across internal and external committees, and author scientific papers to publish findings and advance environmental infection control practices statewide.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Direct activities and staff of the Tuberculin Skin Testing (TST) Surveillance Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. Ensures that staff in the TST Unit conduct periodic and serial testing of targeted high-risk DOH employees. - Direct activities and staff of the Environmental Affairs Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. - Directs respiratory protection fit testing by the TST Unit and the Environmental Affairs Unit for designated staff in BTBC. - Performs employee evaluations - Serve as a resource to the BTBC for environmental issues pertaining to TB infection control devices and measures including UVG lamps, negatives air pressure, ventilation, and respiratory prevention. - Consults on referrals for patients on home isolation - Provides specialty guidance to Bureau and DOH staff associated with TB outbreaks. - Directs TB related infection control surveys, evaluation, and assessments. - Provides recommendations on infection control and the implementation of environmental controls understanding the standards and guidelines set by the Joint Commission of Accreditation of Health Organizations (JCAHO), CDC, OSHA, PESH, and NIOSH. - Writes technical reports, recommendations, and protocols related to TB transmission. - Plans and implements protocols to develop effective coordination of efforts of the Program and outside projects. - Consults and represents the Program with internal and external entities regarding environmental control of tuberculosis and/or related projects, including providing information regarding design, methodology, sampling procedures, skin testing procedures, and technical matters - Conducts research as indicated, writes papers, and publishes on environmental control of TB  Preferred skills: - Excellent written and oral communication skills  - Experience in research design and intervention - jobs.title: Vector-borne Disease Epidemiologist, Bureau of Communicable Diseases
jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory (including COVID-19), zoonotic, and vector-borne diseases.  Position Summary:  This position is in the Zoonotic and Vector-Borne Disease Unit (ZVDU) within the Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD). ZVDU is responsible for overseeing the surveillance for reportable, new, high profile, and emerging vector-borne diseases that are reportable in New York City. Vectorborne diseases include, but are not limited to Lyme disease, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, alpha-gal syndrome and certain high-profile diseases such as legionellosis and cyclosporiasis.   ZVDU is recruiting an experienced epidemiologist and data analyst to work under the Research Scientist to perform and enhance Lyme disease surveillance as well as contribute to similar efforts for other vectorborne diseases. The person will have experience in epidemiology, data management, and analysis, outreach and education for the public and human and animal health providers, as well as participate in a wide range of activities, with an emphasis on vectorborne diseases, and direct oversight of Lyme disease surveillance. They will be a collaborative partner working closely with the Division of Environmental Health, the Public Health Laboratory, and local, state, and federal partners.  Job Duties and Responsibilities:  •	Assist the Research Scientist II in the development and enhancement of surveillance practices, updating (and developing when needed) disease case investigation protocols and standardized investigation case forms used for tick-borne diseases,  •	Conduct case investigations and other activities required for routine surveillance of Lyme disease, •	Participate in the collection, management and analysis of quality data for research and surveillance purposes,  •	Conduct quality assurance of data, •	Maintain, summarize and report on tick-borne disease data from the BCD surveillance system •	Conduct literature reviews of recent and relevant research as it relates to our understanding our diseases of interest, •	Work collaboratively with colleagues in Environmental Health and other agencies and organizations, •	Participate in ZVDU fieldwork which may include tick dragging as well as other fieldwork opportunities, •	Participate in large BCD outbreak investigations as needed, •	Supervise seasonal college interns, •	Conduct outreach to the medical and veterinary communities,  •	Participate in agency-wide response activations as needed  Preferred Skills:   •	Experience with disease surveillance, infectious diseases, and database management •	Ability to work independently and in teams to collect and analyze data, including leading outbreak and cluster investigations •	Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interpret data and convey concepts clearly and concisely  •	Proficiency with SAS (programming and analysis) or other analytic software, Adobe Acrobat, and MS Office software; ability to learn new data systems quickly, document in the data systems, and comply with data integrity and security to safeguard all personal identifiable information •	Flexibility and adaptability are key attributes for this position; candidates should be highly organized with the ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Wellness Advocate Supervisor, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Provide research and data support for the expansion of Relay at new hospitals in collaboration with hospital leadership. Conduct research to develop protocols, communications materials, and presentations. Provide regular supervision to full-time and part-time Wellness Advocates in their role supporting patients following a non-fatal overdose and conducting research. Review reports from the program’s database and dashboard on a regular basis to support data-driven supervision. Utilize the program's database to monitor Wellness Advocates' cases to ensure quality assurance standards are being met for research, data collection and data entry, decision making, and overall documentation. Collaborate with colleagues to support the program’s reporting requirements and record observations, including by performing internal auditing activities and assessing participant records. Participate in monthly calls with ED leadership to discuss program implementation and data trends within each collaborating ED. Using program data, lead discussions around the ED staff training needs. Review resumes, screen and interview candidates, hire, orient and on-board new Wellness Advocates. Help to conduct new hire and ongoing trainings for Wellness Advocates responding to non-fatal overdoses. Work collaboratively with other Relay and BADUPCT staff to support the goals and mission of the program and agency. Other duties as assigned.  PREFERRED SKILLS: - Experience practicing public health and working across systems to further a public health approach to alcohol and other drug use. - Experience in working with programs serving people who use drugs, including those using harm reduction approaches. - Experience in managing a budget and/or contracts. - Experience in program monitoring and evaluation. - Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. - Ability to work independently and as part of a team. - Possess exceptional interpersonal, research, written and verbal communication skills. - Detail-oriented with outstanding organizational skills. - Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. - Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint and statistical software such as SPSS or SAS. jobs.title: Project Administrator for Planning
jobs.description: *This vacancy is only open to 1) current permanent City employees serving in the City Planner civil service title or 2) on leave from the title or 3) candidates who are reachable on the City Planner civil service list, Exam No. 5045. [Please indicate your list number on your cover letter and resume.]  NYC Parks is an award-winning City agency that designs, builds and cares for public spaces for New Yorkers to connect, play and enjoy. NYC Parks manages more than 30,000 acres or 14% of the City’s land, encompassing more than 5,000 individual properties. Our diverse set of assets includes recreational facilities, nature centers, historic buildings and structures, golf courses, athletic fields, playgrounds, tennis courts, public pools, public restroom buildings and nearly 14 miles of beaches.  The Planning team is at the forefront of Parks’ open space agenda: communicating agency goals, policies and advancing plans for a vibrant and sustainable park system that meets the recreational, social, and environmental needs of our city. The team is responsible for the Agency’s real estate and land use functions including the acquisition, disposition and preservation of parkland, Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), environmental review, and the ownership and management of the Agency’s property records. Additionally, the team develops long-term planning strategies including management of citywide and interagency resiliency and waterfront projects, development of the citywide greenway plan and researching new initiatives.  Major Responsibilities	  •	Under general direction, working as a Project Administrator for Planning, with latitude for independent initiative and judgment, manage a portfolio of open space planning projects for the Planning team. •	Perform due diligence to support open space acquisitions to enable increased recreation amenities, improved waterfront access, resiliency planning, sustainable design, natural resource preservation, and an expanded citywide greenway network. •	Advise, coordinate and communicate with other Parks divisions (e.g. Capital), government agencies, stakeholders, and project partners to advance the planning and implementation of Parks’ open space agenda within the context of assigned planning projects. •	Research, analyze, frame and document opportunities for addressing under-resourced communities. •	Present and represent the division and the Agency at project meetings. Negotiate and advocate on behalf of Parks, defending the agency’s open space goals and interests. •	Prepare strategic planning documents, high level maps, and graphics for presentations and planning documents. •	Present proposals to others at Parks, as well as Community Boards, neighborhood groups, and elected officials, and provide expert opinions and recommendations. •	Review, evaluate, and analyze land use review documents and planning documents to advance open space goals and protect existing assets. •	Manage highly complex, high-profile projects, prepare briefing memoranda, project schedules, budget proposals, grant applications, correspondence, reports, and other related documents. •	Administrative tasks related to the above responsibilities including but not limited to taking meeting notes, scheduling meetings and follow-ups. KCDA has an exciting opportunity to work as a IT Resource Analyst in the Information Technology Bureau. The Information Technology Resource Analyst role is to provide support for IT’s Resource Management.  This includes procuring, installing, diagnosing, repairing, moving, maintaining, and upgrading computer hardware and related equipment, removing and/or replacing units as required, and administering software to ensure optimal performance with minimal downtime. The Resource Analysts will also assist in software and license procurements, renewals, installations, and imaging of computers.   Under general supervision, with some latitude for independent initiative and judgment, the prospective candidate will be responsible for the following:  -	IT resource planning •	IT hardware and software lifecycle analysis •	Asset management and tracking: monitor, track and record changes in IT service assets and throughout asset service lifecycle •	Oversee IT resource management processes; make certain purchase orders are input into the IT database accurately -	Diagnose and resolve hardware failures and replace defective components. -	Coordinate warranty repairs with hardware vendors. -	Assist with office relocations and workstations setup. -	Familiarity with Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager. -	Ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical users. -	Knowledge of cybersecurity best-practices for endpoint devices. jobs.description: RICHMOND COUNTY DISTRICT ATTORNEY  The men and women of the Richmond County District Attorney’s office work each day in partnership with Law Enforcement and the people of Staten Island to pursue justice for victims of crime, to prevent crime in all its forms, and to promote the safety and well-being of all citizens of our Borough.  THE DIVISON The Economic Crimes Bureau prosecutes cases of fraud, grand larceny, wage theft, and many other financial crimes. This includes cases of entitlement fraud such as Medicaid or unemployment fraud, construction fraud including the prosecution of construction site fatalities, and theft of goods or services. Additionally, the Economic Crimes Bureau assists the office by seeking the forfeiture of funds which were earned via illegal activity. Some of these assets come back to our office, to be used in furthering the Office’s mission of preventing crime before it happens.  THE ROLE Under the direct supervision of the Forensic Accountant, in close collaboration with other members of the RCDA team. The selected candidate will serve as an Economic Crimes Analyst; duties will include, but are not limited to the following:  •	Perform analytical work in the compilation and examination of complex data in criminal investigations involving money laundering, larceny, and other financial crimes; •	Review and analyze information gathered during criminal investigations as well as utilizing complex databases and analytical software to prepare maps, charts, graphs, reports, spreadsheets and link analysis to support attorneys and law enforcement; •	Analyze statistical data to trace funds through a variety of accounts; •	The Economic Crimes Analyst may be called upon to testify in court regarding analysis performed during investigations; •	Ability to review voluminous financial records and to advise or assist in the investigation of alleged fraud.  •	Other duties as assigned. jobs.title: Investigative Analyst
jobs.description: The New York County District Attorney’s Office has an immediate opening for an Investigative Analyst in its Crime Strategies Unit (CSU). The Crime Strategies Unit proactively gathers and analyzes crime data and intelligence to drive the Office’s strategies on crime reduction and public safety. Members of CSU work closely with the New York City Police Department to identify and study crime trends, as well as groups and individuals most responsible for driving crimes that impact our communities, including violent crime, theft, and fraud. CSU also supports the mission of the Gun Violence Strategic Partnership, which brings together both state and federal law enforcement agencies to combat gun violence throughout New York City. Investigative analysts are responsible for providing CSU with investigative, analytical, and data manipulation support. The position requires a critical thinker with a strong combination of data skills and technological savvy. Candidates should also possess strong organizational and communication skills, as CSU relies on analysts’ work product in presentations to the highest levels of the District Attorney’s Office as well as law enforcement and community partners.    Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  •	Gather, analyze, and process data using industry-current and in-house proprietary applications to produce a complete model of crime trends in Manhattan neighborhoods. •	Assist in developing and implementing intelligence-driven prosecution strategies targeting priority offenders. •	Analyze intelligence to identify gun violence drivers in conjunction with local, state, and federal partners. •	Gather, organize, and analyze firearm traces and ballistic comparison reports and data. •	Support day-to-day unit functions as needed. •	Create descriptive presentations and reports using statistical analysis, including cleaning and synthesizing data, and reconciling qualitative and quantitative data sources. •	Perform a full range of administrative and paralegal duties as needed.   In addition to the Minimum Qualification Requirements, all candidates must possess the following:  •	Level 1 – Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and one (1) year of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.          •	Level 2 -  Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and two (2) years of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.        •	Level 3 -  Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and three (3) years of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.   *Master’s degree can be substituted for years of experience. *   Preferred Requirements/Skills:  •	Proficiency with Microsoft Office products. Excel experience (pivot tables; charts; functions; etc.) preferred. •	Familiarity with data mapping, including geocoding preferred; and a fast learner regarding new technology tools and software. Experience using Photoshop; ArcGIS; i2 Analyst Notebook; etc. a plus. •	Superior organizational, time management, writing, and communication skills are essential. •	Capable of building institutional relationships with community residents and organizations, police, and other law enforcement agencies. •	Ability to effectively communicate investigative results to other team members, and to testify in court if necessary. •	Experience in the Criminal Justice System preferred. •	An understanding of general practices related to legal records management, data protection, and privacy/confidentiality. jobs.title: Investigative Analyst
jobs.description: The New York County District Attorney’s Office (DANY) has an opening for an Investigative Analyst in the Forensic Sciences Unit. In this position, the Investigative Analyst is responsible for providing highly skilled analytical support to the Assistant District Attorneys (ADAs) assigned FSU. The Investigative Analyst will work independently to handle incoming DNA matches and reports, serve as the office-wide liaison to FID and the OCME, and help detectives and ADAs solve no-arrest complaints and build cases with DNA evidence.    Responsibilities include but are not limited to:  •	Manage information in DNA Hits, a web-based application that allows the Office of Chief Medical Examiner’s Forensic Biology (DNA) Lab to simultaneously notify the DANY and NYPD of DNA matches that occur through the local, state, and national DNA databases. This includes analyzing matches, determining whether a match is probative, obtaining police paperwork, coordinating information with other jurisdictions where matches occur, contacting investigators, analyzing offenders’ criminal records, and assisting ADAs in obtaining all relevant documents and reports for Grand Jury presentations and trial. •	Assist Unit Chief and other ADAs in trial preparation for cold case indictments, including interviewing witnesses, obtaining evidence, performing background checks, preparing exhibits for trial and assisting at trial. •	Serve as administrative liaison between DANY and the OCME, as well as our office and the NYPD Forensic Investigative Division, which houses evidence intake, the ballistics, narcotics and trace evidence labs, and the latent print development unit. This includes receiving, analyzing, and distributing all lab reports to the relevant ADA, and monitoring all special requests for testing of evidence. •	Maintain up-to-date logs of all received DNA lab reports, DNA deferral letters, and hit notifications. •	Attend meetings of the NYS Forensic Science Commission and meetings related to NYPD’s Forensic Investigative Division to help manage laboratory issues. •	Manage DANYNET for FS/CCU. This includes reading, cataloguing, and uploading documents for the FS/CCU library. •	Manage DNA Evidence Management Program (DEMP) and train paralegals office-wide in use of the program, which locates vouchers and tracks evidence testing. •	Review cases flagged from ECAB as involving forensic evidence. •	Assist FS/CCU ADAs with all phases of trial preparation, including research for Frye scientific admissibility hearings and preparation of evidence exhibits. •	Assist Unit Chief in preparation of training materials for both office-wide and out of office presentations, including PowerPoint and written materials. •	Perform related tasks as assigned. jobs.description: The New York County District Attorney’s Office is seeking a Senior Investigative Analyst for the Intimate Partner and Sexual Violence Bureau’s (IPSV) IPV Misdemeanor Pre-Arrest Coordination Team (IMPACT) within the Special Victims Division.   IMPACT is a newly established initiative focused on conducting proactive, pre-arrest investigations in IPV misdemeanor cases, strengthening coordination with law enforcement and community partners, and ensuring survivors receive timely access to critical services and resources. The Senior Investigative Analyst will work closely with the Director of IMPACT to identify appropriate cases for pre-arrest investigation, support the development of those investigations, coordinate with internal and external partners, assist in creating and implementing protocols for this new initiative, and maintain and analyze program data. The Analyst will also regularly represent IMPACT and the Office in meetings with the New York City Police Department (NYPD), community-based organizations, and other bureaus and units within the District Attorney’s Office. The position also includes assisting with U visa law enforcement certifications, providing exposure to the intersection of criminal, civil, and immigration law. This position offers a unique opportunity to help shape and implement a new initiative, gain experience with both criminal and civil matters, develop an understanding of immigration law through U visa certification work, and collaborate closely with prosecutors, law enforcement, survivor advocates, community organizations, and other partners.   Responsibilities include but are not limited to:  •	Collaborating closely with the Director of IMPACT to review criminal complaints, domestic incident reports, police reports, and other materials submitted by the New York City Police Department and identify cases appropriate for IMPACT intervention and pre-arrest investigation. •	Assisting with pre-arrest investigations by obtaining and reviewing evidence, generating subpoenas and other records requests, analyzing documents and digital materials, and conducting searches of relevant databases. •	Coordinating with the Survivor Services Bureau by providing advocates with relevant survivors and case information to facilitate survivor outreach and the scheduling of interviews. •	Attending survivor and witness interviews to take detailed notes, assist with case documentation, identify necessary investigative follow-up, and support the development of the investigation. •	Serving as a regular liaison with NYPD personnel, community-based organizations, survivor-service providers, and other external partners regarding IMPACT cases, operations, and initiatives. •	Collaborating with bureaus, units, investigators, analysts, advocates, and other personnel throughout the District Attorney’s Office to facilitate investigations, obtain information, coordinate services, and advance IMPACT initiatives. •	Representing IMPACT and, when appropriate, the District Attorney’s Office at internal and external meetings, working groups, trainings, and community-partner meetings. •	Assisting the Director in developing, documenting, implementing, and refining policies, protocols, workflows, and best practices for IMPACT as the initiative develops and expands. •	Partnering with advocates from the Survivor Services Bureau and outside agencies to coordinate appropriate services, resources, and support for survivors. •	Assisting the Director with the preparation of U visa law enforcement certifications by reviewing case records and related materials to determine whether a matter involves qualifying criminal activity, preparing certification forms and supporting documentation, communicating with immigration attorneys and other relevant parties, and tracking requests through completion. •	Tracking, organizing, and maintaining comprehensive data regarding referrals, investigations, case outcomes, survivor engagement, services, and other IMPACT activities. •	Conducting data collection and analysis to identify trends, measure program activity and outcomes, and support evaluation and continued development of IMPACT. •	Preparing statistical reports, summaries, charts, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, and other materials for internal and external reporting, presentations, program evaluation, and strategic planning. •	Compiling and organizing discovery and other case materials to ensure accurate and timely preparation for legal proceedings. •	Drafting correspondence, memoranda, legal documents, protocols, reports, and other written materials with accuracy and attention to detail. •	Assisting with the development and delivery of training, presentations, and informational materials for NYPD, community partners, and Office personnel regarding IMPACT. •	Supporting special projects and other operational needs of IMPACT as the initiative continues to develop and expand. jobs.description: The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values.  The FDNY Bureau of Enterprise Technology manages key departmental initiatives and drives data-driven decision-making. Its Data Quality unit is responsible for generating actionable insights through analysis, reporting, and visualizations. This unit also ensures accountability and transparency by compiling metrics for the Mayor's Management Report (MMR) and producing datasets for NYC Open Data.  The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) seeks a full-time City Research Scientist, L2 in the Data Quality Unit. With latitude for independent initiative and judgement, the Data Quality Analyst will assist the Department’s in the making evidence-based decisions. Day-to-day responsibilities focus on data quality and insight delivery. This includes rigorously performing data quality checks and anomaly detection. The Data Quality Analyst will also support the building of interactive dashboards, primarily using Tableau and modern Python frameworks (Dash/Streamlit). Other core duties include swift fulfilling of ad-hoc data requests and designing appropriate metrics to track and report on departmental performance. This position will also participate in community outreach, especially in the context of Open Data which could include responding to public inquiries, representing the Department at Open Data Events and gathering feedback from the community. This is a crucial function that connects the FDNY's internal data efforts with the public, leveraging data transparency to enhance safety and build trust. Minimum qualifications: 1.  For Assignment Level I (only physical, biological and environmental sciences and public health) A master's degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological or environmental science or in public health.  To be appointed to Assignment Level II and above, candidates must have:  1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or  2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or  3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least a master's degree in an appropriate field of specialization and at least two years of experience described in "2" above. Two years as a City Research Scientist Level I can be substituted for the experience required in "1" and "2" above.    NOTE:  Probationary Period  Appointments to this position are subject to a minimum probationary period of one year. Preferred skills: Excellent communication and presentation skills, skilled in creating data visualizations and metrics. Excellent programming skills in SQL and Python. Knowledge of basic statistics.

jobs.description: Who We Are Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms. We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes. We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact. What We Build Our products— Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom , Geodes , and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA —are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide. Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application. Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy. These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students. Where We’re Headed Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support. Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale. Job Purpose Reporting to the Director of Policy, the Lead Policy Analyst will act as a senior-level individual contributor, operating as the team’s primary subject matter expert and analytical engine. This role will take ownership of Great Minds’ policy intelligence work by tracking and interpreting the federal, state, and local landscape to ensure the organization is well-positioned to engage and influence. The position will bring depth, initiative, and independent judgment to complex policy questions and will translate findings into strategies that meaningfully shape how Great Minds engages with policymakers, state agencies, and K–12 stakeholders. Responsibilities Serve as the team’s primary analytical resource for K–12 policy trends—independently framing issues, synthesizing intelligence across federal, state, and local levels, and contributing substantively to Great Minds’ company-wide point of view on factors shaping the adoption and implementation of high-quality instructional materials. Own the tracking and monitoring of state and local legislation and policy; identify and escalate emerging policy trends with clear analytical context and recommended implications for the organization. Lead projects that examine how legislative mandates shape policy action at the local, regional, and state levels; develop findings that are rigorous, accessible, and directly connected to Great Minds’ strategic priorities. Translate regional trend analysis into concrete recommendations that help shape the organization’s policy engagement strategy; identifying where and how Great Minds should invest, focus and build relationships. Ensure internal stakeholders are equipped to understand and act on the policy environment by producing clear briefings, frameworks, and recommendations tailored to diverse audiences across the organization. Represent Great Minds externally at policy conferences and sector events, strengthening the organization’s credibility and visibility among policymakers and K–12 influencers. Requirements 7+ years of experience in K–12 policy, applied research, or a closely related discipline, with a track record of owning and advancing substantive policy work Proven ability to independently drive research projects from problem framing through strategic recommendation, with strong judgment about when to escalate and how to prioritize Sophisticated command of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, with the ability to synthesize complex findings into accessible, compelling narratives for varied audiences Proven ability to manage competing priorities and stakeholder demands, balancing ongoing policy monitoring with discrete research projects and time-sensitive requests from across the organization Deep familiarity with state and local policy development processes, including legislative tracking and stakeholder engagement Demonstrated experience converting a complex policy landscape into clear strategic priorities and actionable plans Required Education Bachelor’s degree Preferred Advanced degree in public policy, education policy, or a related field Status Full-time Location Remote The expected base salary range for this position is $107,000-$120,000, however the offered salary may be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations. The base salary is not inclusive of benefits or other incentives. A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position. New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check. Any communication to applicants relating to the Great Minds hiring process will only come from email addresses with the domains greatminds.org or greatminds.recruitee.com . If in the course of the application or hiring process with Great Minds you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact security@greatminds.org Great Minds is an equal opportunity employer. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to solve complex issues. Strong ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with internal and external teams. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive. Why join the Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences? The Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS) is the historic heart of Harvard University. It is the home of Harvard’s undergraduate program (Harvard College, founded in 1636) as well as all of Harvard’s Ph.D. programs (the Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, founded in 1872), Harvard Athletics and the Division of Continuing Education. The 40 academic departments and 30+ centers of the FAS support a community unparalleled in its academic excellence across the broadest range of liberal arts and sciences disciplines. Together, the FAS seeks to foster an environment of ambition, curiosity and shared commitment to knowledge and truth that elicits excellence from all members of our community and prepares the next generation of leaders through a transformative educational experience. Job Summary: The Researcher Affairs Specialist administers a portfolio of researcher appointments and serves as a primary resource for faculty, principal investigators, departments, research centers, and researchers throughout the Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS). Working in partnership with University administrative offices, the Researcher Affairs Specialist ensures researcher personnel actions are processed accurately, efficiently, and in compliance with University policies, collective bargaining agreements, immigration regulations, and applicable federal and state employment laws. The position requires exceptional organizational skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, and a strong customer service orientation while supporting a diverse and complex research community. Maintains researcher personnel records in accordance with FAS processes and policies. Tracks appointment end dates, reappointment dates, and review dates and communicates upcoming actions to departments. Hiring and Onboarding Supports and coordinates researcher hiring processes, including appointment documentation and workflow processing. Coordinates visual compliance screening and visa initiation as appropriate. Initiates and monitors I-9 processing and employment eligibility requirements. Partners with multiple University offices to ensure timely onboarding and appointment completion. jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. Your Team:  The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data.
