This position works with a broad and growing array of technology and has a deep understanding of learning design in order to serve as online pedagogy subject matter expert, project manager, and coach for Husson Online and Distance Education. This position makes data-informed decisions to create meaningful, measurable, and observable student-learning experiences and improve course quality. The Instructional Designer collaborates with university partners to ensure universally-designed, human-centered learning experiences that meet university standards. This position may qualify for remote work. Applications received two weeks from job posting will receive full consideration; applications after this date may receive consideration depending on the status of the search. jobs.description: Instructional Designer Remote, US About Us InStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it. Through this mission, we are expanding access to insurance-based care, increasing engagement in treatment, and improving treatment outcomes. We are doing this by combining research-backed clinical care and innovative technology to eliminate the major problems with care today: difficulty finding providers, months of waiting to be seen, arduous onboarding processes, and inconsistent use of evidence-based therapies and outcomes tracking. Our vision is to become the nation’s most trusted provider of pediatric anxiety and OCD care. Team InStride Health: Our Core Values Give Heart : We lead with heart, treating patients and their families the way we want our loved ones to be treated. Work Smart : We find smarter ways to solve hard problems and fix the broken mental health system by leveraging technology, diversity of thought, and innovation. Have Humility : We leave our egos at the door, empowering our team to collaborate, celebrate diversity, and adopt a growth mindset. Embrace Community: We all belong. We are in this together, and we never worry alone. We believe in each other and recognize that every voice matters. About the Role We are looking for an Instructional Designer to design, build, and manage learning initiatives for our community of providers, including psychiatrists, therapists, and exposure coaches. As a key member of our Learning and Development team, you will partner with clinical leaders and subject matter experts to turn complex behavioral health protocols into engaging, practical training that strengthens the care our providers deliver to kids, teens, and families. The ideal candidate brings a background in online course creation and project management. This is a fully remote position. Responsibilities: Needs Assessment & Instructional Design Conduct front-end needs analyses with clinical leadership to diagnose performance gaps and define measurable, performance-based learning objectives. Apply adult learning theory and instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, SAM, Backward Design) to structure modular asynchronous and synchronous training paths. Partner closely with clinical subject matter experts (SMEs) to translate complex behavioral health protocols into digestible, scenario-based learning experiences. Content Development & Multimedia Production Design and develop interactive e-learning modules, job aids, and knowledge checks using Articulate 360 (Storyline and Rise). Script, record, and edit multimedia elements, including video walkthroughs, audio voiceovers, screencasts, and graphic assets, using tools such as Camtasia. Use generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, AI voiceover platforms) responsibly to accelerate storyboarding, draft scenario scripts, build assessment items, and streamline authoring workflows. Stay current on emerging technologies and trends in digital learning. Measurement, Quality Assurance & Iteration Build assessments that evaluate learner comprehension, retention, and clinical application. Conduct rigorous quality assurance reviews of AI-assisted drafts and finalized modules to confirm clinical accuracy, tone, instructional integrity, and technical functionality before deployment. Gather post-training analytics and learner feedback to continuously refine and improve curriculum assets. Project Management Deliver work against defined project timelines, share regular progress updates with cross-functional partners, and keep project tracking tools (e.g., ClickUp) current in real time. What You Need to Succeed in the Role Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Instructional Technology, or a related field. 2+ years of professional experience in instructional design and digital course development, ideally for specialized, technical, or clinical adult audiences. Demonstrated proficiency in rapid e-learning authoring tools (specifically Articulate 360) and video/audio editing software (e.g., TechSmith Camtasia, Audacity, or Adobe Creative Cloud). Solid foundation in adult learning theory, instructional design models, and assessment design (e.g., Bloom's Taxonomy, Kirkpatrick Evaluation Model). Practical experience using generative AI tools to accelerate content ideation, drafting, and multimedia production while maintaining strict editorial and factual oversight. Strong project management and organizational skills. Clear, effective verbal and written communication across remote, multidisciplinary teams. Ability to work well both independently and as part of a collaborative, cross-functional team in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. Interest or background in behavioral health is a plus. Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic startup environment: we're looking for candidates who embrace change, thrive in ambiguity, and shift readily as priorities and team needs evolve. A portfolio of past instructional design projects, storyboards, or interactive e-learning modules is required with your application. Salary The expected annual salary for this role is between $72,000–$80,000. Actual starting salary will be determined on an individualized basis and will be based on several factors including but not limited to specific skill set, work experience, etc. Why Join Our Team Generous benefits package (401k with match, Flexible PTO, paid holidays, paid service days, 4 week paid sabbatical, 12 week paid parental leave, health benefits starting on your first day, and more) Opportunity to join a mission-driven company that is changing the landscape of pediatric mental health treatment Chance to make a far-reaching impact by helping children and families access desperately-needed, evidence-based care Opportunity to work with talented and experienced team members who have devoted their lives to solving this problem Fully virtual: work from the comfort of your home with periodic in-person retreats Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB) We want to make our clinical services available for everyone, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or how you identify. To achieve this, we recognize we must continually make progress in building a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive team. Through these efforts, we support two primary objectives at InStride Health: Providing high quality patient care to families. We are in a privileged position to support families during a vulnerable time in their lives. We approach all families and each other with compassion and are most effective as a diverse team where all individuals feel valued, respected, and accepted. Building a mission-driven business that lasts. Specifically, we believe our commitment to a supportive culture improves innovation, decision-making, and efficiency. We invite you to share any additional information about yourself or your experiences that may not be reflected in your CV. Inclusion of this information is completely voluntary. Beware of fake job postings and offers. All official communications from InStride Health will come from email addresses ending in @instride.health. jobs.description: Curriculum Design Specialist, Contract Position About inquirED inquirED was founded by teachers to bring rigorous and joyful learning to every student. We’re a fast-growing start-up, serving more educators and students every day. Inkwell, our integrated ELA and social studies curriculum, brings two core subjects studies together into one coherent instructional experience that builds knowledge and literacy skills, saves time and resources, and supports meaningful learning for both students and teachers. Inquiry Journeys, our elementary social studies curriculum, is used in schools and districts across the country to help students develop deep social studies knowledge and the inquiry skills essential for a thriving democracy. Join our team of designers, advocates, guides, thought leaders, and makers to help us make an even greater impact. Together, we can shape the future of education. About the engagement The Project: We’re building an integrated K–5 Core ELA and social studies curriculum designed to meet the needs of diverse learners while making it easier for elementary teachers to meaningfully incorporate social studies without sacrificing literacy goals. As part of this work, we're looking for part-time Curriculum Design Specialist Contractors to support the ongoing development and refinement of instructional materials. jobs.description: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Specialist Fdtn-Office of Philanthropy - Remote, Virginia (Remote) Location Remote, Virginia (Remote) Department Fdtn-Office of Philanthropy Employment Type Regular Full Time About the Internet Society Foundation The Internet Society (ISOC) supports and promotes the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society. Our work aligns with our goals for the Internet to be open, globally connected, secure, and trustworthy. We seek collaboration with all who share these goals. Together, we focus on building and supporting the communities that make the Internet work; advancing the development and application of Internet infrastructure, technologies, and open standards; and advocating for policy that is consistent with our view of the Internet. The Internet Society Foundation (Foundation) is a non-profit organization that works in concert with the Internet Society. It exists to demonstrate and support the positive difference the Internet can make to people everywhere and promote the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society. The Foundation is committed to a culture of diversity and inclusion, where all individuals are valued for their distinct contributions. Our people are the most valuable strengths we have. This position works closely and collaboratively with members of the Philanthropy and Empowerment teams and directly supports the Director, Learning, Evaluation & Impact in ensuring that programs and funded projects are collecting data, supporting analysis efforts to identify results achieved, communicating results, and facilitating learning from data collected. The MEL Specialist will also contribute to the Foundation's capacity building efforts for staff and grantees, particularly in designing and conducting trainings on monitoring, evaluation and learning for staff and partners. The MEL Specialist combines a working knowledge of technical MEL practices with excellent communication and collaboration skills. The Foundation is a small team of passionate, collaborative, and driven staff that depend on each other to move our mission forward; this is true of this critical position. The MEL Specialist will collaborate across the program portfolio, manage multiple priorities, and support internal and external stakeholders. This role requires strong communication, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, globally diverse environment. A track record of teamwork, initiative, and resourcefulness is essential. Location Remote at home location Essential Duties and Responsibilities Provide technical support for the Foundation’s monitoring, evaluation and learning efforts, primarily to program staff. Contribute to assessments and evaluations of Foundation projects, including designing evaluation methodologies, sampling strategies and data collection tools, collecting and analyzing data, and communicating findings in user-friendly formats. Support the design and implementation of learning and adaptation initiatives for program teams, including facilitating reflection sessions. Provide guidance and assistance [including report writing and infographics development] in data collection and data analysis (both quantitative and qualitative) on assessments and evaluations conducted by M&E and program team. Assist program team in review [including of reports] of grant-level metrics and data collection for associated output, outcome, and impact (as appropriate) level results. Provide technical MEL support to grantees, including providing in person and virtual training, developing guiding materials and resources, holding regular consultations and providing real time support for their MEL needs to develop institutional MEL capacity. Advise and assist grantees with the monitoring, evaluation and learning processes, activities and products during the start-up and implementation phases of projects including developing logic models, theories of change, MEL plans, indicators, and evaluation and learning approaches. Travel internationally either conducting data collection, field research, trainings, or learning sessions. Support Foundation’s data quality efforts through conducting data quality spot checks. Work with other members of the team to complete projects, achieve organizational goals and advance Foundation’s Learning agenda and related efforts. Foster and contribute to initiatives that build an equitable and inclusive workplace that embraces diverse identities, backgrounds and experiences. Prepare external communications materials on Foundation’s monitoring, evaluation and learning efforts, including blog posts, articles, presentations, etc. Perform other duties as assigned. Desired Qualifications Undergraduate degree in political/social science, international relations, or related field. Graduate degree preferred. Minimum three years of professional experience in the international development sector, with at least two years of professional experience in MEL related roles. Demonstrated understanding of the program theory-based approach to program design, monitoring and evaluation. Strong knowledge of and experience with common MEL elements including but not limited to: logical frameworks, performance monitoring plans and indicators. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to successfully collaborate with others at all levels of an organization in a virtual work environment. Ability to design and conduct performance evaluations, including designing methodology and data collection tools. Ability to collect and analyze qualitative and quantitative data; experience in designing and administering questionnaires and interviews required. Ability to interpret and present data in a meaningful, user-friendly way. Familiarity with both qualitative and quantitative data analysis software, such as SPSS, STATA, R, NVivo, or Dedoose, preferred. Self-starter with significant project management experience, excellent organizational skills, and ability to work across a range of projects. Display cultural and gender sensitivity, engage with colleagues and partners in a respectful, welcoming manner and demonstrate integrity by modeling Foundation's values. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Additional language skills in French and Spanish preferred. Passion for, and demonstrated commitment to, a more accessible and trustworthy Internet for all! What You'll Love About Us Make an Impact. Compensation and benefits for this position will be paid in local currency and based on the country and geographic location’s local salary and benefits market data for the position. team, translate learning agendas into documented metric definitions, data structures, and processes and translate these into clear stakeholder communications In partnership with the Data Manager, impact Partner with the Research & Learning team to elevate metrics that support the broader research strategy Identify where business questions can't be answered with existing data or tools; develop data stack — warehouse, BI tools, and public data infrastructure — to credibly advise the investment team(s) and inform infrastructure decisions Ensure the data feeding into our systems is accurate, complete, and trustworthy from the point of intake (30%) Project manage annual data collection cycles; partner with the Data Manager and investment team leads on clean rostering, survey development, at the source Partner with the data engineer and fellow analysts to validate and clean incoming data and execute automated quality control checkpoints Review and update databases within the designated investment team's scope, ensuring accuracy and integrity across all data sources Apply and reinforce best practices for capturing data updates regularly and accurately within the investment team Spot and report data anomalies from the stakeholder lens — quality issues automated back-end processing may miss — investigate root cause, report to relevant teammates, and manage stakeholder communications when a resolution isn't immediately possible Turn data into the insights and recommendations that shape investment decisions (30%) Own the analytics relationship for your designated investment team(s), developing deep knowledge of its goals, workflows, and data needs to serve as a trusted, actively sought-out resource Lead ad hoc analyses to support data-driven decision-making and synthesize findings into written investment recommendations Own and respond to data reporting and analysis requests supporting grant and funder reporting Manage and execute ad hoc analysis and rapid prototyping using SQL, BI tools, and AI-assisted analytics to answer business questions Collaborate with Research & Learning and investment teams on custom queries and datasets supporting the learning agenda, team strategy, Board requests, and funder reporting and prospecting Develop planning tools, analysis frameworks, and visualizations that drive insight generation and identify portfolio bright spots, accounting for historical, contextual, and comparative data and perspectives Help colleagues across NewSchools find, trust, and use data themselves (10%) Serve as the go-to resource for data questions across the organization, helping non-technical colleagues navigate systems and dashboards Support implementation and adoption of self-service analytics tools across the assigned investment team(s), including onboarding, coaching, and ongoing support Support ad hoc data needs across the organization QUALIFICATIONS Minimum 2 years of experience in roles working with complex data sets and owning end-to-end data processes (collection, auditing, analysis, meaning-making) Proficiency in SQL and experience with cloud data warehouse platforms (BigQuery preferred) Experience with BI/analytics tools (Omni Analytics preferred) and building self-service artifacts and reporting for non-technical users Experience with data validation, quality control processes, and data cleaning Project management experience, particularly running recurring data collection cycles that involve coordinating multiple internal and external stakeholders Comfort using AI-assisted analytics tools for ad hoc analysis and rapid prototyping Knowledge of the K-12 education sector with experience working with teacher, leader, and edtech data -or- Knowledge of the K-12 education sector with experience working with charter and district school and student data strongly preferred Travel up to 10% for in-person team meetings, retreats and conferences EXPERIENCE YOU BRING Building and maintaining knowledge management structures that make portfolio data and findings reusable across teams Supporting progress monitoring and research partnerships, including what gets collected and how data quality is protected Translating analysis into clear insights and recommendations for various stakeholders and audiences Implementing continuous improvement initiatives that increase efficiency Planning, prioritizing and managing multiple workstreams YOUR WAYS OF WORKING Ground decisions, priorities, and actions in NewSchools’ mission and commitment to equity Communicate clearly and proactively, share information before being asked, and raise questions and concerns directly Adapt how you communicate to the audience, make a clear case for your recommendations, and give and and market through regular scanning of research, data and public sources, and use it to surface patterns and gaps the team should examine COMPENSATION A competitive compensation package including base This position will be in support of Uniformed Service’s University Center for Advanced Research for Military Optimization, Readiness, and Rehabilitation (ARMORR). The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals. Responsibilities Edit and proofread content (articles, infographics, slide decks, speaker notes, reports, scripts, SCORMS) in evidence-based health and wellness course curricula without altering the technical content to be presented. Compile, maintain, and update metrics, databases, and spreadsheets, and assists in dissemination by preparing documents and standard project reports. Monitor organizational workflow tasks and update Standard Operating Guides or Procedures. Tracks and communicates needs and updates to appropriate team members. Provide administrative support on projects. Engage and consult with internal and external stakeholders to identify learning needs. Analyze learning needs and provide recommendations for situationally appropriate training solutions, including but not limited to learning activities, curricula, and training materials. Develop, field and collect content/experience assessments and evaluations. Analyze and report on results, adjusting as needed for success and improvement. Create and deliver dynamic and engaging experiences for adult learners with diverse learning styles, ensuring alignment with learning objectives, training strategies and organizational branding guidelines. Lead and facilitate training efforts (i.e. workshops, presentations, and webinars). Provide quality control feedback to clients and other staff members on training performance. Develop and sustain relationships with DoW stakeholders (Service Members, health care and performance providers, military leaders, etc.) to inform the creation and dissemination of materials. Engages in outreach efforts to increase the DoW and professional communities’ awareness of HPRC’s resources. May perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. This may include attendance of and participation in required training for role. Qualifications Education and Experience Bachelor's Degree required in Health Sciences, Instructional Design, Human Performance or a similar field. Master's Degree preferred. Minimum of 3-5 years experience required. Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Experience with plain language writing, public speaking, and presenting. Strong knowledge of adult learning theory, effective instructional design strategies as well as regulations and best practices related to learning design accessibility requirements (i.e. Section 508). Demonstrated ability to design, develop, implement, deliver and facilitate high-quality, engaging in-person, blended and e-learning content. Ability to guide the development process from initial concept to final implementation and evaluation, including creation of clear and concise storyboards, graphics concepts, audio scripts, user interactions, navigation, and other related elements. Ability to manage several complex projects simultaneously while working under pressure to meet deadlines. Experience in interpreting research data and peer-reviewed publications and have knowledge and translation of research in the fields of social, emotional, and psychological health, public health, and relational health. Knowledge of public health/social science theories of behavior change. Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to interact with all levels of employees and management. Ability to work independently as well as partner effectively in a team environment. Strong analytical, problem solving and customer service skills, with a focus on relationship management and customer satisfaction. Computer proficiency and technical aptitude, including working knowledge of MS Office tools, Learning Management Systems, and Adobe products (i.e. Acrobat, InDesign, Captivate). Military experience preferred. Ability to obtain and maintain a T1/ Public Trust background check. Physical Capabilities Lifting: Requires lifting materials up to 10 lbs. Ability to stand or sit at a computer for prolonged periods. Work Environment This position will take place primarily in an office setting. Travel may be required (up to 20%). Compensation The hourly pay range for this position is $32.45 - $48.00. Actual hourly pay will be determined based on experience, education, etc. Employment with HJF is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, which may include, but is not limited to, contacting your professional references, verification of previous employment, education and credentials, a criminal background check, and a department of motor vehicle (DMV) check if applicable. Any qualifications to be considered as equivalents, in lieu of stated minimums, require the prior approval of the Chief Human Resources Officer. jobs.title: Senior Merchant Mariner Evaluation Specialist (Deck)
jobs.description: This vacancy is for a GS - 2101 - 13, Senior Merchant Mariner Evaluation Specialist (Deck) located in the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Coast Guard, NMC MARINER EXAMINATIONS BRANCH in Location Negotiable After Selection Qualifications: Basic Requirements: This position has a positive Education Requirement in addition to at least one year of Specialized Experience or substitution of education for experience or combination (if applicable) in order to be found minimally qualified. Transcripts must be submitted with your application package. You MUST meet the following requirements: EDUCATION: Undergraduate and Graduate Education: Major study -- accounting, business administration, business or commercial law, commerce, economics, engineering, finance, industrial management, statistics, traffic management, transportation, motor mechanics, or other fields related to the position. or Experience Specialized Experience: Experience that demonstrated a knowledge of the transportation function(s) of the position to be filled. AND To qualify at the GS-13 grade level, your resume must demonstrate at least one (1) full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the federal sector. Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work. Examples of specialized experience include performing the following types of tasks on a regular basis. Performing deck officer duties on large, self-propelled vessels, including planning and executing safe navigation, supervising complex on-deck operations, managing vessel stability, and ensuring compliance with safety and security protocols Leading a technical program or team by setting priorities, directing and reviewing work, assigning duties to meet strategic goals, and providing training or mentorship on complex policies and procedures Serving as a technical expert responsible for preparing official written documents (e.g., policy recommendations, final reports) and authoritatively communicating complex information and final decisions to diverse audiences. NOTE: All experience statements (i.e., duties, specialized experience, or related applicable assessment) copied from this announcement and pasted into your resume will not be considered as a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. NOTE: Education can not be substituted for experience at this grade level. Selective Placement Factor(s) must be met in order to receive further consideration. You will be given the opportunity to address these when you apply on-line. U.S. Merchant Mariner Pathway: Hold (or have held) a valid U.S. Merchant Mariner Credential (MMC) in the grade of Chief Mate any gross tons or higher Military Pathway: Possess equivalent military experience as a DWO on vessels of 1600 GRT or higher Subject Matter Expert Pathway: Have been employed for two (2) or more years as a civilian Subject Matter Engineer Expert in the Mariner Training and Assessment Division at the National Maritime Center (NMC). National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

jobs.title: Clinical Lab Scientist
jobs.description: This position is eligible for the Education Debt Reduction Program (EDRP), a student loan payment reimbursement program. You must meet specific individual eligibility requirements in accordance with VHA policy and submit your EDRP application within four months of appointment. Program Approval, award amount (up to $200,000) and eligibility period (one to five years) are determined by the VHA Education Loan Repayment Services program office after complete review of the EDRP application. Qualifications: Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency: Candidates must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 7403 (f) Education: A bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university. Foreign Education. To be creditable, education completed outside the U.S. must be deemed at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. program by a private organization specializing in the interpretation of foreign educational credentials. Graduates of foreign baccalaureate degree programs meet the educational requirements if they meet either of the following: Foreign transcripts are evaluated by an acceptable evaluation agency, and the degree is found to be equivalent to a NAACLS-approved U.S. clinical laboratory science degree program. OR The applicant submits a letter from ASCP BOC or AMT stating the individual is eligible to take the certification examination. NOTE: Possession of a certification identified below automatically determines the foreign education as creditable and no further documentation or proof of equivalency is needed. Certification: Candidates must meet one of the certification options below. Generalist certification as an MLS given by ASCP BOC or AMT. Generalist certification as an MT given by ASCP BOR or AMT. Categorical certification or Specialist certification by ASCP or AMT. NOTE: Categorical and specialist certifications are not acceptable for CLS Generalist positions or lab sections unrelated to the categorical or specialist certification held. Categorical or specialist certifications are acceptable for higher-graded positions within the relevant lab section or one of the non-section specific assignments (including, Ancillary Testing Coordinator, Education Coordinator, Laboratory Information Manager, Quality Manager, Laboratory Manager, Regional Technical Specialist, National Quality and Compliance Agent, Regional Program Manager, Regional Director, Laboratory Director, or National Quality and Compliance Officer). May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). GS-11 Grade Determination: Experience: 1 year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade level. OR Education. Must have 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education or a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in medical technology or a directly related science. AND Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs: Knowledge of professional clinical laboratory science principles, practices, concepts, and theories that support sound, independent work. Knowledge of laboratory quality control and quality assurance procedures and principles of performance improvement. Skill in informatics, laboratory data flow, and laboratory processes. Ability to maintain, troubleshoot, and repair instrumentation. Ability to use independent technical judgment to analyze and interpret laboratory results. Ability to read, interpret, and apply complex written instructions. Ability to communicate, consult, and interact with other members of the health care team, external relations, customer service, and patient education. Preferred Experience: 2-5 years of experience as a CLS Generalist covering all sections in Lab including Blood bank, Chemistry/UA, Hem/Coag, Microbiology/Molecular, Quality Management, and other related duties as assigned. Understanding of regulatory compliance and Quality Management. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-11. Physical Requirements: See VA Directive and Handbook 5019, Employee Occupational Health Service for requirements.
